analysisSections.title: Phase 4 — Broker Reaction Simulation
analysisSections.text: 1. Dominant line items: #1: China impairment (~£16m non-underlying) + strategic review. Even as non-cash/non-underlying, the loss of a China growth foothold will headline all broker notes. FY27 estimates must be revised. #2: H1 revenue miss vs seasonal norm / 40/60 phasing. £49m vs £58m implied seasonal expectation will dominate risk-reward debate — partially resolved by pre-guidance. 2. Forecast revision direction and magnitude: FY1 (FY26) — Revenue: Hold / −0 to −3%. EPS (underlying): Hold / −0 to −2%. Adj. operating profit explicitly confirmed £24.4m. FY2 (FY27) — Revenue: −3% to −6% (China contribution removed). EPS: −2% to −5%. 3. Target price and recommendation implications: Consensus TP £21.98 is severely stale vs £12.65 market price. Expect significant TP cuts toward £14–18 range. Recommendations likely held at Buy/Add but with flagged caution. No upgrades to recommendation from this RNS. 4. "Conservative guidance" read-through: FY26 guidance references the specific £24.4m footnote — this is a quantified in-line hold, not a conservative "not less than" framing. No upgrade cycle language. 40/60 phasing pre-communicated since January update. Partially cushions H1 miss interpretation. 5. Key risk / offsetting factor: H2 delivery requires a 27.5% YoY revenue ramp. 70% cover from order book is supportive but execution risk is real given macro uncertainty and geopolitical commentary. China uncertainty clouds FY27 visibility. 6. Overall broker-note tone forecast: Cautious but constructive. Brokers maintain medium-term Buy thesis (structural demand, OEM-agnostic, regulatory tailwinds for active safety/AV) while flagging near-term H2 execution risk and China strategic overhang. TP cuts likely across the board. First notes probably titled "In line, but China and H2 the focus" — holding conviction with reduced near-term momentum.

analysisSections.title: Phase 5 — Score Rationale
analysisSections.text: Final Score: 43 / 100 Band: 30–49 — Likely Flat to Slight Cut Confidence range: 38–48 Mode: Pre-H1 Score components: +40 Base (FY guidance confirmed in-line, quantified at £24.4m) −9 China impairment + strategic review (FY27 revenue/EPS cuts required) −8 H1 rev −7.4pp seasonal miss (partially mitigated by pre-guided 40/60 phasing) −5 H2 burden +27.5% YoY revenue requirement (execution risk) +6 Order book £47m +11.9% YoY, 70% FY26 cover +3 Net cash £39.3m, robust balance sheet −2 EPS trend +8.3% but flat 4-week momentum; price/TP gap signals stale TPs −2 Macro/geopolitical risk language; no upgrade trigger language = 43 The score of 43 reflects a genuine "hold the line" RNS. FY26 underlying estimates are likely to be maintained, preventing a formal cut cycle. However, the China impairment forces FY27 revision, the H1 revenue miss (however pre-guided) elevates H2 scrutiny, and the large gap between stale consensus TPs and the market price creates a headwind for any re-rating catalyst. The key near-term event is the full H1 results on 14 April 2026 — that will be the scorecard that matters for FY26 delivery confirmation.

analysisSections.title: Phase 1 — Data Context
analysisSections.text: Consensus forecasts: FY1 EPS 21.6p, FY1 Revenue £137.9m. FY2 EPS 25.4p, FY2 Revenue £155.8m. Current price 188p vs consensus TP 308p (+63.8% upside). Weekly snapshot momentum: EPS net change over full period (May '25–Mar '26) = +15.5% (18.7p → 21.6p), driven almost entirely by a single step-up in early December 2025 (likely post-FY25 results beat: 17.4p → 21.6p, approximately +24% in one week). The 4-week trend is FLAT — EPS has been static at 21.6p for 13 consecutive weeks. Revenue forecasts have drifted lower over the period (£142.2m → £137.9m, −3.0%). 3-year avg H1 % of FY: Revenue = 50.7% (3yr avg, provided). EPS = 12.8% (2yr avg, provided — note only 2yr available for EPS, reflecting unusual H1 loss years in FY23/FY24). Implied H1 baselines (pre-H1 mode): H1 Rev baseline = 50.7% × £137.9m = £69.9m. H1 EPS baseline = 12.8% × 21.6p = 2.77p. Implied H2 FY26 (consensus-derived): H2 EPS = 21.6p − 2.77p = 18.83p (87.2% of full-year burden). H2 Rev = £137.9m − £69.9m = £68.0m. Seasonal baselines (pre-H1 mode): • 3yr avg H1 Rev % of FY = 50.7% → implied H1 baseline = £69.9m • 2yr avg H1 EPS % of FY = 12.8% → implied H1 baseline = 2.77p Buy trigger thresholds (+1.5pp): • Rev: H1 > 52.2% × £137.9m = £71.97m → 🟢 MILD BUY • Rev: H1 > 53.7% × £137.9m = £74.06m → 🟢 STRONG BUY • EPS: H1 > 14.3% × 21.6p = 3.09p → 🟢 MILD BUY • EPS: H1 > 15.8% × 21.6p = 3.41p → 🟢 STRONG BUY Sell trigger thresholds (−1.5pp): • Rev: H1 < 49.2% × £137.9m = £67.83m → 🔴 CAUTION • Rev: H1 < 47.7% × £137.9m = £65.77m → 🔴 SELL SIGNAL • EPS: H1 < 11.3% × 21.6p = 2.44p → 🔴 CAUTION • EPS: H1 < 9.8% × 21.6p = 2.12p → 🔴 SELL SIGNAL H2 Burden: H2 EPS burden = 87.2% of FY26 consensus EPS. FY1 forecast = FY27 (year ending Sep 26). ▸ TRAJECTORY & HoH ANALYSIS Revenue trajectory: Highly volatile. FY24 saw a large anomaly (H2 Rev collapsed from £91m to £39m — likely restructuring/refocusing period). Recovery in FY25 (+6.3%) and FY26 (+1.7%). FY27 consensus (+14.1%) assumes a meaningful acceleration — this is now at risk. EPS trajectory: Decelerating from extreme base-effect growth rates (FY24: +56%, FY25: +29%, FY26: +42%, FY27 cns: +18%). The deceleration is expected and healthy — but downward revisions to FY27 consensus would accelerate this pattern further. Implied H2 FY27 momentum: +28.2% YoY EPS (consensus-implied). Classified as STRONG. However, this assumption is now fundamentally challenged by guidance suspension and geopolitical headwinds. If H2 demand to Mediterranean/Turkey destinations remains depressed, the implied H2 growth collapses — bear case H2 EPS could be flat to prior year (14.7p), implying FY27 EPS of only ~17–18p vs 21.6p consensus. Forecast momentum divergence: Price has fallen from 317p (May 25) to 188p (Mar 26, −40.7%) while EPS was revised up +15.5%. This severe divergence signals the market has been pricing in geopolitical/structural risk well ahead of this RNS. The guidance suspension now validates what the market was already pricing. This may limit further downside in price but ensures broker EPS cuts follow.

analysisSections.title: Phase 4 — Broker Reaction Simulation
analysisSections.text:
1. Dominant line items: #1 Driver: Guidance suspension. The withdrawal of explicit £39m–£43m Adj. PBT guidance removes the anchor for broker models. Every house must now rebuild from scratch using geopolitical scenario analysis — a fundamentally higher-uncertainty exercise. This alone dominates the note tone. #2 Driver: Volume momentum vs destination exposure conflict. Bookings +10%, Q2 +34% are genuine and strong. But Turkey, Greece, Cyprus, Egypt are OTB's core beach corridors. Brokers must model demand elasticity and substitution (City/Cruise offsets) vs core destination demand destruction. 2. Forecast revision direction & magnitude: FY1 Revenue: Down 5–10%. Middle East conflict disrupts core Mediterranean summer demand. Estimate range: £124–131m. FY1 EPS: Down 10–20%. Consensus 21.6p → estimated 15–18p in near-term broker revisions. Bear case could see 13–15p if H2 summer demand recovery fails to materialise. FY2 Revenue: Hold / modest cut −3–5%. Market likely assumes conflict resolution or demand normalisation by FY28. FY2 EPS: Hold / modest cut −5%. 25.4p → ~24p range. Medium-term targets of 38.7p EPS remain the long-run anchor. 3. Target price & recommendation: Brokers will cut TPs materially. Consensus 308p likely moves to 220–260p range (−15 to −29%). Price is already at 188p — significant discount to even cut TPs. Most brokers likely maintain Buy/Add with a recovery narrative. No downgrades to Hold/Sell expected from house brokers (Cavendish, Peel Hunt likely). 4. Conservative guidance read-through: The opposite of a "not less than" comfort signal. Guidance suspension is unambiguously negative. The word "temporarily" is management's attempt to soften the signal but brokers will not treat this as a buying flag. The medium-term targets reiteration (38.7p, £85m PBT) shows confidence in the structural story but provides zero FY1 earnings visibility. 5. Key risk / offsetting factor: The single most important counter-argument is the asset-light balance sheet: OTB carries no committed inventory (unlike TUI, Jet2), meaning it can flex capacity without stranded costs. Cash generation continues through the conflict period. This limits the downside scenario significantly — it is not an existential risk, but it is a meaningful FY1 earnings risk.

6. Overall broker note tone forecast: ⚠ CAUTIOUS / DOWNGRADES PROBABLE — The first 1–3 broker notes (expected within 24–48 hours of the RNS) will cut FY1 EPS and revenue estimates materially, lower target prices, but likely maintain Buy recommendations citing the structural story, medium-term targets, and asset-light resilience. Tone will be: "near-term uncertainty elevated; long-term thesis intact; risk/reward improves at current levels but new information needed before upgrading." The H1 results on 12 May 2026 become the critical next catalyst.

analysisSections.text: Final Score: 29 / 100 Confidence range: 22–36 (wide — binary geopolitical resolution timeline) Verdict: GUIDANCE SUSPENDED · CUTS LIKELY Score components: Base (pre-H1 AGM, neutral start): +50 Guidance suspension (explicit negative, forces broker rebuild): −15 Geopolitical binary risk (unknown duration/magnitude, core destinations affected): −10 Forecast momentum (FLAT 13wks, price -40.7% vs EPS: market already pricing concern): −4 Volume momentum (bookings +10%, Q2 +34% — genuine positive): +6 Asset-light structural resilience (limits downside, cash positive): +2 New verticals / medium-term targets reiterated: +2 Later booking mix (more pronounced FY26, increases H2 burden): −2 FX adjustment: nil ───────────────────────────────────── Final: 29 The score of 29 reflects a clear near-term negative catalyst (guidance suspension into geopolitical uncertainty) which will force broker EPS cuts of 10–20% on FY1. It does not go lower because (a) the asset-light model genuinely limits downside vs peers, (b) volume momentum is real and strong, (c) medium-term targets provide recovery anchor, and (d) the market has already de-rated the stock substantially. The wide confidence range (22–36) reflects that geopolitical resolution could quickly move this to 40+ with unchanged numbers, or could push it lower if the conflict extends through summer. Watch: H1 results 12 May 2026. Key thresholds — H1 Rev >£71.97m (mild buy signal); H1 EPS >3.09p (mild buy signal). These will be the first hard data points to assess whether the geopolitical headwind has been absorbed or has materially impaired H1 performance.

scorecards.analysisHtml:
PHASE 0 — ROUTING & FX
PHASE 0A — Routing

Routing mode: pre-H1 (latest qtrly report = 'Q4'). Interpreting incoming RNS as H1 results accordingly. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

PHASE 0B — FX Revenue Check
  • US revenue: £6,709k = 45.8% of H1 revenue — exceeds 30% threshold, FX Rule 1 applies
  • GBP/USD H1 FY26 avg (Jul–Dec 2025): ~1.339
  • GBP/USD H1 FY25 avg (Jul–Dec 2024): ~1.291 (used as prior baseline — no formal Currency Movements table in RNS)
  • GBP was ~4.8c stronger in the current period vs prior year
  • Exposure band: 35–50% · Direction: GBP headwind · Penalty: [−10 pts]
  • Badge: FX Rule 1 applied (−10 pts) · 45.8% USD · GBP headwind
PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT
  • Routing: pre-H1 mode (latest qtrly report = 'Q4'). Interpreting incoming RNS as H1 Results. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.
  • FY1 consensus: EPS 8.5p · Revenue £40.3m
  • FY2 consensus: EPS 10.3p · Revenue £45.3m
  • Forecast momentum: Net EPS change: +7.6p to 8.5p = +11.8%. Single step-up 18 Oct 25. Last-4-week trend: STALLING (20 consecutive flat weeks). Revenue net change +8.0%.
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 44.2% of FY1 = £17.8m · EPS 25.7% of FY1 = 2.18p
  • Prior-year H1 actuals: Revenue £15.79m · EPS 2.61p (underlying diluted)
  • Implied H2 YoY (pre-RNS): Revenue: FY1 £40.3m − prior H1 £15.79m = £24.51m implied H2 vs prior H2 £20.12m = +21.8%. EPS: 8.5p − 2.61p = 5.89p implied H2 vs prior H2 4.6p = +28.0%
  • FX: 45.8% USD · GBP/USD H1 FY26 avg ~1.339 vs H1 FY25 avg ~1.291 · GBP headwind · Penalty [−10 pts] confirmed. No formal Currency Movements table — period average used as proxy.
PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

RNS Type: H1 Results (six months ended 31 December 2025, announced 16 March 2026)

  1. Revenue: H1 FY26 £14.65m vs H1 FY25 £15.79m = −7.3% YoY. vs seasonal baseline £17.8m = −17.7% miss. FY guidance "in line with expectations" — no numeric upgrade. Implied H2: £40.3m − £14.65m = £25.65m.

"Revenues of £14.65m (H1 2025: £15.79m)"

"the Board's outlook of a full year performance in line with its expectations"

  1. EPS / Earnings: Underlying diluted EPS −0.68p (H1 FY25: +2.61p). Basic statutory EPS −2.53p. vs baseline +2.18p = catastrophic miss. Implied H2 EPS burden: 8.5p − (−0.68p) = 9.18p.

"Underlying diluted EPS3 -0.68 pence (H1 2025: 2.61 pence)"

"Strong profit progression anticipated in H2 as recently secured contracts progress through deployment and revenue recognition commences."

  1. ACMRR / Forward work: ACMRR £32.80m, +15% YoY. TCV signed £11.9m, +23% YoY (record). £7m TCV in December alone including £6m Proximity Cloud — ~50% (~£3m) to be recognised in H2 FY26.

"Annualised Committed Monthly Recurring Revenue (ACMRR) up 15% to £32.80m (H1 2025: £28.50m)"

"Total Contract Value of new contracts signed in the period up 23% to £11.9m (H1 FY25: £9.7m)"

  1. Margin / profitability: Gross profit £4.50m (H1 FY25: £6.03m), −25%. Gross margin 30% vs 38%, −800bps. EBITDA £4.12m (H1 FY25: £5.74m), −28%; EBITDA margin 28% vs 36%. Underlying PBT loss £0.69m (H1 FY25: profit £1.89m). Three drivers: timing of upfront revenue (~6%), infrastructure investment ahead (~2%), revenue-share model (Kraken, no upfront).

"Margin movement reflects timing and capacity investment rather than structural changes in pricing or unit economics"

"Infrastructure commitments in H2 are expected to increase at a slower rate, supporting margin improvement."

  1. Capital / cash: No dividend. Net cash £3.29m (FY25: £6.90m). Gross cash £6.96m maintained. New: £1.5m bank loan + £2.0m asset financing. Strategic investment £0.8m in Liquid-Markets-Solutions. Capex £3.2m H1. Inventory up to £3.4m.

"Gross cash was largely maintained at £6.96m (30 June 25: £7.36m) with net cash of £3.29m following upfront investment to support contract wins"

  1. Qualitative tone: Seven exchanges on Exchange Cloud (four on revenue-share). Kraken now monthly-profitable March 2026 ahead of expectations. ASX live. BMV DR site H2. TMX and nuam H2 go-lives. Market Edge Intelligence launched; Tier 1 bank in contractual discussions. 30+ Tier 1 banks/investment managers on platform.

"We enter the second half with strong momentum and a customer base comprising some of the world's largest financial institutions, each with significant expansion opportunity."

"the live sites are transitioning into monthly profitability ahead of our anticipated timeline"

PHASE 3 — HISTORICAL BENCHMARKING
  1. Half-on-Half (HoH) Growth Pattern

H2 derivations: FY26 H2 Rev implied = £40.3m − £14.65m = £25.65m. H2 EPS implied = 8.5p − (−0.68p) = 9.18p.

EPS trajectory: Decelerating at H1 level. H1 broke to loss from +1.8p prior year. H2 implied at +99.6% YoY — mechanistically required by consensus but unprecedented.

  • H2 2y ago vs H2 3y ago: 2.8p vs 3.4p = −17.6%
  • H2 1y ago vs H2 2y ago: 4.6p vs 2.8p = +64.3%
  • H2 FY26 implied vs H2 1y ago: 9.18p vs 4.6p = +99.6%

Revenue trajectory: Volatile — strong historic H2 growth but H1 FY26 broke pattern severely.

  • H2 2y ago vs H2 3y ago: £12m vs £11m = +9.1%
  • H2 1y ago vs H2 2y ago: £16m vs £12m = +33.3%
  • H2 FY26 implied vs H2 1y ago: £25.65m vs £16m = +60.3%

HoH Table:

| Period | Rev £m | YoY % | EPS p | YoY % |

|||||---|

| H1 3y ago | 8.0 | — | 0.8 | — |

| H2 3y ago | 11.0 | — | 3.4 | — |

| H1 2y ago | 11.0 | +37.5% | 1.2 | +50.0% |

| H2 2y ago | 12.0 | +9.1% | 2.8 | −17.6% |

| H1 1y ago | 13.0 | +18.2% | 1.8 | +50.0% |

| H2 1y ago | 16.0 | +33.3% | 4.6 | +64.3% |

| H1 FY26 | 14.65 | −7.3% | −0.68 | −137.8% |

| H2 FY26* | 25.65 | +60.3% | 9.18 | +99.6% |

*Implied H2 — FY1 consensus minus H1 actual

  1. Seasonal H1% of FY Baseline, Tracking Deviation and Signal

Revenue:

  • Baseline: 44.2% × £40.3m = £17.81m
  • Actual: £14.65m ÷ £40.3m = 36.4% vs 44.2% → deviation [−7.8pp]
  • Signal: 🔴 SELL SIGNAL (≤ −3pp)
  • Buy trigger (£18.08m): ✗

EPS:

  • Baseline: 25.7% × 8.5p = 2.18p
  • Actual: −0.68p ÷ 8.5p = −8.0% vs 25.7% → deviation [−33.7pp]
  • Signal: 🔴 SELL SIGNAL (≤ −3pp, catastrophically below)
  • Buy trigger (2.21p): ✗

H2 EPS burden: 9.18p required vs 3yr avg H2 of 3.6p — burden MASSIVELY HIGHER than consensus assumes. Management guided "in line" implying brokers already modelled this extreme H2.

Historical hit rate: No prior year with H1 deviation of this magnitude in the 3yr dataset. Precedent absent.

Key note — deployment timing thesis: H1 FY26 contained only £0.57m upfront revenue vs £3.30m H1 FY25. Management states "the majority of these deployments have now been completed." If true, H2 catch-up is mechanistically secured.

  1. Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical
  • H2 3yr avg revenue: £13.0m (11 + 12 + 16 ÷ 3)
  • Implied H2 FY26: £25.65m vs £13.0m = +97.3% above 3yr avg
  • H2 3yr avg EPS: 3.6p (3.4 + 2.8 + 4.6 ÷ 3)
  • Implied H2 FY26: 9.18p vs 3.6p = +155% above 3yr avg
  • Classification: strong in direction — but binary execution risk. Not organic acceleration; a recovery trade.
  1. Forecast Momentum Overlay
  • EPS trend: 7.6p → 8.5p (+0.9p, +11.8%). Single upgrade event 18 Oct 25. No movement since.
  • 4-week trend: STALLING — 20 consecutive flat weeks
  • Revenue trend: £37.3m → £40.3m (+8.0%), single step
  • Divergence: Price −40.3% (335p → 200p) while EPS consensus +11.8%. Severe price/forecast divergence — market pricing in implicit downgrade risk not yet reflected in consensus.
  1. Structural / One-Off Flags
  • Revenue-share model transition [STRUCTURAL]: Exchange Cloud moving from upfront recognition to monthly revenue-share permanently. Depresses H1 during transition but improves revenue quality. "we expect it to deliver greater revenue in the medium term than the prior model"
  • Deployment lag [TIMING — RESOLVING]: "More pronounced than usual" in H1. "The majority of these deployments have now been completed" — key management assertion.
  • ACMRR vs P&L divergence [LEADING INDICATOR]: £32.8m ACMRR annualised (£16.4m/half) vs £14.65m reported H1. 12% gap = unrecognised contracted revenue due to convert.
  • H2 front-loading [YEAR-SPECIFIC ANOMALY]: £0.57m upfront H1 vs £3.30m prior H1. ~£3m from December Proximity Cloud wins due H2. Not a recurring pattern.
PHASE 4 — BROKER-REACTION SIMULATION
  1. #1 and #2 Drivers: #1 — ACMRR growth (+15% to £32.8m) vs P&L divergence. Brokers anchor here as the forward revenue indicator validating the H2 recovery thesis. #2 — H2 recovery credibility. The specificity of management's visibility (£3m Proximity Cloud, BMV DR, TMX, nuam go-lives) gives concrete items to model. Most retain estimates but reduce conviction.
  1. Forecast revisions: FY1 Revenue: hold, possibly −2 to −4% if H2 slip risk modelled. FY1 EPS: hold to −5 to −10% cut (H1 loss worse than most models; H2 burden unprecedented). FY2 Revenue: hold to +0–3% upgrade on ACMRR strength. FY2 EPS: hold to +0–5% upgrade if H2 FY26 delivers.
  1. Target price / recommendation: Likely hold TP with some cuts −10 to −15%. Current TP 335p vs 200p spot = 67.5% upside. Extreme upside-to-TP gap means brokers unlikely to upgrade; stock needs to demonstrate H2. Possible TP range 250–310p from cautious brokers. Recommendations shifting to "hold" or "speculative buy."
  1. Conservative guidance read-through: "In line with its expectations" is neutral maintenance language, not "comfortable" or "not less than." Does not increase upgrade cycle probability. Minimum bar to avoid downgrades only.
  1. Key risk: H2 execution failure — any deployment slip on BMV, TMX, nuam, or Proximity Cloud wins beyond 30 June 2026 makes £25.65m H2 revenue and 9.18p EPS unachievable, requiring material FY consensus cuts. "the timing of deal signature can be hard to predict"
  1. Overall tone: Cautious / downgrades or target cuts probable — H1 P&L misses significant; H2 burden unprecedented; share price already at −40% signalling market scepticism. Most brokers will formally maintain FY estimates but cut TPs and lower tone.
Phase 5 — Final Score & Verdict
32
/100
Confidence range: 26–40 · FX penalty −10 pts: 45.8% USD · GBP headwind (H1 FY26 avg ~1.339 vs H1 FY25 avg ~1.291)
ACMRR +15% YoY — strong leading indicator+12
TCV +23% / £11.9m record — commercial momentum+8
Management "in line" FY guidance maintained+5
H2 deployment visibility (£3m Proximity, BMV, TMX, nuam)+6
Kraken profitable ahead of schedule+4
H1 revenue −7.3% YoY, −17.7% vs seasonal baseline−8
H1 EPS −0.68p vs +2.18p baseline — −33.7pp deviation−10
Gross margin collapse 38% → 30%, EBITDA −28%−7
Unprecedented H2 EPS burden (9.18p vs 3.6p 3yr avg)−8
Net cash decline, new debt drawn, FX headwind−5
Forecast momentum stalled, 20 weeks no movement−3
USD FX headwind (Rule 1)−10
Price/consensus divergence (−40% vs +12% EPS)−2

This is a structurally complex H1 result where the headline numbers are emphatically negative on every reported P&L metric, yet the leading commercial indicators tell an entirely different story. The #1 metric — ACMRR of £32.8m, up +15% YoY — is the number brokers must hold onto, because the reported figures are almost entirely a function of deployment timing rather than demand. H1 revenue of £14.65m was −7.3% YoY and −17.7% below the seasonal baseline of £17.8m, the largest H1 tracking deviation in the company's history. Underlying diluted EPS of −0.68p versus the 2.18p seasonal baseline is a −33.7pp deviation, triggering a mechanical 🔴 SELL SIGNAL on both metrics. The single definitive catalyst is the deployment timing thesis: H1 FY26 contained just £0.57m of upfront revenue versus £3.30m in the same period last year, with the majority of the December £6m Proximity Cloud contract wins deliberately back-loaded into H2. This is not a demand problem — TCV of £11.9m was signed in H1 alone, up +23% YoY and above the prior record — but a cash-conversion timing problem of unusual severity.

The H2 EPS burden is the central risk in this investment case. Consensus FY1 EPS of 8.5p requires 9.18p from H2 alone — more than double the 3-year average H2 of 3.6p and +99.6% above the prior comparable period H2 of 4.6p. Management has provided specific, itemised H2 revenue drivers: approximately £3m from December Proximity Cloud wins already contracted and deploying; BMV disaster recovery site go-live; TMX and nuam Exchange Cloud go-lives; and the Kraken Exchange Cloud contract now moving into monthly profitability in March 2026, ahead of schedule. The ACMRR run-rate of £32.8m annualised (implying £16.4m per half in pure recurring revenue) provides the base. The £10.1m of accrued income on the balance sheet will also unwind as cash, further supporting reported revenue. The downside case is contained if — and only if — deployments execute on schedule; the structural risk is that any single meaningful slip creates a domino effect on H2 deliverability. The FX headwind (GBP ~4.8c stronger vs the prior-year H1 average) applies a further mechanical drag on the 45.8% USD revenue base.

Brokers are likely to hold FY1 consensus formally — management's "in line" guidance gives cover — but with sharply increased confidence intervals. FY1 EPS held at 8.5p by most, with a subset cutting −5 to −10% to ~7.7–8.1p if they model deployment slippage. FY2 EPS of 10.3p may see modest upgrades (+0 to +5%) as ACMRR trajectory supports the medium-term narrative. Consensus TP of 335p likely to see cuts to 250–310p range from a majority of brokers. The main constraint on the score is the binary nature of the investment case: if H2 FY26 delivers, the stock is materially undervalued at 200p; if it does not, FY consensus requires a double-digit cut. Upgrade cycle probability is low over the next 6–8 weeks — the catalyst is H2 trading evidence, likely via a pre-close update in May or June. Score of 32/100 reflects that this RNS comprehensively fails the mechanical H1 tracking tests and delivers broker uncertainty rather than broker confidence, even as the underlying commercial picture is the strongest in the company's history.

scorecards.analysisHtml:
Phase 0 — Routing & FX
  • Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as a pre-FY trading update for the year ending 31 March 2026. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.
  • FX Check: The RNS contains no Currency Movements section. DSW Capital is a UK-domiciled professional services network operating exclusively in the United Kingdom. No single non-GBP currency exceeds 30% of revenues. No FX penalty or adjustment applies. No Rule 1 triggered.
Phase 1 — Data Context
  • FY1 consensus (pre-RNS): EPS 6.9p; Revenue £7.5m. FY2 consensus: EPS 7.2p; Revenue £8.5m. No consensus target price available (Shore Capital sole broker).
  • Forecast momentum (12-month): EPS net change over full period +23.2% (5.6p → 6.9p), driven by a single large upgrade event in the week of 12 July 2025 (5.6p → 7.3p coinciding with DR Solicitors acquisition/results uplift), followed by two subsequent downward revisions (7.3p → 7.1p Nov 2025 → 6.9p Dec 2025). Last-4-week trend: FLAT. Net direction: one upgrade cluster followed by stalling and partial reversal — momentum reversing/stalling.
  • 3-year average H1 % of full-year (historical actuals only): Revenue H1 avg = 41.9% of FY; EPS H1 avg = 39.7% of FY.
  • Implied H2 derivation (pre-FY mode): RNS guides FY26 Total Income c.£6.2m. H1 Revenue actual (Sharescope) = £3m → Implied H2 Revenue = £3.2m vs prior-year H2 £4m → H2 YoY −20%. Guided Adj PBT = £1.3m / 25.1m shares → implied FY EPS ≈ 5.2p vs cns 6.9p = −24.6% miss. H2 implied EPS (guided basis) ≈ 3.6p vs prior-year H2 3.8p.
  • FX: No FX exposure relevant. Rule 1 not triggered. No adjustment.
Phase 2 — RNS Extraction & Quantification

RNS Type: Pre-FY Trading Update

  1. Total Income guided: c.£6.2m vs FY1 cns £7.5m = −17.3% miss.
    "the board now expects to report Total Income of c.£6.2m, Adjusted EBITDA of c.£1.6m and Adjusted profit before tax of c.£1.3m for FY26."
  2. Adjusted EBITDA guided: c.£1.6m vs FY1 cns £2.9m = −44.8% miss.
    "the board now expects to report Total Income of c.£6.2m, Adjusted EBITDA of c.£1.6m and Adjusted profit before tax of c.£1.3m for FY26."
  3. Adjusted PBT guided: c.£1.3m vs FY1 cns £2.4m = −45.8% miss.
    "the board now expects to report Total Income of c.£6.2m, Adjusted EBITDA of c.£1.6m and Adjusted profit before tax of c.£1.3m for FY26."
  4. Implied FY26 EPS ≈ 5.2p (Adj PBT £1.3m / 25.1m shares) vs cns 6.9p = −24.6%. Note: tax adjustments and SBP add-backs may vary; this is directional.
  5. Causal driver: geopolitical shock — Iran war → M&A collapse specifically in March (peak completion month).
    "the outbreak of war with Iran has severely impacted M&A activity in the UK, with many deals the Group expected to complete in March being aborted or postponed until the long-term economic ramifications of the war are established."
  6. March seasonality context explicitly named — March is the critical month for M&A completions ahead of UK tax year end.
    "March is traditionally an important month for M&A completions, ahead of the tax year end."
  7. DR Solicitors: c.11% revenue growth in FY26 to date — positive partial offset; diversification strategy delivering.
    "achieving Revenue growth of c.11% at DR Solicitors in FY26 to date"
  8. Cash £1.4m / Net Debt £0.5m at 28 Feb 2026 — after £1m OakNorth loan repayment and £0.8m dividend payments in FY26. Balance sheet solvent; dividend sustainability under scrutiny given EBITDA miss.
    "Our cash reserves remain strong with cash of £1.4m at 28 February 2026 and Net Debt of £0.5m. This is after £1m loan repayment of the £3.0m OakNorth Bank revolving credit facility, drawn down fully to part fund the acquisition of DR Solicitors, and £0.8m dividend payments across October 2025 and January 2026."
  9. No dividend change declared in this RNS. Prior DPS payments of £0.8m in FY26 already made. Sharescope forecasts DPS 3.30p (FY1) / 3.50p (FY2) — sustainability risk elevated given earnings miss magnitude.
  10. CEO qualitative tone — acknowledges shortfall explicitly; maintains strategic narrative; defers full trading update to May 2026 in line with usual timetable.
    "Whilst it is very disappointing that the robust performance of FY26 has stalled, the Board's strategic aim continues to focus on growing the business and building a resilient and diversified group of licensee businesses."
    "The Group remains profitable and cash generative, despite the current geo-political and economic uncertainties, with a strong pipeline of diversification opportunities in its sights and will announce a full trading update post year end, in May 2026, in line with its usual timetable."
  11. Implied H2 Revenue = £3.2m (£6.2m guided − £3m H1 actual) vs prior-year H2 £4m → H2 YoY −20.0%.
  12. Implied H2 EPS (guided basis) ≈ 3.6p (5.2p implied FY − 1.6p H1 actual) vs prior-year H2 3.8p → H2 YoY approx −5%. The real story: consensus had implied H2 EPS of 5.3p (76.8% of FY1 cns) — now reset to ~3.6p, a −32% cut to the implied H2 burden.
Phase 3 — Historical Benchmarking
  • Half-on-Half growth pattern — Revenue: FY3y total £3m → FY2y £2m (YoY −33%) → FY1y £5m (YoY +150%) → FY1 cns £7.5m (YoY +50% pre-RNS); guided £6.2m (YoY +24%). Classification: Volatile — no consistent trend; DR Solicitors acquisition creates structural step-change mid-series.
  • Half-on-Half growth pattern — EPS: FY3y 5.0p → FY2y 2.0p (−60%) → FY1y 5.0p (+150%) → FY1 cns 6.9p (+38% pre-RNS); guided ~5.2p (+4%). Classification: Volatile. Historical patterns offer limited predictive value given acquisition-driven step-changes.
  • H2 Momentum (pre-FY mode): Implied H2 Revenue £3.2m vs 3-year H2 average £2.0m (£1m + £1m + £4m)/3 — nominally above average but vs prior-year H2 of £4m (post-acquisition base) = −20% YoY → Weak. Implied H2 EPS ~3.6p vs prior-year H2 3.8p = −5% → Flat/Weak. The consensus H2 EPS burden of 5.3p (76.8% of FY) was structurally fragile; now reset to 3.6p.

1#1 Driver — Triple miss (Revenue / EBITDA / PBT): Revenue −17%, EBITDA −45%, PBT −46% vs consensus. 6Overall broker-note tone: Negative / material downgrades expected. Shore Capital's first post-RNS note will cut FY1 EPS by approximately 20–28%, FY2 EPS by 10–17%, and reset the TP lower. DSW Capital's pre-FY trading update for the year ending 31 March 2026 is an unambiguous profit warning. Guided Total Income of c.£6.2m is 17% below the pre-RNS consensus of £7.5m; Adjusted EBITDA of c.£1.6m is 45% below consensus of £2.9m; and Adjusted PBT of c.£1.3m is 46% below consensus of £2.4m. Implied FY EPS is approximately 5.2p versus consensus 6.9p — a 25% miss at the per-share level.

The structural driver is a geopolitical shock: the outbreak of war with Iran collapsed M&A activity in March, which is the single most important month for DSW's core DSW Capital network given UK tax-year-end deal completions. The company's H2 EPS had always carried a structurally extreme 76.8% of the FY consensus — leaving no buffer. DR Solicitors' 11% revenue growth and the group's £1.4m cash position provide a floor and a credible diversification narrative, but are insufficient to offset the magnitude of the March M&A collapse.

Brokers — Shore Capital as sole house — will cut FY1 EPS by an estimated 20–28% and FY2 EPS by 10–17%, reset the target price materially lower (estimated 60–75p from a likely prior 80–100p), and maintain a cautious Buy on recovery optionality. The next catalyst is the full post-year-end trading update in May 2026. Score 14/100: firmly in the profit warning band. Confidence range 10–18 — tighter than usual given hard point estimates with minimal "circa" wiggle room and a 15-day year-end horizon.

scorecards.analysisHtml:
Phase 0 — Routing & FX
  • Routing mode: pre-FY (Q2). RNS = FY Results year ended 31 December 2025. No FX rule triggered — Boku reports in USD, no single currency exceeds 30% of revenues.
Phase 1 — Data Context
  • FY1 cns: EPS 8.9p, Revenue $127.9m. FY2: EPS 10.8p, Rev $155.4m.
  • Momentum: EPS +7.2% (8.3p→8.9p). Revenue +7.0%. Last-4-week FLAT. Stock de-rated 246p→166p despite improving EPS — asymmetric re-rating opportunity.
  • Implied H2 (pre-RNS): Rev H2 cns $64.6m vs prior H2 $52.0m = +24.2% YoY. Actual H2 $65.5m = +1.4% beat vs implied H2 cns.
Phase 2 — RNS Extraction & Quantification

FY Results — Year ended 31 December 2025

  1. Revenue: $128.8m vs cns $127.9m = +0.7% beat. +30% YoY. +15% vs start-of-year cns $112m (explicitly flagged by management).
    "particularly against consensus expectations at the start of the year of c.$112m for revenue and c.$36m for adjusted EBITDA"
  2. Adj EBITDA: $41.3m vs cns ~$40.1m = +3.0% beat. +36% YoY. Margin 32.1% (+1.6pp). Underlying ex-FX reclassification = 34.0%.
    "Adjusted EBITDA increased by 36% to $41.3m… adjusted EBITDA margin of 32.1% (FY 2024: 30.5%)"
  3. Digital Wallets & A2A: +67% to $43.5m, 34% of revenues (FY24: 26%). C.$3m non-recurring launch-phase pricing from single DW connection in H1.
    "Digital Wallets & Account to Account revenues grew by 67%… This included c.$3m from launch-phase pricing related to a single Digital Wallet connection in H1 2025"
  4. Bundling: +71% to $14.9m. Non-DCB now 45% of revenues (FY24: 35%, FY23: 27%). Core diversification thesis on track.
    "Bundling revenues increased by 71% year-on-year, contributing 11% of total revenues"
  5. MAUs +31% to 114.4m; TPV +27% to $15.7bn. Q4 milestone: >100m transacting monthly.
    "Monthly Active Users in December 2025 +31% to 114.4m… Total Payment Volume +27% to $15.7bn"
  6. Own cash +28% to $102.9m. Debt-free. Buyback $12.3m FY25 + new 4m programme completed Feb 2026 ($11.9m).
    "Own cash grew by 28% to $102.9m… 4 million shares were repurchased in January-February 2026, at a total cost of $11.9m"
  7. FY26 new catalysts: Brazil PIX (authorised), India UPI (final approval), UK PISP (authorised) — all going live to merchants in 2026.
    "In Brazil, we secured Payment Institution authorisation… which we expect to make available to merchants in 2026"
  8. Medium-term guidance unchanged: >20% CAGR; >30% EBITDA margin; progressive accretion from FY26.
    "we expect organic revenue growth exceeding 20%… adjusted EBITDA margin exceeding 30% with progressive accretion from 2026"
Phase 3 — Historical Benchmarking
  • Revenue trajectory: FY24 $99.3m → FY25A $128.8m = +29.7%. Two consecutive years ~30% growth. Steady at ~30% pa — tracking ahead of >20% CAGR guidance.
  • Non-DCB diversification: 45% (FY23: 27%, FY24: 35%, FY25: 45%). Linear trajectory accelerating. Core re-rating thesis.
  • H2 FY25: Rev $65.5m (+25.9% vs H2 FY24 $52.0m). Beat implied cns H2 by +1.4%. EPS recovery sharp from near-zero historical base.
  • Structural risk — $3m non-recurring + take-rate dilution: H1 FY26 faces elevated comparator; Bundling growth dilutes blended take-rate (guided to trend down).

Phase 4 — Broker Reaction Simulation
1#1 — $112m→$128.8m narrative (+15% vs start-of-year cns): Management explicitly called this out. Investec and Peel Hunt will lead with this. Third consecutive year of ~30% growth tracking ahead of >20% CAGR guidance.
2#2 — EBITDA margin +1.6pp to 32.1%, opex +27% vs rev +30%: First clear evidence of operating leverage. "Progressive accretion from FY26" gives brokers licence to model meaningful margin expansion in FY26–27.
3FY2 revisions: Revenue +3–7% to $160–165m; EPS +5–10% to ~9.4–9.8p. $3m non-recurring H1 element creates FY26 comparator headwind — brokers will model explicitly.
4TP raise to 350–380p: Cns 327p vs current 166p = 97% implied upside. Extreme gap reflects sentiment de-rating. Strong results provide re-rating catalyst.
5Key risk — Amazon warrant dilution ($11.5m FV, 5.3m warrants) + $10.5m annual SBP + take-rate headwind from Bundling mix. Statutory EPS $0.04 remains very low.
6Overall tone: Strongly positive / upgrade cycle starting. Investec and Peel Hunt publish "BUY, TP raised" within 24–48 hours. EPS upgrades 5–10% FY2. Stock de-rating creates disproportionate re-rating potential.
Phase 5 — Final Score & Verdict
79
/100
Confidence range: 75–84 · No FX · Pre-FY mode
Revenue +30% YoY; +0.7% vs cns; +15% vs start-of-year cns+6

Baseline+50

Boku delivered its strongest FY results to date: revenue $128.8m (+30% YoY, +15% vs start-of-year consensus), adj EBITDA $41.3m (+36%) with margin expanding to 32.1% (+1.6pp) — first clear evidence of operating leverage as opex grew only 27% vs revenue +30%. Non-DCB revenues reached 45% of total (FY24: 35%, FY23: 27%), with Digital Wallets +67% and Bundling +71%. MAUs +31% and TPV +27% confirm the platform is scaling faster than revenue.

Medium-term guidance of >20% CAGR confirmed unchanged — but FY25's 30% delivery makes this effectively conservative, giving brokers licence to model above the floor. New regulatory licences in Brazil (PIX), India (UPI) and UK (PISP) provide incremental FY26 revenue streams. The stock's 44% de-rating from recent highs (327p → 166p) despite improving fundamentals creates asymmetric re-rating potential.

Brokers Investec and Peel Hunt are expected to publish strongly positive upgrade notes within 24–48 hours, raising FY2 EPS to ~9.4–9.8p (+5–10%), FY2 revenue to $160–165m (+3–7%), and TPs to 350–380p. Watch points: H1 FY26 clean underlying growth ex-$3m non-recurring item, first PIX/UPI merchant revenues, and Bundling Americas momentum.

Phase 0 — Routing & FX
  • Routing mode: pre-H1 (latest qtrly report = 'Q4'). Interpreting incoming RNS as H1 results (six months ended 31 January 2026). Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.
  • FX Check: Close Brothers is a UK specialist banking group. Revenue is overwhelmingly GBP-denominated (domestic UK lending). No single non-GBP currency approaches 30% of revenues. No FX Rule 1 penalty applies.
Phase 1 — Data Context
  • FY1 consensus (pre-RNS): EPS 43.6p, Revenue n/a (banking model, not tracked). FY2 consensus: EPS 61.1p.
  • Forecast momentum: EPS net change over full snapshot period = −39.6% (from 72.2p to 43.6p). A sustained cutting cycle throughout the period driven by escalating motor finance provisions. Last-4-week trend: FLAT — the cutting cycle has plateaued at 43.6p since late January. Momentum classification: bottomed / dormant.
  • 3-year average H1 % of FY (EPS): 41.9% (3yr avg). Revenue H1 avg: n/a (no revenue consensus data).
  • H1 actual EPS: Adjusted basic EPS from continuing operations = 27.1p. H1 tracking vs seasonal norm: 27.1p / 43.6p FY1 cns = 62.2% vs 3yr avg 41.9% → deviation = +20.3pp → 🟢 STRONG BUY SIGNAL.
  • Implied H2 from consensus: FY1 43.6p − H1 27.1p = 16.5p implied H2. This would require H2 adj EPS to fall −48.8% vs H2 FY25 (32.2p) — an implausibly severe collapse not supported by trading commentary. FY consensus is materially too low.
Phase 2 — RNS Extraction & Quantification
  1. Adjusted operating profit H1 FY26: £65.2m vs H1 FY25 £80.5m = −19.2% YoY. Driven by reduced income (lower loan book) partly offset by lower impairment charges.
    "Adjusted operating profit decreased 19% to £65.2 million (H1 2025: £80.5 million), driven by reduced operating income, partly offset by lower impairment losses."
  2. Adjusted basic EPS H1 FY26: 27.1p (H1 FY25: 33.8p). Vs FY1 consensus H1 implied (43.6p × 41.9% = 18.3p expected) → actual 27.1p = +48% beat vs seasonal baseline.
    "Adjusted basic earnings per share (continuing operations): 27.1p" (from key financials table).
  3. Statutory operating loss: −£65.5m (H1 FY25: −£102.2m). Improvement of £36.7m YoY. The £135m motor finance provision increase in H1 FY26 (vs £165m in H1 FY25) is the primary driver of the statutory loss.
    "Operating loss before tax: (65.5) [H1 2026]... primarily reflecting the additional £135.0 million motor finance provision taken in October 2025."
  4. Accelerated cost savings — primary structural upgrade signal: FY26 annualised savings raised from £20m to £25m; total savings target of £60m now expected by end-2027 (previously end-2028). FY26 adjusted opex guided at c.£450m.

scorecards.analysisHtml:
Phase 0 — Routing & FX
  • Routing mode: pre-H1 (Q4). RNS = H1 Results for six months ended 31 December 2025 (H1 FY26). Eagle Eye year-end is 30 June. No FX rule triggered — GBP-denominated revenues.
  • NRS distortion: Neptune Retail Solutions contract lost June 2025. Two revenue KPI sets presented (inc/exc NRS). Consensus (£45.0m FY1) is post-NRS. For H1 tracking, inclusive figure (£23.0m) is used as it matches the consensus baseline.
Phase 1 — Data Context
  • FY1 cns: EPS 2.6p, Revenue £45.0m (FY26, updated after Jan 2026 trading update upgrade). FY2: EPS 8.9p, Rev £51.9m (FY27).
  • Momentum: EPS −85% over period (17.3p → 2.6p) — dominated by Sep 2025 NRS cut, then partial recovery. Revenue −5.7% (47.7m → 45.0m). Last-4-week FALLING. Stock: 900p → 400p (Jun 2025) → 530p (Feb 2026 post Jan upgrade).
  • 3yr avg H1%: Revenue 48.2%. EPS: n/a (historically unreliable).
  • H1 tracking (Revenue): £23.0m / £45.0m = 51.1% vs 3yr avg 48.2% → +2.9pp → 🟢 MILD BUY SIGNAL. H2 burden reduced by ~£1.3m vs baseline expectation.
  • EPS tracking: UNTRACKABLE — historical H1 EPS flagged n/a; adj EPS basis not directly comparable to Sharescope series.
Phase 2 — RNS Extraction & Quantification

H1 Results — Six months ended 31 December 2025 (H1 FY26)

  1. H1 Revenue (inc NRS): £23.0m vs H1 FY25 £24.2m = −5%. Ex-NRS: £22.4m vs £19.3m = +16%. H1 tracking: £23.0m/£45.0m = 51.1% vs 3yr avg 48.2% = +2.9pp.
    "Group revenue, excluding the impact of the NRS contract, grew by approximately 16%, to £22.4m"
  2. ARR: £42.2m (+29% ex-NRS). New H1 ARR exceeded full FY25 new ARR.
    "Underlying ARR grew by 29% from £32.8m in H1 2025. This growth was driven by securing eight major multi-year contracts"
  3. Adj EBITDA: £4.3m (margin 18%) — ahead of Board's expectations. FY26 exit 20% run-rate target maintained.
    "Adjusted EBITDA of £4.3m represented an 18% margin, ahead of the Board's expectations"
  4. FY26 full-year outlook: in-line with recently increased market expectations. No further upgrade beyond Jan 2026 upgrade.
    "the Board confidence in delivering results for FY26 in line with recently increased market expectations"
  5. FY27 guidance: "return to double digit revenue and EBITDA growth in FY27." Exit FY26 with 20% EBITDA margin run rate.
    "The Board continues to expect to exit FY26 with a 20% EBITDA margin run rate, and is confident that the momentum being achieved across the business will support a return to double digit revenue and EBITDA growth in FY27"
  6. US momentum: 4 wins, £2.5m new ARR in H1 FY26 — key validation of strategic expansion.
    "The US contributed £2.5m in new ARR in H1 2026, thanks to four significant wins"
  7. OEM: First 2 contracts secured — blue-chip European retailers. Estimated ARR c.£2.0m. Revenue-generating from FY27.
    "First two customer contracts secured through OEM partnership… with expected ARR of c.£2.0m"
  8. Recurring revenue 85% (H1 FY25: 81%). NRR ex-NRS = 108% (H1 FY25: 104%). EagleAI +23% to £3.6m.
    "Recurring revenue now represents 85% of total Group revenue, up from 81% in the prior period"
  9. Net cash: £12.1m (+3% YoY) after £0.6m share buybacks. Cash generative.
    "The Group was cash generative in the Period and ended the Period with net cash of £12.1m"
Phase 3 — Historical Benchmarking
  • H1 Revenue tracking: £23.0m / £45.0m = 51.1% vs 3yr avg 48.2% = +2.9pp → 🟢 MILD BUY SIGNAL. H2 burden slightly reduced — implied H2 = £22.0m vs prior H2 £24.0m (NRS loss explains decline, not organic deterioration).
  • Revenue YoY: FY24 +35.6% → FY25 +0.1% (NRS distorted) → FY26E ~0% (NRS distorted). Ex-NRS H1 FY26 +16% showing underlying recovery. Classification: Recovering from NRS disruption.
  • Structural — OEM + US: These are the FY27 catalysts. First OEM contracts signed; US ARR £2.5m in H1 alone.
  • H2 EBITDA burden: H1 adj EBITDA £4.3m. For 20% exit run-rate, H2 must deliver ~£4–5m. H2 is traditionally stronger for EYE. The pattern is achievable but requires execution.

Phase 4 — Broker Reaction Simulation
1#1 — ARR +29% ex-NRS; H1 new ARR > full FY25: The leading SaaS metric. Canaccord and Shore will emphasise the ARR trajectory and the strength of the Win momentum as the key re-rating trigger.
2#2 — EBITDA margin 18% ahead of expectations; 20% exit target confirmed: Demonstrates cost restructuring is working. Provides confidence for the FY27 profitability recovery thesis.
3FY1 (FY26) EPS: Hold at 2.6p; Revenue hold at £45.0m. FY2 (FY27) EPS: raise from 8.9p towards 10–12p (+12–35%) and Revenue from £51.9m towards £54–57m. The upgrade cycle is entirely a FY27 story driven by OEM, US and NRS-free comparators.
4TP: Hold or modestly raise to 530–600p. Current 328p vs 530p cns TP = 38% discount. Wide valuation gap provides upside even without material FY26 EPS upgrades.
5Key risk — H2 FY26 EBITDA delivery: H2 must step up from H1 £4.3m to deliver ~£4–5m H2 EBITDA for the 20% exit run-rate. H2 implied revenue of £22.0m is lower than H1 — NRS loss continues to suppress headline. OEM revenue only from FY27, not FY26.
6Overall tone: Constructive / FY27 upgrade cycle starting. FY26 confirmed; FY27 is the upgrade story. Notes will emphasise ARR velocity, US traction, OEM first contracts. Low absolute EPS (2.6p) means FY26 upgrades are immaterial — institutional re-rating requires FY27 evidence.
Phase 5 — Final Score & Verdict
72
/100

FY26 in-line only; no further FY1 EPS surprise−3

EPS −85% over period; last 4 weeks FALLING; NRS distorts all YoY−4
OEM revenue from FY27 only; NRS headwind continues H2−2
Baseline+50

Eagle Eye delivered a strong H1 FY26, with H1 revenue tracking +2.9pp above the seasonal norm (£23.0m = 51.1% of FY1 consensus vs 3yr avg 48.2%), triggering a 🟢 Mild Buy Signal. The headline is ARR growth: underlying ARR +29% ex-NRS to £42.2m, with H1 new ARR exceeding the entirety of FY25 — a powerful leading indicator. Adj EBITDA of £4.3m at an 18% margin came in ahead of Board expectations, and the 20% FY26 exit run-rate remains on track. US momentum (4 wins, £2.5m ARR) and the OEM first contracts (c.£2.0m estimated ARR) provide clear FY27 growth catalysts.

FY26 full-year guidance is confirmed in-line with the recently upgraded consensus — this is a confirmation, not an upgrade. The FY1 EPS upgrade cycle is effectively complete at 2.6p. The score is driven by FY27 upgrade potential: brokers are expected to raise FY27 EPS from 8.9p towards 10–12p and revenue from £51.9m to £54–57m, based on the OEM ramp, NRS-free comparators, and the management guide of double-digit revenue and EBITDA growth in FY27.

The primary constraint on a higher score is that FY26 EPS (2.6p) is extremely low in absolute terms, making near-term institutional EPS upgrades immaterial. The re-rating is a FY27 story. Watch points: H2 EBITDA delivery (implied H2 = £22m revenue vs H1 £23m — NRS effect), first OEM revenue recognition timing, and US win pipeline conversion in H2.

Phase 1 — Data Context

Phase 2 — RNS Extraction & Quantification

RNS TYPE: H1 Results (six months ended 31 December 2025)

  1. Revenue H1: £42.3m (+9.1% YoY from £38.8m). vs FY1 cns implied H1 (52.0% × £80.3m = £41.8m): +1.2% beat.
    "Revenue for the period grew by 9% to £42.3m (H1 FY25: £38.8m)"
  2. Gross profit H1: £10.5m (+7.1% YoY from £9.8m). GP margin 24.9% vs 25.2% prior — marginal compression. Growth driven by mobile payments +6%, messaging +20%, managed services +1%. UK +6%, rest of Europe +24% (Ireland + Portugal).
    "Gross profit for the period increased to £10.5m (H1 FY25: £9.8m) growing 7.1% on the previous period."
  3. Adjusted EPS H1: 6.2p — flat YoY (H1 FY25: 6.2p). H1 tracking = 6.2p / 11.2p = 55.4% vs 2yr avg 53.9% = +1.5pp ahead of seasonal norm. Implied H2 EPS = 11.2p – 6.2p = 5.0p vs prior H2 5.1p = –2% YoY.
    "Adjusted EPS 6.2p (H1 FY25: 6.2p) +0.0%"
  4. Adjusted EBITDA: £8.3m (+6.4% from £7.8m). Adjusted PBT £8.0m (+2.6% from £7.8m). Margin compression from lower interest income, higher amortisation, and rising effective tax rate. Operating costs +16% to £2.27m.
    "adjusted earnings per share rose only marginally, reflecting lower interest income, higher amortisation associated with increased capitalised software investment over the past three years and a modest rise in the effective corporation tax rate."
  5. FY guidance: "in line with market expectations" — explicit confirmation. No upgrade language. Full year guidance reiterated.
    "The Board remains confident in the Group's strategy and its ability to deliver sustainable gross profit growth and long-term value for shareholders in line with market expectations."
  6. International expansion: Portugal live (second European market, launched Sept 2025, gaining traction). Third European market: pilot live with major broadcaster since end-February 2026.     "Gambling now represents less than 6% of Group gross profit and we therefore expect the impact to be manageable."

Phase 0 — Routing & FX
  • Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as pre-FY trading update (year end 31 March 2026). Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.
  • FX Check: Americas revenues from H1 results = £6.6m / £8.2m total = ~80.5% of revenues USD-denominated. Threshold of 30% far exceeded. Web search conducted: GBP/USD spot ~1.3245 (17 March 2026). Prior year average rate (FY25, year ended 31 March 2025) estimated at ~1.275 based on known GBP/USD history — the RNS contains no Currency Movements section, so missing baseline fallback applies.
  • FX Rule 1 applied: GBP spot 1.3245 vs estimated FY25 avg ~1.275 = +4.9 cents stronger GBP (headwind for USD earners). Exposure >50% + adverse move >3 cents = −11 pts penalty. No prior average rate from RNS → confidence range widened ±5pp. FX badge: FX Rule 1 applied (−11 pts) · ~80% USD · GBP headwind.
Phase 1 — Data Context
  • FY1 consensus (pre-RNS): EPS 5.9p, Revenue £18.7m. FY2 consensus: EPS 5.8p, Revenue £21.0m.
  • Forecast momentum: EPS net change = +9.3% over period (5.4p → 5.9p). A single upgrade step in late November 2025 post-H1 results. Revenue held flat at £18.7m since. Last-4-week trend: FLAT. The pre-RNS consensus had NOT priced in any warning.
  • 3-year average H1 % of FY: Revenue H1 avg = 44.5%. EPS H1 avg = n/a (highly variable pattern).
  • H1 actual (from H1 results Nov 2025): H1 Revenue = £8.2m; H1 EPS = 2.1p (basic). H1 tracking: Revenue 8.2/18.7 = 43.9% vs 44.5% avg = −0.6pp (IN LINE). EPS: UNTRACKABLE (n/a avg).
  • Implied H2 required pre-warning: £18.7m − £8.2m = £10.5m H2 revenue needed from consensus. RNS now guides FY ~£17.0–17.1m, making H2 actual ~£8.9m = −15.2% below the H2 consensus implied figure.
  • FX summary: ~80% USD exposure. GBP/USD spot ~1.3245 vs estimated prior avg ~1.275 = headwind. FX Rule 1 penalty −11 pts confirmed.
Phase 2 — RNS Extraction & Quantification
  1. RNS type: Pre-FY Trading Update (year end trading update, FY26, year ending 31 March 2026).
  2. Revenue miss — primary warning: FY26 revenue anticipated approximately 8–9% below current market expectations of £18.7m. Implied actual: ~£17.0–17.1m. Miss vs consensus: −£1.6–1.7m.
    "full-year revenue is anticipated to be approximately 8-9% below current market expectations."
  3. EBITDA miss: Adjusted EBITDA expected approximately 15–18% below market expectations of £4.6m. Implied actual: ~£3.8–3.9m. The operating leverage amplifies the revenue miss given the high fixed cost base.
    "The revenue shortfall flows through to adjusted EBITDA, which is expected to be approximately 15-18% below current market expectations."
  4. Cash beat — sole positive: Year-end cash expected approximately 3–5% ahead of consensus £19.0m. Implied actual: ~£19.6–20.0m. Debt-free balance sheet maintained.
    "cash balances at year-end expected approximately 3-5% ahead of current market expectations... The Group maintains a debt-free balance sheet."
  5. Cause of miss — procurement delays, not structural: US procurement delays and customer purchasing deferrals due to geopolitical uncertainty (Middle East conflict).
    "This reflects procurement delays, particularly in the United States, and customer purchasing deferrals attributable to heightened geopolitical uncertainty, including the ongoing Middle East conflict."
  6. "Delays not losses" framing:
    "Critically, these opportunities are delayed, not lost. Active customer engagements continue across the pipeline, and order intake momentum improved in H2 FY26."
  7. ARR growth confirmed: Continued Annual Recurring Revenue growth in FY26 from support & maintenance and subscription licence income.
    "Intercede expects to deliver continued Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) growth in FY26, driven by increased support and maintenance revenues and further adoption of subscription-based licence income."
  8. FY27 £21m revenue target reaffirmed: Management confidence that FY26 delays are timing, not structural.
    "Intercede reaffirms its FY27 revenue target of £21 million, reflecting management's confidence that the FY26 revenue delays represent timing shifts rather than fundamental demand weakness."
  9. H2 FY26 order momentum improved:
    "order intake momentum improved in H2 FY26, validating underlying demand for the Group's solutions and products."
  10. EPS impact implied: With adj EBITDA ~£3.8–3.9m (15–18% below £4.6m cns), and applying a similar tax/share count structure as H1, adj EPS for FY26 ≈ 4.8–5.0p vs consensus 5.9p = approximately −15–19% miss.
  11. Full detail on 9 April 2026: More complete trading update with unaudited revenue, constant currency analysis, and actual cash due 9 April 2026.
    "The Group aims to report a more complete trading update... for the twelve months ended 31 March 2026 on 9 April 2026."
Phase 3 — Historical Benchmarking
  • HoH revenue pattern: Volatile/declining. FY24: £20.0m. FY25: £17.7m (−11.5%). FY26 guided: ~£17.0–17.1m (−3.7–4.0%). H2 FY26 actual implied ~£8.9m vs H2 FY25 £9.2m = −3.3% YoY. Revenue has been declining for three consecutive years, though the rate of decline is slowing. ARR growth (recurring revenues) is a positive offset.
  • HoH EPS pattern: Highly distorted by perpetual licence timing. No reliable EPS trend applicable. FY26 implied adj EPS ~4.8–5.0p vs FY25 ~6.9p = approximately −28 to −30% YoY — a significant annual earnings decline.
  • H1 tracking (pre-FY mode): H1 Rev 43.9% vs avg 44.5% = −0.6pp (IN LINE — within ±1.5pp). EPS: UNTRACKABLE. The H1 results were broadly in line — the miss is a H2 event driven by procurement delays that occurred after the November 2025 H1 report.
  • Implied H2 momentum: H2 FY26 actual ~£8.9m vs H2 FY25 £9.2m = −3.3% YoY. Weak. However, the context matters — H2 FY25 itself benefited from a large perpetual licence deal. On a normalised basis, H2 performance reflects the genuine procurement deferral issue described in the RNS.
  • Forecast momentum: EPS was upgraded +9.3% post-H1 (5.4p → 5.9p). This upgrade is now entirely reversed by today's warning. Net full-cycle impact will be negative relative to the starting 5.4p (actual landing ~4.8–5.0p = −8 to −11% vs pre-upgrade start).
  • Structural flags: The subscription model transition (perpetual → recurring) is strategically correct but creates a revenue valley. ARR is growing (support & maintenance £5.4m H1 FY26 vs £4.9m H1 FY25 = +10.2%) while professional services is declining (£1.4m vs £2.7m = −48%). The revenue mix shift is structural and intentional. Cash position (~£19.6–20m) provides M&A optionality. Middle East geopolitical tensions (oil >$100 per search results) are likely to persist, maintaining near-term procurement headwinds for US federal/defence customers.

2#2 Driver — EBITDA miss 15–18% below consensus: Operating leverage at Intercede is significant — staff costs represent ~74% of operating expenses. A modest revenue miss translates to a disproportionate EBITDA impact. Adj EBITDA guided ~£3.8–3.9m vs £4.6m consensus = a substantial earnings shortfall.

FY2: Cavendish will likely maintain the FY27 £21m target as a management aspiration but shade their own model to £19–20m, with FY2 EPS moving from 5.8p to perhaps 5.5–6.0p pending the 9 April fuller update. Target price likely cut from 225p to 150–185p.
4Conservative guidance read-through: Management's "delays not losses" framing and the explicit FY27 £21m reaffirmation are designed to put a floor under sentiment. The cash beat (£19.6–20m vs £19m cns) is a genuine positive that will be highlighted. ARR growth confirmation reassures on business quality. However, US procurement delays are a recurring risk factor for this sector and brokers will assign uncertainty premium to the FY27 target conversion.
5Primary risk: Deferred orders do not convert in FY27 at the rate management anticipates. Middle East geopolitical tensions have worsened (web search confirms oil >$100, conflict "several more weeks"), maintaining near-term procurement headwinds. The subscription model transition while strategically correct creates a multi-year revenue valley before ARR builds sufficiently to compensate for declining perpetual licence and professional services revenue.
6Overall broker-note tone: Cautious / downgrades to estimates probable. This is a meaningful profit warning. Cavendish will issue a note reducing FY26 estimates by ~15–19% while maintaining Buy rating and FY27 target anchoring. Share price at 97p is likely to fall 15–25p on publication. The cash strength (~£19.6–20m, nearly equal to the market cap at ~£58m) provides some floor — the company is trading close to cash value with the software business on minimal premium. Fuller detail available 9 April 2026. Cautious / Cuts Probable
Phase 5 — Final Score & Verdict
17

Confidence range: 12–22 (widened ±5pp: no prior FX average rate available) · FX Rule 1 applied (−11 pts) · ~80% USD · GBP headwind
Revenue 8–9% below consensus (profit warning)−22
EBITDA 15–18% below consensus−15

EPS implied cut −15–19%−8
Cash beat 3–5% ahead of consensus+4
ARR growth confirmed (recurring revenue quality)+5
FY27 £21m target reaffirmed+4
H2 order momentum improved+3

Subscription transition (structural positive)+3
Base50

FY26 revenue is guided approximately 8–9% below the £18.7m market consensus (~£17.0–17.1m actual) with adjusted EBITDA approximately 15–18% below the £4.6m consensus (~£3.8–3.9m), driven by US procurement delays and customer purchasing deferrals linked to Middle East geopolitical tensions. Implied adjusted EPS is approximately 4.8–5.0p vs consensus 5.9p — a miss of 15–19%. FX Rule 1 applies: with ~80% of revenues USD-denominated and GBP spot at 1.3245 materially stronger than the estimated FY25 average rate of ~1.275, an additional −11 point headwind is confirmed.

The sole significant positive is cash: year-end balances expected 3–5% ahead of the £19.0m consensus, maintaining the debt-free balance sheet and providing M&A optionality. ARR growth continues in the recurring support & maintenance and subscription licence lines, validating the strategic transition to a more predictable revenue model. Management has reaffirmed the FY27 £21m target and framed the FY26 shortfall explicitly as timing-related rather than structural demand erosion.

Cavendish, as sole nominated adviser and broker, will issue a note resetting FY26 estimates sharply lower while maintaining the Buy rating anchored to FY27 potential. The 9 April fuller trading update is the next information catalyst. At 97p, the share price already implies the business trades close to its ~£19.6–20m cash value on the market cap of ~£58m — the software business is valued on a minimal premium. However, until geopolitical conditions stabilise and deferred US government orders begin to convert, near-term EPS trajectory is negative and broker estimates will be cut.

FY26 current trading is positive with Q1 applications +13% YoY and MAB's fixed-rate maturity book running 19% higher than the market's 3–6% forecast. Adviser count +10%, productivity +13%, and net debt reduced to £3.3m all point to a well-functioning organic growth engine.

The key constraint is margin compression with an explicit FY26 cost headwind. Adj PBT margin fell to 11.4% (−0.6pp, 360bps below 15%+ target) with admin costs growing faster than revenue. Management explicitly warned the admin cost ratio will increase further in FY26 as H2 2025 acquisitions annualise. This limits FY2 EPS upgrade magnitude to 2–5% rather than 10%+. Consensus had already partially re-rated (EPS +2.5%, TP raised Feb 2026).

The Main Market listing in Q2 2026 (FTSE All-Share eligibility) adds an incremental re-rating catalyst not yet fully priced in. At 540p versus consensus TP of £11.33–13.00, even modest upgrades could have disproportionate price impact. Watch points: FY26 admin cost ratio trajectory, acquisition synergy realisation pace, and Q1 conversion to completions without H2 pull-forward effect.

  • Missing baseline fallback applied: No formal Currency Movements table with prior-year average rates present in the RNS. However, the RNS discloses the net FX impact explicitly: currency headwinds reduced both Group revenue and adjusted operating profit in the year by 0.6%. Prior year impact was −1.8% / −1.6% — improving trend.
  • Direction: GBP modestly stronger vs prior year average (confirmed by headwind disclosure). Headwind is mild — only 0.6% revenue impact, at the low end of the 35–50% exposure band.
  • Penalty applied: −5 pts (35–50% exposure band, neutral-to-mild headwind, lower-end of −10/−5 range given actual disclosed impact of only 0.6%). Confidence range widened ±5pp per missing baseline fallback rule.
  • Badge: FX Rule 1 applied (−5 pts) · ~38% EUR · GBP headwind (mild)
Phase 1 — Data Context
  • Routing mode: pre-H1 (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). RNS is FY 2025 full year results. Sharescope reflects pre-RNS state: FY1 consensus EPS 21.6p, FY1 revenue £1,305.5m; FY2 consensus EPS 23.9p, FY2 revenue £1,354.0m.
  • Consensus momentum: EPS net change over full 10-month snapshot period = 0.0%. Zero upgrades, zero downgrades — consensus completely static at 21.6p throughout. Revenue equally static at ~£1,305m. 4-week trend: FLAT. Remarkable stasis; brokers had no conviction to move either direction.
  • Seasonal H1 baselines: 3-year average H1 revenue split = 47.9% of full year. 2-year average H1 EPS split = 44.1% of full year (3y unusable: FY23 shows H2 as −15.0p placeholder). These baselines apply to FY26 forecasting; H1 FY26 not yet reported.
  • Implied H2 FY25 context (from actuals): H2 revenue = £1,270.8m − £620.3m (Sharescope H1) = £650.5m; H2 EPS = 22.37p − 6.7p = 15.67p. H2 revenue YoY = −2.7% vs prior H2 £668.5m. H2 EPS YoY = +8.1% vs prior H2 14.5p.
  • FX summary: EUR exposure ~38%, GBP mild headwind, −0.6% revenue impact disclosed. No prior-year average rate in RNS (missing baseline fallback). −5 pts penalty applied and carried to Phase 5.
Phase 2 — RNS Extraction & Quantification

RNS Type: FY Results — Year ended 31 December 2025

  1. Revenue — FY actual £1,270.8m (continuing), −1.5% vs prior year (−0.8% constant currency). vs FY1 consensus £1,305.5m = miss of −2.7%. H1 actual £620.3m; implied H2 £650.5m = −2.7% YoY vs H2 FY24 £668.5m. H1 FY25 was −2.4% YoY; H2 FY25 was +0.8% YoY — return to H2 growth confirmed.
    "Group revenue of £1.27bn was marginally below 2024 (by 1.5%), with gross margins flat at 17.7%."
    "Group revenue declined by 2.4% in the first half of the year compared with growth of 0.8% in the second half."
  2. Adjusted EPS — FY actual 22.37p vs FY1 consensus 21.6p = beat of +3.5%. YoY decline −17.0% (FY24: 26.96p). H1 FY25 actual 6.7p; H2 FY25 actual 15.67p = +8.1% YoY vs H2 FY24 14.5p. Adjusted profit before tax £30.5m (2024: £39.1m, −22.1%).
    "Adjusted EPS decreased by 17% (2024: 30%) to 22.37p (2024: 26.96p)."
  3. H2 profit weighting — 60% of adjusted operating profit generated in H2 (vs 54% in FY24). Implies H2 adjusted operating profit ≈ £26.2m, H1 ≈ £17.4m. This H2 skew is increasing structurally and is a key read-through for FY26 H1 expectations.
    "Adjusted operating profit of £43.6m (2024: £48.9m), with 60% (2024: 54%) generated in the second half."
  4. Gross margin — record 17.7% maintained on continuing basis (2024: 17.7%). UK&I improved to 18.6% (2024: 18.0%); EMEA 17.1% (2024: 17.0%); APAC 16.6% (2024: 16.4%); North America 17.5% (2024: 19.3% — vendor loss drag). No margin deterioration at group level despite revenue pressure.
    "Gross profit margins excluding exited businesses remain at record levels of 17.7% (2024: 17.7%)."
  5. Adjusted operating profit £43.6m (2024: £48.9m) = −10.7%; margin 3.4% (2024: 3.8%). Adjusted net finance costs increased to £13.1m (2024: £9.8m) due to full-year impact of prior M&A debt. UK&I operating profit +30% to £25.7m; EMEA −21% to £19.9m; North America −46% to £5.1m.
    "Adjusted operating profit fell by £5.3m to £43.6m, with adjusted profit before tax being £8.6m lower at £30.5m."
  6. Cash conversion exceptional — 123% (2024: 97%); well above long-term average of ~80%. Adjusted net debt reduced to £126.0m (2024: £130.6m). Leverage 2.17x adjusted EBITDA, improved from H1 2025 peak of 2.5x; within 3.0x covenant. Total facilities >£300m; RCF matures mid-2028.
    "Adjusted cash flow conversion of 123% (2024: 97%), reflecting the continued focus on driving near term working capital management efficiencies."
    "Adjusted net debt to adjusted EBITDA ratio at the period end was 2.17x, in line with Board and market expectations. This also reflects a positive reduction since H1 2025 (H1 2025: 2.5x)."
  7. Dividend reset — total 5.25p (2024: 13.0p) = −60% YoY. New policy: ~25% payout ratio of adjusted EPS. Final 3.5p proposed (2024: 7.5p), interim 1.75p paid (2024: 5.5p). Covered 4x by adjusted earnings. DPS progressive medium-term commitment maintained.
    "Proposed final dividend of 3.5p (2024: 7.5p) plus interim dividend of 1.75p (2024: 5.5p) equates to total dividends for 2025 of 5.25p (2024: 13.0p), reflecting the Group's updated dividend policy."
  8. Exceptional items — £38.3m total. Dominated by £27.0m ERP impairment (ERP rollout paused; only one country live). Restructuring costs £8.7m (headcount fell 1,900 to ~1,750). Loss on derecognition of acquired intangibles £4.4m. Insurance recovery £1.8m (Dubai warehouse fire Dec 2024). Statutory loss before tax £30.5m (2024: £22.3m profit). All exceptional — not in adjusted figures.
    "Following a comprehensive review of the ongoing deployment and future cost and benefits, the Board concluded that the ERP programme rollout should be paused, with only one country fully live. This resulted in a one-off impairment charge of £27.0m in the year."
  9. Outlook — no improvement assumed in 2026 market conditions; return to profit growth expected. New digital/AI strategy replacing ERP to deliver benefits faster and cheaper. M&A paused in 2025 but pipeline healthy; expected to resume in 2026. Germany expected to improve from 2026. New CFO Adam Councell joined 2 March 2026.
    "Whilst there have been no material improvements in the macroeconomic backdrop or the Pro AV market at the start of 2026, the Board expects that the actions taken by the Group will support a return to profit growth in 2026."
  10. Regional highlights — UK&I the standout; EMEA and North America remain drags. UK&I: revenue +6.7% to £508.3m, operating profit +30% to £25.7m. EMEA: revenue −5.3% to £517.5m (Germany entirely responsible; rest of EMEA +9.7%). North America: revenue −8.9% to £201.0m (Canada vendor loss + US tariff disruption). APAC: revenue −4.2% to £44.0m (+1.4% constant currency); being restructured into UK&I and EMEA regions from 2026.
    "Strong revenue and profit growth in UK&I due to market share gains and new vendors, despite challenging market conditions continuing."
    "A robust performance in EMEA, with revenue growth in the region excluding Germany, which is expected to improve from 2026."
Phase 3 — Historical Benchmarking
  • Half-on-Half revenue trajectory: Decelerating. FY23 YoY ~+8%; FY24 YoY ~+6.8%; FY25 YoY −1.5%. H1 FY25 £620.3m = +1.6% YoY (slowing from H1 FY24 +7.3%). H2 FY25 £650.5m = −2.7% YoY vs H2 FY24 £668.5m — though improved vs H1 trend (+0.8% actual H2 YoY per RNS, reflecting mix of continuing vs exited base).
  • Half-on-Half EPS trajectory: Recovering in H2. H1 FY25 EPS 6.7p = −38.5% YoY vs H1 FY24 10.9p. H2 FY25 EPS 15.67p = +8.1% YoY vs H2 FY24 14.5p. Full year −17.0%. The H2 recovery is the bull case underpinning FY26 expectations.
  • Seasonal baselines for H1 FY26 (pre-H1 mode — next event): Revenue H1 baseline = 47.9% × FY2 consensus £1,354.0m = £648.5m. EPS H1 baseline = 44.1% × FY2 consensus 23.9p = 10.5p. Buy trigger: H1 Rev > £657.5m (+1.5pp); H1 EPS > 10.7p (+1.5pp). Sell trigger: H1 Rev < £638.6m; H1 EPS < 10.3p. Note: FY2 baselines will shift post broker revisions; update triggers once consensus resets.
  • H1 FY26 UNTRACKABLE — both REV and EPS (H1 FY26 results not yet reported; no H1 data in current RNS which is FY results). H1 indicator on card: na for both metrics.
  • H2 momentum vs 3-year average: H2 FY25 revenue £650.5m vs 3yr avg H2 £651.5m = −0.2% (flat classification). H2 FY25 EPS 15.67p vs 3yr avg H2 EPS 16.66p = −6.0% (weak classification). However YoY H2 EPS was +8.1% — the 3yr average is depressed by the prior two weak years. The directional trend is improving.
  • Forecast momentum overlay: EPS flat at 21.6p for entire 10-month period. Revenue flat at ~£1,305m. Zero broker activity. 4-week trend FLAT. Price also unchanged at 329p throughout — extraordinary stasis. Actual EPS of 22.37p is a +3.5% beat into completely static consensus; this should prompt first broker revisions in months.
  • Structural flags: (1) ERP write-off £27.0m removes ongoing capex drag — future FCF improves. (2) H2 profit weighting increasing (60% in FY25 vs 54% FY24) — H1 FY26 will likely disappoint seasonally; manage expectations. (3) Dividend reset to 25% payout — balance sheet prioritised; removes progressive dividend expectation near term. (4) CFO change March 2026 — Adam Councell new; Stephen Lamb departed. (5) APAC folded into UK&I/EMEA from 2026 — operational simplification.

Phase 4 — Broker Reaction Simulation
1 #1 Driver — Revenue miss vs consensus (−2.7%): At £1,270.8m vs £1,305.5m, this is the headline number brokers must address first. Despite being only −0.8% at constant currency, the reported shortfall against a static consensus will dominate initial coverage. #2 Driver — EPS beat (+3.5%, 22.37p vs 21.6p): The mitigant. Better-than-expected profit conversion driven by H2 profit weighting (60%), margin discipline and cost reduction — the first meaningful data point in 10 months of total consensus stasis.
2 Forecast revision direction: FY26 (new FY1) EPS: +3–6% upward from current FY2 base of 23.9p, driven by higher FY25 base, ERP capex removal and cost restructuring benefits. FY26 revenue: −1–3% downward from £1,354.0m given cautious "no improvement assumed" outlook, Germany still weak, North America restructuring. Net result: modest EPS upgrade cycle accompanied by revenue estimate reduction.
3 Target price and recommendation: Consensus TP 329p vs current price 160p = 106% implied upside — stock screens extremely cheap at ~7x FY26 EPS. Most brokers will reiterate Buy/Overweight with TPs held in 300–350p range; no cuts warranted given EPS beat and recovery narrative. No recommendation upgrades either — the stock has been at a deep discount to TP for months with no catalyst. Re-rating awaits H1 FY26 evidence of recovery.
4 Conservative guidance read-through: The outlook — "working assumption that there will be little improvement in 2026" — is deliberately cautious framing paired with "greater confidence in our performance in 2026 and beyond." Classic AIM sandbagging: set low bar, beat it. Restructuring complete, ERP overhang cleared, UK&I firing, H2 conversion improving — probability of FY26 EPS consensus beating if Germany shows any recovery is meaningful. This language increases upgrade cycle probability in H2 FY26.
5 Key risk brokers will highlight: Leverage trajectory — adjusted net debt/EBITDA 2.17x (improved from 2.5x at H1 but above FY24's 2.0x). Finance costs increased to £13.1m (2024: £9.8m) from prior M&A debt. Dividend reset signals balance sheet strain. North America vendor loss and Canada restructuring not fully resolved. M&A paused — removes a key historical growth driver. CFO transition adds execution risk. North America gross margin structurally lower at 17.5% (2024: 19.3%) until new vendor secured.
6 Overall broker-note tone forecast: Constructive / modest upgrades likely. EPS beat will prompt first broker estimate revisions in months. Revenue miss and cautious macro cap enthusiasm. H2 recovery narrative (60% H2 profit weighting, UK&I +30% operating profit) is credible. Most houses reiterate Buy with unchanged or slightly higher TPs. Stock at 160p vs 329p TP — the valuation case is compelling but the re-rating catalyst awaits H1 FY26 results and evidence of German market recovery.

Phase 5 — Final Score & Verdict

Midwich's FY25 results present a genuinely split picture. The revenue miss of −2.7% vs a completely static consensus is the headline negative — £1,270.8m vs £1,305.5m — and brokers who had sat on their hands for 10 months must now acknowledge the softer revenue environment. Germany and North America remain material drags. Yet the adjusted EPS beat of +3.5% (22.37p vs 21.6p) is real and structural: record gross margins at 17.7%, H2 profit conversion increasing to 60%, exceptional cash conversion at 123%, and UK&I operating profit up 30%. The ERP write-off removes an overhang and future capex drag.

The key structural positive is the improving H2 profit weighting. H2 EPS of 15.67p was +8.1% YoY — the first meaningful H2 recovery after two years of sharp declines. Cash conversion of 123% (long-term average ~80%) signals working capital discipline and de-leveraging progress. Adjusted net debt/EBITDA improved from 2.5x at H1 to 2.17x at year end, with £300m+ of facilities available. The dividend reset to 25% payout (5.25p vs 13.0p) is painful for income holders but signals balance sheet prioritisation ahead of an expected M&A resumption in 2026.

The score sits at the amber band floor (50) because the upgrade impulse is real but constrained. Brokers will revise FY26 EPS +3–6% upward from the 23.9p FY2 base while trimming revenue estimates. Most will reiterate Buy with 300–350p TPs — giving 90–120% upside from 160p — but the re-rating catalyst is absent until H1 FY26 shows Germany recovering, North America stabilising, and the new digital/AI productivity investments delivering. The H2 FY26 profit seasonality (60%+ expected again) means H1 FY26 will likely disappoint relative to full-year hopes, making patience essential.
