scorecards.analysisTitle: PEBB · The Pebble Group PLC · 17 Mar 2026
scorecards.analysisHtml:
Phase 0 — Routing & FX
  • Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY results for year ended 31 December 2025. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.
  • FX Check: Facilisgroup revenues are USD-denominated (~£17.2m / £124.7m total = 13.8% of Group revenue). No single non-GBP currency exceeds 30% of revenues. Brand Addition invoices in multiple currencies with no single currency exceeding 30%. No FX Rule 1 penalty applies.
Phase 1 — Data Context
  • FY1 consensus (pre-RNS): EPS 3.8p, Revenue £126.5m. FY2 consensus: EPS 4.5p, Revenue £131.8m.
  • Forecast momentum: EPS net change over snapshot period = 0.0% (completely static at 3.8p throughout ~10 months). Revenue drifted from £128.8m to £126.5m (−1.8%). Zero upgrades in EPS. Last-4-week trend: FLAT. Momentum classification: dormant — the RNS is the first new information in nearly a year.
  • 3-year average H1 % of FY: Revenue H1 avg = 48.2%; EPS H1 avg = 39.9%.
  • H1 actuals (from Sharescope): H1 Revenue = £58.6m; H1 EPS = 1.2p. Implied H2 actual = £66.1m revenue (+2.5% vs prior H2 £64.5m); 2.66p EPS (−1.5% vs prior H2 2.7p).
  • FY results vs consensus: Adj EPS 3.86p vs 3.8p cns (+1.6% beat). Revenue £124.7m vs £126.5m cns (−1.4% miss). EBITDA £15.8m = exactly in line with cns £15.8m.
Phase 2 — RNS Extraction & Quantification
  1. Group revenue: £124.7m (FY24: £125.3m) = −0.5% YoY, and −1.4% vs cns £126.5m.
    "Group revenue of £124.7m (FY 24: £125.3m) was in line with the prior year."
  2. Adjusted EPS: 3.86p (FY24: 4.63p) = −16.6% YoY, but +1.6% vs cns 3.8p.
    "Basic adjusted earnings per share was 3.86 pence per share (FY 24: 4.63 pence per share), a decrease of 0.77 pence per share."
  3. Adj EBITDA: £15.8m (FY24: £16.7m) = exactly in line with cns £15.8m. The planned investment in Facilisgroup sales/marketing (~$1m incremental) absorbed as guided.
    "Group Adjusted EBITDA was £15.8m (FY 24: £16.7m), reflecting the signalled investment to accelerate new Partner acquisition at Facilisgroup."
  4. Facilisgroup Partner wins: 30 new Partners in FY25 vs 16 in FY24. Total: 253 Partners (FY24: 239). Underlying retention 97% (FY24: 96%). Average LTV ~$0.5m per new Partner.
    "Secured 30 new Partners during the year (FY 24: 16), following an incremental investment of approximately $1m in sales and marketing."
  5. Facilisgroup ARR flat in USD: ARR $21.6m both FY24 and FY25. GBP decline due to FX only. Revenue recognition lag — Partner subscription build lagged churn impact in FY25. FY26 to benefit from in-year cohort.
    "ARR from Partner subscriptions was flat in the year reflecting reduced Partner numbers entering FY25. The in-year build of subscriptions from new Partner acquisition lagged the impact of Partner churn."
  6. Brand Addition margin improvement: EBITDA margin 10.6% (FY24: 10.0%). Gross margin 37.0% (FY24: 35.2%). EBITDA £11.4m (FY24: £10.8m). Revenue flat at £107.5m. New client wins £6.5m (FY24: £5.3m).
    "Adjusted EBITDA returns increased to 10.6% (FY 24: 10.0%) and gross margin increased to 37.0% (FY 24: 35.2%)."
  7. Free cash flow conversion: 91% (FY24: 68%). Operating cash flow £7.5m. Reduced capex (£4.9m vs £6.8m) driving improvement.
    "Free cash flow conversion increased to 91% (FY 24: 68%), reflecting reduced capital expenditure and demonstrating the inherent cash-generative characteristics of the business."
  8. Capital returns: £11.7m in FY25 (FY24: £3.4m) via £3.0m dividend, £2.2m market buybacks, £6.5m tender offer. New £5.0m share buyback commencing today.
    "Capital returns to shareholders totalled £11.7m in FY 25 (FY 24: £3.4m)... Today we announce our intention to commence a share buyback for consideration of up to £5.0m."
  9. Dividend: Final 2.0p per share (FY24: 1.85p), +8.1%. Payable 11 May 2026.
    "The Board is pleased to propose the payment of a final dividend of 2.0 pence per share for FY 25 (FY 24: 1.85 pence per share)."
  10. FY26 outlook: Facilisgroup expected revenue growth from accelerating Partner cohort; Brand Addition seeking revenue growth with maintained margin improvement above 10%.
    "At Facilisgroup, we are becoming increasingly confident in the high Partner lifetime value and the ability to convert new Partners at a healthy acquisition cost which underpins expected revenue growth... At Brand Addition, the new business momentum continues and in 2026 we seek to increase revenues whilst maintaining the improvement in profit margins."
  11. Strategic review: Board "actively reviewing its strategic options, including the Group's structure." This introduces optionality around a potential separation of Facilisgroup and Brand Addition.
    "The Board continues to actively review its strategic options, including the Group's structure, to ensure long-term shareholder value creation reflects the financial strength and market-leading positions of the Group's individual businesses."
  12. Cash: £9.6m at 31 Dec 2025 (FY24: £16.5m); £7.4m at 16 March 2026. Debt-free with £10m undrawn RCF. Share count reduced from 164.8m to 148.7m at year-end.

scorecards.analysisTitle: SWG · Shearwater Group PLC — Cybersecurity · 17 Mar 2026
scorecards.analysisHtml:
Phase 0 — Routing & FX
  • Routing mode: pre-H1 (Q4). RNS = H1 Results for six months ended 31 December 2025 (H1 FY26). SWG changed year-end to 30 June 2025. No FX rule — UK-domiciled revenues 78% of total.
  • Comparability note: SWG restated prior periods for revised revenue recognition policy (cloud-hosted software spread over contract life). H1 FY25 restated = Jul–Dec 2024 (£10.7m). The gross margin decline (20% H1 FY26 vs 30% restated prior) is policy-driven, not a deterioration of underlying economics.
Phase 1 — Data Context
  • FY1 cns: EPS 4.5p, Revenue £35.5m. FY2: not in consensus.
  • Momentum: EPS +200% (1.5p → 4.5p — two large upgrade steps Jul and Nov 2025). Revenue: 39m → 35.5m (−8.9% — reflects revised recognition methodology). Last-4-week FLAT. Stock: 78p → 90p (Nov 2025) → 42p (current — de-rated despite EPS upgrades).
  • 3yr avg H1%: Revenue 37.7% (3yr avg). EPS: 20.0% (1yr avg only — unreliable).
  • H1 tracking baseline: Revenue 37.7% × £35.5m = £13.4m. Actual H1 = £14.0m.
  • H1 tracking (Revenue): £14.0m / £35.5m = 39.4% vs 3yr avg 37.7% → +1.7pp → 🟢 MILD BUY SIGNAL (just above threshold).
  • EPS tracking: UNTRACKABLE — adj EPS −1p H1 vs 4.5p FY cns; entire EPS delivery deferred to H2 in SWG's established pattern.
Phase 2 — RNS Extraction & Quantification

H1 Results — Six months ended 31 December 2025 (H1 FY26)

  1. Revenue: £14.0m vs H1 FY25 restated £10.7m = +31% YoY. H1 tracking: 39.4% vs 3yr avg 37.7% = +1.7pp 🟢 Mild Buy.
    "Revenue of £14.0m, an increase of 31% on the equivalent period in the prior year"
  2. Adj EBITDA: £0.0m (£9k) vs H1 FY25 £0.1m = flat. Entire FY26 cns EBITDA (£2.4m) must be delivered in H2 — binary H2 risk.
    "small Adjusted EBITDA profit for the period of £0.0m, broadly in line with that in the equivalent period of the prior year"
  3. Key H1 contract wins: £7.3m MNO extension (£3.5m revenue in FY26); ~£1m Government expansion.
    "A £7.3m contract extension and expansion with a leading mobile network operator… with £3.5m of revenue from this contract expected to impact FY26 results"
  4. Post-period wins (H2 already contracted): £9m financial organisation renewal; £1.3m UK telco network monitoring. Total >£13m H2 contracted.
    "we have more than £13m of contracted business since the start of H2, which support the delivery of FY26 expectations"
  5. FY26 full-year guidance: in line with market expectations. "confident in delivering improved profitability in H2."
    "the Board is confident in delivering improved profitability in H2 and achieving full-year expectations"
  6. Gross margin 20% vs 30% restated prior — policy-driven, not structural. H1 FY26 revenue = £10m new on-premise solutions at 21.5% margin + carry-forward from FY25; H2 expected to deliver higher-margin new solutions.
    "This component of revenue has a lower margin profile than up-front revenue recognised on the delivery of new solutions"
  7. Cash: £2.2m (H1 FY25: £3.6m). Adjusted for £1.5m post-period receipt = £3.7m (in-line). Timing distortion.
    "period-end cash of £2.2m… the receipt of £1.5m from the customer only arriving on 20 January 2026"

Shearwater delivered H1 FY26 results with H1 revenue of £14.0m tracking +1.7pp above the seasonal norm (39.4% of FY1 consensus vs 3yr avg 37.7%), triggering a 🟢 Mild Buy Signal. Revenue grew +31% YoY (Services +37%), reflecting strong demand from blue-chip telco, financial services and government clients. Post-period, the Group has already secured >£13m of H2 contracted business — including a £9m financial organisation renewal — which substantially de-risks H2 delivery. Pentest returned to profitability and G-Cloud 15 will expand available public sector products from 32 to 55.

The dominant concern is that H1 adj EBITDA was £0.0m (£9k), meaning the entire FY26 consensus EBITDA of £2.4m must be delivered in H2. This is structurally consistent with SWG's established H2-weighted pattern (FY25 showed H1 EBITDA £0.6m vs H2 £1.5m annualised), and management confirms confidence in H2 delivery. The gross margin decline from 30% to 20% is driven by the revenue recognition policy change (cloud-hosted services spread over contract life) rather than a fundamental deterioration — but this will require broker education. Cash of £2.2m (adjusted £3.7m for one timing receipt) is low in absolute terms.

Cavendish is expected to publish a BUY-maintained note citing the revenue trajectory and H2 contracted pipeline, but near-zero H1 EBITDA and the gross margin optics will prevent a meaningful re-rating until H2 results in September/October 2026. This is a binary outcome: strong H2 delivery confirms the 90p TP case; any H2 slippage would create further downside from the already de-rated 42p. Phase 0 — Routing & FX
  • Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). RNS is FY Results for year ended 31 December 2025.
  • FX Check: TPFG operates entirely in the UK. Zero non-GBP currency exposure. FX Rule 1 does not apply. No penalty.
Phase 1 — Data Context
  • FY1 consensus: EPS 37.0p, Revenue £84.3m. FY2: EPS 38.7p, Revenue £87.6m.
  • Consensus net change: +5.1% (35.2p → 37.0p). Multiple modest upgrades. Revenue flat at £83.5–84.3m. Last-4-week: FLAT. Momentum: stalling.

Phase 2 — RNS Extraction & Quantification

RNS TYPE: FY Results (year ended 31 December 2025)

    "Group revenue increased 25% to £84.3m (2024: £67.3m), 9% growth on a pro-forma basis"
  2. Adj EPS: 40.3p (+27% YoY) vs cns 37.0p = +8.9% beat. Lower effective tax rate (22% vs 29% prior year) contributed.
    "Adjusted basic earnings per share increased 27% to 40.3p (2024: 31.7p)"
  3. Adj PBT: £31.0m (+39% YoY) vs cns £30.7m = +1.0%. EBITDA £30.3m (+49%). Adj op margin 38% (+400bps).
    "EBITDA increased 49% to £30.3m (2024: £20.4m)"
  4. Net debt: £2.3m (leverage <0.1x) vs £9.1m prior year. Cash generated £22.1m (+50%). Ahead of expectations.
    "Net debt reduced to £2.3m (2024: £9.1m)... which was ahead of our expectations"
  5. Dividend: 22p total (+22% from 18p). Final 15p. DPS cns 21p = +4.8% beat.
    "Proposed final dividend of 15p, making a full year dividend of 22p per share, up 22%"
  6. SAFS acquisition (Jan 2026): 85% stake, 34 advisers added (total 315), immediately earnings accretive, total consideration £1.5m.
    "In January 2026, we completed the acquisition of an 85% stake in Smart Advice Financial Solutions ('SAFS')... is immediately earnings accretive"
  7. Privilege programme: £1.5m incremental revenue in year 1. AI sales agent (launched early 2026) +25% valuation appointments.
    "An AI sales agent launched earlier in 2026 is already delivering measurable benefits, generating 25% more valuation appointments than traditional in-person processes"
  8. Renters' Rights Act: Portfolio moderated 153k→149k. "We do not view this as a structural threat."
    "our platform model, compliance infrastructure and scale enable franchisees to navigate regulatory change with confidence"
Phase 3 — Historical Benchmarking
  • H1 Revenue tracking: £40.3m / £84.3m = 47.8% vs 3yr avg 45.5% = +2.3pp → 🟢 MILD BUY SIGNAL (noting distortion from acquisition timing in 3yr avg).

  • H2 EPS delivered: 40.3 – 18.1 = 22.2p vs prior H2 16.3p = +36.2% YoY — synergies accelerating in H2.
  • EPS trajectory: ~28.4p → ~28.4p → ~31.4p (+10.6%) → 40.3p (+28.3%). Accelerating — post-acquisition earnings power step-change.
  • Structural flags: (1) Privilege programme scaling — new income stream. (2) SAFS immediately accretive, adviser count restored. (3) AI tools delivering measurable productivity gains. (4) Net debt <0.1x — M&A firepower for platform building. (5) Renters' Rights Act manageable through franchise model.

Phase 4 — Broker Reaction Simulation
1#1 Driver — Adj EPS +8.9% beat (40.3p vs 37.0p): Canaccord and Berenberg will lead with the 40.3p delivery. The beat is multi-source: operating leverage, cost synergies, lower effective tax rate (22% vs 29%), and Privilege programme contribution in year one.
2#2 Driver — Balance sheet ahead of expectations (<0.1x leverage): The significantly better-than-expected net debt position unlocks immediate M&A optionality for a business with a proven buy-and-build track record. Brokers will model a further platform acquisition during FY26.
3Forecast revisions: FY26 EPS upgrade from 37.0p to ~42–45p (+14–22%); SAFS earnings accretion, Privilege scaling, AI productivity. FY27 to ~46–50p. Revenue FY26 ~£87–88m. TP 649p → likely 700–750p+.

The Privilege programme provides some offset but is early stage. "landlord caution ahead of the Renters' Rights Act and a more measured pace of portfolio acquisitions"
6Tone: Strongly positive / upgrade cycle starting. Record results, EPS beat, DPS beat, balance sheet ahead, SAFS accretion, AI delivering, Privilege scaling. Canaccord will issue enthusiastic buy note with material FY upgrades and TP increase.
Strongly Positive · Upgrade Cycle Starting

80

Confidence range: 76–84 · No FX penalty
Adj EPS +8.9% beat+9

SAFS post-period accretion+2
Renters' Rights Act portfolio headwind–3
Tax rate partly one-off?–1
Base (pre-FY, significant beat)+60

TPFG delivered record FY25 results with adjusted EPS of 40.3p — a 8.9% beat against the 37.0p consensus — and revenue exactly in line at £84.3m. The beat was broad-based: all three divisions (Franchising, Financial Services, Licensing) delivered growth; EBITDA grew 49% to £30.3m with adjusted operating margin expanding to 38% (+400bps); and the balance sheet improved dramatically to net debt of £2.3m (leverage <0.1x), significantly ahead of expectations.

The structural improvement in earnings quality is the key investment thesis. The integration of Belvoir and GPEA has delivered synergies ahead of schedule, the Privilege programme generated £1.5m incremental revenue in year one, and the SAFS acquisition (315 advisers, immediately accretive) provides FY26 EPS accretion. The AI sales agent deployed in early 2026 is generating 25% more valuation appointments — a structural productivity improvement. The balance sheet at <0.1x leverage provides significant M&A firepower for further platform building.

FY26 EPS should be upgraded from 37.0p to the 42–45p range. The primary near-term risk is the Renters' Rights Act driving further portfolio moderation, but the franchise model's regulatory navigation capability and Privilege programme provide meaningful mitigation. Canaccord will issue a strongly positive upgrade note; the stock at 412.5p trades at a significant discount to what should be a revised TP of 700–750p+.

TPFG delivered a definitive EPS beat as the single most important catalyst: adjusted basic EPS of 40.3p versus FY1 consensus of 37.0p, a beat of +3.3p (+8.9%). Revenue of £84.3m matched consensus exactly. Adjusted PBT of £31.0m versus consensus £30.7m was a marginal beat at the top line, with the real earnings surprise flowing through a sharply improved effective tax rate of 22% (prior year: 29%) and 4pp margin expansion to an adjusted operating margin of 38%. This is unambiguously a results beat driven by structural quality improvement, not one-off items.

The H2 FY25 EPS implied from full-year actuals is 22.2p versus prior-year H2 of 16.3p — a +36% YoY H2 EPS surge that confirms the operating leverage thesis and validates the post-acquisition consolidation. Although the H1 EPS tracking appeared soft at the interim stage (18.1p representing only 44.9% of the eventual FY versus the 48.9% historical baseline — a −4.0pp deviation), this was a structural artefact of the enlarged group's H2 weighting rather than a genuine earnings shortfall. The bear case is further contained by net debt of just £2.3m (leverage 0.1x) and cash from operations of £22.1m (+50% YoY), giving the group a fortress balance sheet. The only genuine structural risk — the managed lettings portfolio declining by 4,000 properties (−2.6%) to 149,000 due to Renters' Rights Act landlord caution — is partially offset by the Privilege programme (£1.5m incremental revenue) and does not threaten the overall growth trajectory given Financial Services and Licensing division momentum.

FY26 EPS consensus will need to move from 37.0p to approximately 40–42p (a +8–12% upgrade cycle) to reflect the higher earnings base now established. FY27 follows at 42–45p range. Target price consensus of 649p — already implying 57% upside from the current 412.5p — is unlikely to be cut and may see modest uplifts to 650–700p on updated models anchored to 40p+ FY26 EPS at 15–16x. The primary constraint on a higher score is the absence of a revenue beat (exact match only), the EBITDA undershoot versus consensus, and the mild overhang from the lettings portfolio contraction narrative. However, the upgrade cycle is highly probable: a clean 9% EPS beat with margin expansion, near-zero debt, a raised dividend, and confident multi-driver FY26 outlook represents exactly the conditions that generate sustained broker upgrades and price target re-ratings on AIM franchise businesses.

  4. Balance sheet: Net total debt $19.3m at year-end; ND/EBITDA 1.17x. M&T Bank credit facilities expanded post-period: working capital line to $3.8m, acquisition line to $22m ($19.5m drawn). Balance sheet described as "robust."

The H1 EPS tracking data confirms structural weakness in the consensus: at 22.4p, H1 represents only 57.1% of the 39.2p FY1 consensus, against a 3-year seasonal average of 67.2% — a deviation of –10.1pp, which fires the SELL SIGNAL. The implied H2 EPS burden of 16.8p is nearly double the historical H2 average of 9.7p, making the current consensus structurally implausible without a transformational change in H2 profitability that has no historical precedent.

The FX Rule 1 penalty of –11 points is applied for ~100% USD exposure with no prior-year average rate disclosed. Despite solid underlying operational execution (EBITDA +15%, margins improving, balance sheet strong at 1.17x ND/EBITDA), the GBP translation issue and EPS H1 tracking weakness together point firmly to a cut cycle. The market has already priced in significant deterioration (share price –68% from peak), but formal broker downgrades to revenue and EPS are expected following this RNS. The IoT/Bluebot strategy is interesting but early-stage and insufficient to prevent near-term cuts.

Record retail market share was achieved across timber, tiling & flooring and paint, with TradePro active membership growing to 643,000 (+10.7% YoY). Design & Installation recorded five consecutive quarters of ordered sales growth and three consecutive quarters of delivered sales growth. Net cash of £91.7m reflects strong underlying cash generation.

The H1 EPS tracking signal of +5.3pp above seasonal norm was the leading indicator that a FY beat was probable. The explicit FY26 guidance — "comfortable with consensus expectations for adjusted PBT" citing the specific £57.6m midpoint — provides an unusually direct confirmation of the FY26 floor. The 300-store ambition with capex accelerating to £40–45m from FY26 creates a clear long-term growth runway, even if near-term FCF is modestly compressed by the investment step-up.

Brokers will upgrade FY26 EPS from ~15.9p to the 18–19p range (consistent with the confirmed £57.6m adj PBT) and raise TPs from £2.60 to approximately £2.80–3.00. The main near-term headwind is the working capital unwind of £5–10m in FY26 and the capex acceleration, but these are investment for sustainable growth rather than structural concerns. The stock at 215p versus a revised TP of ~£2.80 represents meaningful upside.

scorecards.analysisHtml:
Phase 0 — Routing & FX
  • Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY Results for the year ended 31 December 2025. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.
  • FX Check: Approximately 91% of sales denominated in currencies other than sterling, mostly USD and EUR. USD/GBP average 2025 = 1.312 vs 2024 = 1.278 — GBP strengthened 2.7% against USD (adverse for USD revenues). EUR/GBP average 2025 = 1.173 vs 2024 = 1.177 — GBP marginally weaker vs EUR (near-neutral). USD exposure estimated at ~35% of revenues. GBP/USD change = ~3.5 cents, just above the ±2-cent neutral band. However, the company deployed forward exchange contracts and the net PBT impact of currency movements was effectively nil (+£0.1m). FX Rule 1 applied at the lower band: –8 points. Badge: FX Rule 1 applied (−8 pts) · ~35% USD · GBP headwind largely hedged.
Phase 1 — Data Context
  • FY1 consensus (pre-RNS): EPS 32.0p, Revenue £158.3m. FY2: EPS 39.5p, Revenue £191.6m.
  • Consensus momentum: EPS net change +8.8% over full period (29.4p → 32.0p), with step upgrades in Aug 2025, Jan–Feb 2026. Last-4-week trend: FLAT. Momentum: building through the year, stalling immediately pre-results.
  • 3yr avg H1 % of FY: Revenue 48.5%; EPS 33.8% (highly H2-weighted for earnings).
  • H1 known from Sharescope: Revenue £77.4m; EPS 19.4p. Implied H2 = 38.0 – 19.4 = 18.65p vs prior H2 ~13.35p = +39.7% YoY.
  • FX: Rule 1 applied (−8 pts). USD ~35%. GBP/USD 2025 avg 1.312 vs 2024 avg 1.278. Net PBT impact after hedging: +£0.1m (effectively nil). Penalty carried forward.
Phase 2 — RNS Extraction & Quantification

RNS TYPE: FY Results (Preliminary, unaudited, year ended 31 December 2025)

  1. Revenue FY25: £158.5m (+7.2% YoY from £147.8m) vs FY1 cns £158.3m = +0.1% in line. Record Group revenue.
    "Record Group revenue of £158.5m, 7% higher than the prior year (2024: £147.8m)"
  2. Adjusted EPS: 38.0p vs FY1 cns 32.0p = +18.75% beat. vs prior year 25.95p = +46% YoY. This is the dominant metric and far exceeds even the FY26 consensus forecast.
    "Adjusted Basic EPS up 46% to 38.00p (2024: 25.95p)"
  3. Adjusted PBT: £21.2m (+38.6% YoY from £15.3m) vs FY1 cns PBT ~£21.1m = essentially in line. The EPS beat is partly driven by a favourable effective tax rate of 12.3% adjusted (R&D, patent box) and recognition of deferred tax assets in Poland (£3.6m) and US (£1.5m).
    "Adjusted profit before tax increased 38% to £21.2m (2024: £15.3m)"
  4. Adjusted operating margin: 14.4% (+220bps from 12.2%). Adjusted operating profit £22.8m (+26% from £18.1m). Structural margin expansion driven by MEL closure, mix improvement, operational efficiency.
    "Adjusted Operating Margin 14.4% · 220bps [improvement]"
  5. H1/H2 split: H1 EPS 19.4p (from Sharescope); implied H2 = 38.0 – 19.4 = 18.65p. Implied H2 vs prior H2 (FY24 adj EPS 25.95p – H1 12.6p = 13.35p): +39.7% YoY. H2 momentum: Strong.
    "2025 Adjusted Basic EPS 38.00p vs 2024 25.95p"
  6. Cash generation: £39.7m (+31% from £30.4m). Cash conversion 101%. FCF before M&A: £23.1m. Net debt (bank basis) £31.5m, leverage 0.8x (improved from 0.9x). Balance sheet described as "strong."
    "Cash generated from operations up 31% to £39.7m (2024: £30.4m) … FCF of >£23m … leverage ratio improved at 0.8x"
  7. Dividend: 7.85p total (5.35p final + 2.50p interim) vs cns DPS 8.00p = –0.15p (immaterial). +5% increase on prior year total of 7.48p. Subject to AGM approval.
    "Final dividend up 5% to 5.35p (2024: 5.10p)"
  8. OKC acquisition: Completed November 2025 at €27.6m initial + deferred up to €8.4m. Added £2m revenue in FY25 (partial year). Earnings accretive FY26. Full-year contribution targeted for 2026.
    "The acquisition is expected to be earnings accretive in 2026."
  9. Vietnam factory: £4.3m invested in FY25 of ~$32m total project. Partnership with Seoheung (17.5% stake, $10m contribution). Initial production expected late 2026/early 2027.
    "Construction and commissioning of the leased Vietnam site is underway, ahead of planned completion later this year / early 2027."
  10. Medium-term targets: FY2029 revenue >£230m (7% CAGR from £158.5m); operating profit >£40m by FY2029 (~75% above FY25 £22.8m); ROCE >20% by FY2029; cash conversion >95%. Longer-term ambition: revenue >£300m, operating profit >£60m.
    "Organic growth of 7% CAGR to deliver FY2029 revenue of >£230m; Operating profit of >£40m by FY2029; ROCE of over 20% by FY2029"
  11. FY26 trading outlook: "Trading in the early part of the year has been in line with our expectations." Footwear volumes to moderate as customers normalise inventory. Transport & Smart Technologies continuing strong. OKC integration progressing well.
    "Trading in the early part of the year has been in line with our expectations, supported by continued demand in Transport & Smart Technologies and improving order books across several markets."
  12. Footwear moderation caveat: "In footwear, we expect volumes to moderate from the unusually high levels experienced in 2024 and 2025 as customers normalise inventory positions which is an expected transition."
    "In footwear, we expect volumes to moderate from the unusually high levels experienced in 2024 and 2025 as customers normalise inventory positions which is an expected transition, and our operating plans reflect this shift."
Phase 3 — Historical Benchmarking
  • Revenue HoH trajectory: FY YoY growth: FY23 £127.3m → FY24 £126.9m (–0.3%) → FY25 est H1 £77.4m → FY25 actual £158.5m (+7.2%). H1 revenue growth: 9.5% → 10.1% → 8.8% (steady deceleration). H2 revenue: prior year £76.7m, implied FY25 H2 = £81.1m (+5.7% YoY). Classification: Volatile then Steady — large swing in FY24 due to MEL, underlying foams business showing consistent mid-to-high single digit revenue growth.
  • EPS HoH trajectory: FY23 adj EPS ~£29.8p (est); FY24 adj EPS 25.95p (–13%); FY25 adj EPS 38.0p (+46%). H1 EPS: 12.6p → 19.4p (+54% YoY). H2 EPS: FY24 H2 ~13.35p; FY25 H2 implied 18.65p (+39.7%). Classification: Accelerating — clear step-change in earnings power from MEL closure and margin expansion.
  • Implied H2 Momentum (pre-FY mode): H2 Revenue: +5.7% YoY vs prior H2 → Moderate. H2 EPS: +39.7% YoY vs prior H2 → Strong. The H2 EPS acceleration is structural (MEL eliminated, tax benefits, margin improvement).
  • Forecast momentum overlay: EPS consensus stepped up from 29.4p (May 2025) through multiple upgrades to 32.0p. Last 4 weeks flat at 32.0p pre-results. Now 38.0p actual = immediate comprehensive upgrade requirement. Net change full period +8.8% — understates the actual delivery. Revenue consensus very stable at £158.3m for most of the period, confirming revenue was well-flagged; the surprise is entirely in EPS/margins.
  • Structural flags: (1) MEL permanently closed — removes ~£4-5m annual loss drag permanently. (2) Margin step-change: 12.2% → 14.4% with medium-term target >18%. (3) OKC acquisition adds European revenue diversity. (4) Vietnam factory creates Consumer & Lifestyle capacity closer to Asian customers. (5) Tax benefits (R&D, patent box, deferred tax) structurally improve effective rate below 20%. These are durable earnings improvements, not one-offs.

Phase 4 — Broker Reaction Simulation
1#1 Driver — EPS +18.75% beat vs consensus: The 38.0p actual against 32.0p pre-results consensus is the dominant number. Every broker note will lead with this figure and note that the company has delivered FY25 EPS comfortably ahead of the existing FY26 forecast of 32.0p. This forces immediate comprehensive upgrades to FY26/FY27 EPS estimates.
2#2 Driver — Structural margin expansion: The 220bps improvement to 14.4% operating margin, with a stated medium-term target of >18%, provides a credible multi-year upgrade runway. Brokers will model the trajectory from 14.4% toward 18%+ and assign higher earnings multiples accordingly.
3Forecast revision FY1/FY2: FY26 (new FY1) EPS: upgrade from 32.0p to likely 42–46p range (+31–44%). Revenue FY26: upgrade to ~£165-170m (+5–8%), incorporating OKC full year contribution and organic growth. FY27 EPS: from 39.5p to approximately 48–54p. Target price: consensus £6.06 will almost certainly be revised to £7.00–£8.00+ range. At 379p close, the stock trades on a significant discount to likely revised TPs.
4"In line" FY26 guidance read-through: "Trading in the early part of the year has been in line with our expectations" is a contained, pragmatic statement — not a conservative flag in the traditional sense given the massive FY25 beat. Brokers will interpret this as management anchoring FY26 expectations while the footwear normalisation plays out. The medium-term targets (£230m revenue, £40m+ operating profit by 2029) are the more significant forward signals.
5Key risk — footwear moderation: The explicit caveat that footwear volumes will moderate in FY26 is the primary constraint on the upgrade narrative. Consumer & Lifestyle was 50% of revenue in FY25. If footwear declines materially, it could suppress H1 FY26 revenue growth. Brokers will model this conservatively, which is why FY26 revenue upgrades are likely to be modest (5–8%) even as EPS upgrades are more aggressive (driven by base effect and margin improvement). "In footwear, we expect volumes to moderate from the unusually high levels experienced in 2024 and 2025."
6Overall broker-note tone: Strongly positive / upgrade cycle starting. Peel Hunt, Singer Capital Markets and others covering ZTF will issue immediate positive flash notes with material upgrades. The combination of a record-breaking EPS beat, clear structural margin improvement, strong cash generation, a multi-year growth strategy with explicit targets, and a FY25 EPS that has already exceeded FY26 consensus creates a compelling upgrade narrative. The stock at 379p will be seen as materially undervalued on revised estimates.
Strongly Positive · Upgrade Cycle Starting
Phase 5 — Final Score & Verdict
76
/100
Confidence range: 72–82 · FX Rule 1 applied (−8 pts) · ~35% USD · GBP headwind largely hedged
EPS beat +18.75% vs consensus+20
Margin expansion +220bps structural+5
H2 EPS momentum +39.7% YoY+4
Record cash generation / strong BS+2
Medium-term strategy roadmap clarity+3
Footwear moderation FY26 headwind–4
FX Rule 1 penalty (~35% USD)–8
Base midpoint (significant beat)+54

Zotefoams delivered a landmark set of FY25 results, with adjusted EPS of 38.0p representing an 18.75% beat against the 32.0p consensus — and, remarkably, already exceeding the FY26 consensus forecast. Revenue of £158.5m was essentially in line (+0.1%), confirming the EPS beat was entirely margin-driven: adjusted operating margin expanded 220bps to 14.4%, driven by the elimination of MEL losses, improved product mix and operational efficiency. Cash conversion hit 101% with FCF over £23m.

The structural improvement in earnings power is the key investment thesis: MEL is permanently closed, the effective tax rate has been reduced through R&D credits and patent box claims, deferred tax assets of £5.1m have been recognised in Poland and the US, and the OKC acquisition brings full-year FY26 accretion. The medium-term targets — £230m revenue and £40m operating profit by FY2029 — imply a 75% increase in operating profit from FY25 and provide a clear multi-year upgrade runway. Brokers must now comprehensively re-base FY26 EPS estimates from ~32p to the 42–46p range.

The primary constraint on a higher score is the footwear moderation caveat for FY26 (Consumer & Lifestyle = 50% of revenue) and the FX Rule 1 penalty reflecting GBP strength against USD. However, these headwinds are well-flagged and partly offset by OKC, Vietnam optionality and Transport & Smart Technologies strength. The upgrade cycle is clearly starting; the only debate among brokers will be the pace and magnitude of the re-rating.

Phase 0 — Routing & FX
  • Routing mode: pre-H1 (latest qtrly report = 'Q4'). Interpreting incoming RNS as a pre-H1 trading update accordingly. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.
  • FX: Brief trading update — no Currency Movements section and no explicit revenue-by-currency breakdown. Diploma has material USD/CAD exposure through North American operations but no single non-GBP currency is confirmed above 30% in this RNS. No FX penalty applied — insufficient confirmed exposure data.
Phase 1 — Data Context
  • Consensus: FY1 (FY ending 30 September 2026) EPS 195.8p, revenue £1,665.0m; FY2 EPS 207.8p, revenue £1,758.5m. Analyst consensus adjusted operating profit for FY26: £377m — cited verbatim in the RNS footnote by management (as at 17 March 2026).
  • Forecast momentum: EPS upgraded 160.9p → 195.8p over ~10 months (+21.7%) — one of the most consistent upgrade cycles in this batch. Large step in November 2025 (172→188p), further step December–January (191→196p). Last 4 weeks: FLAT. Revenue +13.4%.
  • 3yr avg H1% of FY: revenue 46.6%, EPS 45.0%. Consensus H1 baselines: revenue £776.9m; EPS 88.1p. Buy triggers: H1 Rev > £788.6m; H1 EPS > 89.4p. Assessable at HY results 19 May 2026.
  • H1 tracking: UNTRACKABLE. No H1 actual numbers provided in this qualitative pre-H1 update. Both column 5 indicators fire as N/A. H1 results due 19 May 2026.
Phase 2 — RNS Extraction & Quantification
  1. Organic revenue growth guidance upgraded to 9% (from 6%). +3pp upgrade to the primary growth metric. Remaining H1-weighted per management commentary.
    "Organic revenue growth increased to 9% (from 6%), remaining H1 weighted"
  2. Operating margin guidance upgraded to c.25% (from c.22.5%). +250bps expansion. On FY1 consensus revenue ~£1,665m, this implies operating profit ~£416m vs prior consensus £377m = ~+10.3% OP upgrade.
    "Operating margin increased to c.25% (from c.22.5%)"
  3. "c.13% upgrade to consensus operating profit." Management cites prior consensus OP (£377m, dated 17 March 2026) then states it needs to increase by 13% — exceptional transparency; rare for a FTSE 100 company to self-quantify a consensus upgrade in a trading update.
    "Representing a c.13% upgrade to consensus operating profit. Analyst consensus adjusted operating profit for FY26 is £377m, as at 17 March 2026."
  4. "Earnings growth over 20%." Explicit EPS guidance — not a range. Current consensus 195.8p; 20% growth on any reasonable base implies minimum ~215–235p, materially above current consensus.
    "We expect another year of sustainable quality compounding, with earnings growth over 20% at strong returns on capital"
  5. Peerless — "outstanding organic growth performance in H1, with H2 returning to more typical growth rates." H2 moderation explicitly guided — management pre-managing expectations to avoid a negative H2 surprise against very strong comparators.
    "We expect another outstanding organic growth performance in the first half, with the second half returning to more typical growth rates against very strong comparators."
  6. Windy City Wire — "performing very well... strong growth in datacentres and digital antenna systems." Structural AI/datacentre demand driver within the Controls segment.
    "Windy City Wire is performing very well. Strong growth supported by excellent execution in markets including datacentres and digital antenna systems."
  7. International Seals — "remains challenging, particularly in the UK." Drag on overall Seals H1 growth, consistent with FY25 growth rates.
    "International Seals remains challenging - particularly in the UK - and will somewhat hold back overall Seals H1 growth rates, consistent with FY25 growth rates."
  8. Organic growth excluding Peerless — "strong and well ahead of our financial model." Critical signal: the upgrade is not Peerless-dependent. Confirms broad-based portfolio outperformance.
    "Organic growth excluding Peerless is strong and well ahead of our financial model."
  9. 8 acquisitions in preceding two quarters, ~£130m consideration, ~£20m annualised OP contribution. Not included in guidance — represents potential further upside if further deals completed.
    "we completed 8 acquisitions in the preceding two quarters for c.£130m with expected annualised operating profit contribution of c.£20m."
  10. Life Sciences — "performing consistently in a tough healthcare market, with share gains across medtech and IVD." Third segment delivering steady share gains despite market headwinds.
    "Life Sciences: Performing consistently in a tough healthcare market, with share gains across medtech and IVD."
  11. Net acquisition growth unchanged at 3%. M&A pipeline described as "healthy" near-term. Could increase if further acquisitions completed.
    "Net acquisition growth unchanged at 3%. This will increase if further acquisitions are made"
Phase 3 — Historical Benchmarking
  • Revenue trajectory: Strongly Accelerating. H1 FY24 +30.0%, H2 FY24 +9.4%, H1 FY25 +9.6%, H2 FY25 +17.4%. Now guiding ~12% total FY26 (9% organic + 3% acquisition). Continuous acceleration across every successive period.
  • EPS trajectory: Accelerating. H1 FY24 +25.4%, H2 FY24 +11.1%, H1 FY25 +10.4%, H2 FY25 +19.8%. Now guiding "over 20%" for full FY26 = acceleration continuing.
  • H1 tracking: UNTRACKABLE. No H1 actuals in this RNS — this is a qualitative pre-H1 update only. Baselines and buy triggers set for assessment on 19 May 2026 HY results: H1 Rev baseline £776.9m (buy trigger > £788.6m); H1 EPS baseline 88.1p (buy trigger > 89.4p). Qualitative signals (Peerless "outstanding," ex-Peerless "well ahead of model") are strongly positive but cannot be quantified for column 5 scoring until actuals are available.
  • Implied H2 momentum: Organic upgrade is H1-weighted; H2 returns to "more typical" rates for Peerless (~5–7% organic). With 3% acquisition growth, total H2 ~8–10%. Margin expansion to 25% applies to both halves. H2 classified moderate/solid — management has fully pre-communicated the moderation, substantially reducing surprise risk.
  • Forecast momentum: +21.7% EPS upgrade — the most consistent sustained upgrade cycle in this batch. Currently FLAT. This update restarts the cycle definitively — "over 20% earnings growth" requires a minimum upgrade from 195.8p to ~215–235p (+10–20%).
  • Structural flags: (1) Peerless aerospace: "demand and supply characteristics are favourable and sustainable" — multi-year structural tailwind. (2) Windy City Wire: AI/datacentre demand cited explicitly. (3) IS Group and Clarendon in "structurally growing markets like energy, defence and aerospace" — geopolitical tailwinds embedded in end-markets. (4) Eight acquisitions in two quarters — M&A compounding at pace; £20m annualised OP contribution not in any guidance figure.

Phase 4 — Broker Reaction Simulation
1#1 Driver — Formal, quantified OP margin upgrade to c.25% (+250bps) = ~13% OP upgrade to consensus: Management stated the prior consensus OP figure (£377m) and said it needs to increase by 13%. For a FTSE 100 quality compounder, a self-quantified guidance upgrade of this magnitude is extremely rare and will dominate every broker note.
2#2 Driver — "Earnings growth over 20%" as an explicit EPS guidance statement: Current consensus 195.8p. 20% growth on FY25 underlying EPS of ~175p implies ~210p; 20% on 195.8p implies 235p. Either framing puts current consensus materially below the floor. Brokers are forced to upgrade FY1 EPS to at minimum 215–235p range.
3Forecast revisions — FY1 EPS +13–20%, FY2 EPS +8–12%: Operating margin 25% on £1,710–1,730m revenue = £428–433m OP vs prior £377m. After finance costs and tax (~26% effective rate), EPS of ~215–235p. Target prices: £60.40 → £65–72+ range. Revenue upgrades to £1,710–1,730m range.
4Conservative guidance read-through: Management has 5 months of FY26 visibility when issuing this guidance (Oct 2025 – Mar 2026 largely locked). "Over 20% earnings growth" is a floor statement. Peerless H2 moderation is explicitly pre-communicated — downside risk in H2 is substantially reduced by this pre-management of expectations.
5Key risk — Peerless H2 moderation after exceptional H1: H2 returns to "more typical" growth vs "very strong comparators." International Seals UK remains challenging. If both headwinds converge in H2, the upgrade could partially reverse — but management has pre-communicated both, substantially reducing surprise risk.
6Overall tone: Strongly positive / upgrade cycle starting. A FTSE 100 quality compounder with a 7-year track record of 18% EPS CAGR issuing a self-quantified ~13% OP upgrade with "over 20% earnings growth" guidance, broad-based organic outperformance (ex-Peerless also "well ahead"), and a healthy M&A pipeline. Every major broker covering Diploma will issue an upgrade note today.
Phase 5 — Final Score & Verdict

Diploma has issued one of the most explicit and shareholder-friendly trading upgrades in its recent history. The direct citation of prior consensus operating profit (£377m) followed by a stated ~13% upgrade, combined with "earnings growth over 20%" for the full year, leaves virtually no room for misinterpretation. For a FTSE 100 compounding business with a seven-year track record of 18% EPS CAGR, this clarity of language signals genuine management conviction that is rare at this stage of a financial year.

Critically, the upgrade is broad-based: organic growth ex-Peerless is described as "well ahead of our financial model," confirming outperformance is not concentrated in a single aerospace name. The structural drivers are intact — Peerless aerospace benefits from "favourable and sustainable" supply/demand dynamics, Windy City Wire captures AI/datacentre demand, Life Sciences takes share in medtech and IVD, and eight acquisitions totalling £130m with £20m annualised OP contribution are not in any guidance figure. Current consensus EPS of 195.8p requires an upgrade to at minimum 215–235p, representing a 10–20% step-up.

The primary constraint on a higher score is the explicit H2 moderation signal for Peerless and the fact that H1 actuals cannot yet be verified. However, management's exceptional transparency in quantifying the upgrade, the self-citation of prior consensus, and the broad-based organic outperformance make this the highest-conviction upgrade catalyst in the FTSE 100 this reporting season.

scorecards.analysisHtml:
Phase 0 — Routing & FX
  • Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY results accordingly. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.
  • FX: TruFin derives 98% of revenues from the UK (segmental note 4). No non-GBP currency exceeds 30%. No FX penalty applied.
Phase 1 — Data Context
  • Consensus: FY1 EPS 8.0p, revenue £63.0m; FY2 EPS 9.3p, revenue £66.1m. FY1 EBITDA £11.8m. No FY1 PBT consensus available in Sharescope.
  • Forecast momentum: EPS surged 1.9p → 8.0p over ~10 months (+321.1%) with multiple distinct upgrade steps: May (1.9→3.0p), August (3.0→5.0p), September (5.0→5.6p), December (5.6→7.8p), January 2026 (7.8→8.0p). Last 4 weeks: FLAT — consensus plateaued waiting for results.
  • Critical H2 finding: H1 actuals in Sharescope = £36.0m rev / 5.6p EPS. Consensus-implied H2 = £63.0m − £36.0m = £27.0m rev; 8.0p − 5.6p = 2.4p EPS. Actual FY25 H2 (from RNS) = £29.9m rev / 6.4p EPS → H2 EPS beat vs consensus-implied: +167%. This is the central finding of the analysis.
Phase 2 — RNS Extraction & Quantification
  1. Gross revenue: £65.9m, +20% (2024: £55.0m). vs FY1 consensus £63.0m → beat +£2.9m / +4.6%.
    "Gross revenue grew 20% to £65.9m (2024: £55.0m)"
  2. Adjusted EBITDA: £12.6m, +66% (2024: £7.6m). vs FY1 fc £11.8m → beat +£0.8m / +6.8%. 20% revenue growth producing 66% EBITDA growth — exceptional operating leverage in action.
    "Adjusted EBITDA was £12.6m (2024: £7.6m), a 66% year-on-year improvement"
  3. Adjusted PBT: £8.4m (2024: £0.9m), +848%. Step-change in profitability quality — the central investment case validation point.
    "Adjusted Profit Before Tax was £8.4m (2024: PBT of £0.9m), an 848% year-on-year improvement"
  4. Adjusted EPS: 12.0p (basic 11.3p). vs FY1 consensus 8.0p → beat +50%. Complete reset of FY2 estimates required — maintaining 9.3p FY2 is immediately untenable when FY1 delivered 12.0p.
    "Basic EPS: 11.3 pence… Adjusted EPS: 12.0p"
  5. Playstack: revenue £55.3m, +24%. EBITDA £13.5m, +20%. PBT £12.2m, +59%. Exceptional catalogue performance (Abiotic Factor, Balatro). 20m new installs; combined catalogue exceeded $100m lifetime Steam revenues.
    "Playstack grew revenue by more than 24% to £55.3m (2024: £44.6m). EBITDA increased 20% to £13.5m"
  6. Oxygen: revenue £9.1m, +18%. EBITDA £3.8m, +67%. EBIT +383% to £2.1m. Dividend to group £2.5m (2024: £1.3m, +92%). 100% client retention; 65 Early Payment clients; average committed tenure 7.7 years.
    "Oxygen grew revenue by 18% to £9.1m. EBITDA increased 57% to £3.8m (2024: £2.3m)"
  7. Satago: revenue £1.2m, −50%. Net loss £2.6m (2024: £4.8m, −47%). Planned transition from own-book lending. Cost base cut 45%. Loss narrowing — improving trajectory.
    "Satago saw revenues decline by 50% to £1.2m after losing its contract with a Tier-1 Bank in July 2024"
  8. Share buybacks: £8m in 2025 (7.5m shares at avg 106p). Post year-end: further £6m buyback announced January 2026. Third and fourth capital returns since IPO. Share count declining — accretive to remaining holders.
    "Two share buybacks totalling £8m executed during the year acquiring 7.5m shares at an average price of 106p."
  9. Current trading Jan–Feb 2026: "not less than £9.3m" (unaudited). Conservative floor language. Jan–Feb is seasonally lighter for Playstack pre-launches — not a negative signal.
    "Group revenue for the two months ended 28 February 2026 are tracking in line with the Board's expectations at not less than £9.3m (unaudited)"
  10. Oxygen FY26 visibility: "more than 98% of forecast 2026 Early Payment revenue expected from existing clients." Near-full-year cover before any new business — structural moat in revenue predictability.
    "More than 98% of forecast 2026 Early Payment revenue is expected to be generated from existing clients"
  11. Playstack 2026: Mortal Shell II (PC/PS/Xbox), 8 total titles. Board has "immense confidence" in pipeline. Mortal Shell II set wish-list records when announced at Summer Game Fest June 2025.
    "Playstack expects to release 8 titles in 2026 including the hotly anticipated Mortal Shell II and Raccoin"
  12. Deferred tax asset: £7.0m recognised (2024: £3.8m) — £3.2m uplift in year. Auditor/management recognition signals high confidence in sustained future profitability from Oxygen and Playstack. Total unutilised losses without DTA: £51m.
    "Deferred tax assets related to carried-forward tax losses in Oxygen Finance Limited and Playstack Limited have been recognised."
Phase 3 — Historical Benchmarking
  • Revenue trajectory: Strongly Accelerating. FY23: £13.9m, FY24: £55.0m (+296%), FY25: £65.9m (+20%). Growth on a much larger base in FY25 is commercially meaningful — Playstack's model is scaling, not just growing from a tiny starting point.
  • EPS trajectory: Step-change positive. FY23 adj: −11.7p (losses), FY24: 5.4p (first full profit year), FY25: 12.0p (+122%). Operating leverage is real and demonstrated.
  • Critical H2 beat finding: Consensus-implied H2 EPS was only 2.4p (= 8.0p FY − 5.6p H1). Actual H2 delivered 6.4p — +167% beat on implied H2 expectation. The market had severely under-modelled the back-half operating leverage of Playstack's catalogue and Oxygen's EBIT inflection. The full-year +50% EPS beat was essentially an H2 phenomenon.
  • Implied H2 momentum (pre-FY mode): H2 revenue £29.9m vs H2 FY24 £29.7m = +0.7% (flat). H2 EPS 6.4p vs H2 FY24 2.1p = +205% (strong base effect). Revenue flat but EPS strong — reflects operating leverage working as designed, not revenue acceleration.
  • Forecast momentum: +321.1% EPS upgrade — highest in the batch. FLAT last 4 weeks. The 50% EPS beat will require FY2 (currently 9.3p) to be fully reset upward. Direction is unambiguous.
  • Structural flags: (1) Playstack 84% group revenue concentration — single-title risk is real. (2) Oxygen 7.7yr avg client tenure + 100% retention = genuine structural moat. (3) DTA £7m recognition = independent auditor validation of profitability sustainability. (4) Buyback at avg 106p signals board confidence at current 126p price. (5) Satago losses narrowing — optionality, not drag, going forward.

Phase 4 — Broker Reaction Simulation
1#1 Driver — EPS 50% beat vs consensus (12.0p adj vs 8.0p): A complete reset of FY2 estimates is required. TruFin has 1–2 brokers (Panmure Liberum); the note will lead with this beat and the implied FY2 step-up. Maintaining FY2 below 12p would be seen as immediately too conservative.
2#2 Driver — Simultaneous beats across revenue (+4.6%), EBITDA (+6.8%), and PBT (+848%): The beat is not a fluke — it occurred across all metrics simultaneously. Playstack +24% revenue and +59% PBT on a £55m base is exceptional for an AIM games publisher. Oxygen EBIT +383% demonstrates the leverage model working precisely as described.
3Forecast revisions — FY2 EPS reset to 13–16p (from 9.3p = +40–72% upgrade): Revenue FY2 from £66.1m → ~£72–76m. EBITDA from £15.4m → ~£17–20m. Significant revisions executed over 1–3 broker notes post-results.
4Conservative guidance read-through — "not less than £9.3m" for Jan–Feb 2026: Typical small-cap floor language. Jan–Feb below annualised run-rate, but Playstack revenues are highly non-linear around game launches. Mortal Shell II has not yet launched. Brokers will model above this floor for 2026.
5Key risk — Playstack concentration (84% of group): Mortal Shell II commercial reception is unverifiable pre-launch. A single underperforming title or launch delay could knock 15–25% off FY2 estimates. Satago's continued losses (£2.6m) also a drag, though on an improving trajectory.
6Overall tone: Strongly positive / upgrade cycle starting. A 50% EPS beat on a stock that has already had +321% EPS upgrades over 10 months is exceptional. DTA recognition + buyback at 106p avg + Mortal Shell II pipeline = strong upgrading thesis. AIM liquidity constraints may slow broker update timing but direction is unambiguously positive.
Phase 5 — Final Score & Verdict
92
/100
Confidence range: 87–96 · No FX adjustment applied
EPS beat +50% vs consensus (12.0p adj vs 8.0p — full estimate reset required)+22
Revenue beat +4.6%+8
EBITDA beat +6.8%+6
H2 EPS actual 6.4p vs consensus-implied 2.4p (+167% H2 beat)+12
Playstack +24% revenue, PBT +59% — structural proof of repeatable model+7
Oxygen EBITDA +67%, 100% retention, £2.5m dividend to group+6
Ongoing buybacks (£6m post-YE) — capital discipline signal+4
Deferred tax asset £7m recognition (auditor confidence in future profits)+3
Satago still loss-making (£2.6m net loss)−5
Playstack revenue concentration (84% of group — single-title risk)−5
AIM liquidity / limited broker coverage (upgrade lag risk)−3
Jan–Feb guidance "not less than £9.3m" — below implied annualised run-rate−2

TruFin has delivered a remarkable full-year result that materially exceeds all consensus expectations across every metric. The adjusted EPS of 12.0p vs 8.0p consensus (+50%) requires a complete reset of FY2 estimates — maintaining 9.3p FY2 is untenable when FY1 has delivered 12.0p. The critical finding: consensus-implied H2 EPS was only 2.4p (= 8.0p FY − 5.6p H1 known), yet actual H2 delivered 6.4p — a +167% beat on the implied H2 expectation, indicating the market had severely under-modelled the back-half operating leverage of Playstack's catalogue and Oxygen's EBIT inflection.

The quality of the beat is excellent across all subsidiaries. Playstack's +24% revenue and +59% PBT on a £55m base demonstrates repeatable, scalable economics not reliant on a single blockbuster. Oxygen's EBIT +383% confirms the leverage model embedded in the Early Payment SaaS business. The recognition of a £7m deferred tax asset provides independent auditor validation of management's confidence in sustained future profitability.

Primary constraint on a higher score is Playstack concentration (84% of group) and AIM-market limitations on broker coverage. FY2 estimates require upgrades of 40–72% from 9.3p — a protracted process with a small broker team. Direction is unambiguous. Buyback accretion, DTA uplift, and Mortal Shell II launch optionality make TruFin one of the highest-conviction upgrade situations in the small-cap space today.

scorecards.analysisHtml:
PHASE 0A — ROUTING
  • Routing: pre-H1 mode (latest qtrly report = 'Q4'). Interpreting incoming RNS as H1 results (26 weeks to 28 December 2025). Sharescope data reflects pre-RNS state.
PHASE 0B — FX
  • USD exposure is on cost-of-goods side only (Far East sourcing); revenues entirely GBP. No single non-GBP revenue currency exceeds 30%. Phase 0B skipped. USD tailwind on COGS embedded in gross margin bridge (+30bps, +£1.9m).
PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT
  • Routing: pre-H1 mode (Q4). H1 results 26 weeks to 28 Dec 2025.
  • FY1 consensus: EPS 15.2p · Revenue £1,090.6m
  • FY2 consensus: EPS 18.6p · Revenue £1,131.0m
  • Forecast momentum: EPS net change +6.8p (+81.0%) from 8.4p to 15.2p. Two major upgrades: Oct 25 (8.9p → 13.3p, +49%) and Jan 26 (13.2p → 15.2p, +15%). Last-4-week trend: FLAT (15.2p held 7 consecutive weeks). Revenue +£64.5m (+6.3%).
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 49.9% of FY = £544.0m · EPS 33.0% (2yr avg) of FY = 5.0p
  • Prior-year H1 actuals: Revenue £504.5m · EPS 5.3p (underlying)
  • Implied H2 YoY (pre-RNS): Revenue £546.6m (+3.9% vs prior H2) · EPS 10.2p (+175.7% vs prior H2 3.7p)
  • FX: N/A
PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

RNS type: H1 Results (26 weeks ended 28 December 2025)

  1. H1 Revenue — in-line / slight beat: £547.7m vs baseline £544.0m = [+£3.7m / +0.7%] vs seasonal baseline. +8.6% YoY vs prior H1 £504.5m.

"Revenue growth of 8.6% reflecting the growth in order intake and the benefit of a stronger opening order bank"

  1. H1 Underlying EPS — massive beat: 9.8p vs baseline 5.0p = [+4.8p / +96%] vs seasonal baseline. H1 EPS as % of FY1 consensus = 64.5% vs 33.0% historical baseline.

"Underlying basic EPS: 9.8p (H1 FY25: 5.3p)"

  1. H1 PBTu(A) — strong beat: £30.9m vs H1 FY25 £17.0m = [+£13.9m / +81.8% YoY]. H1 alone = 65.1% of FY1 Sharescope consensus PBT £47.5m.

"Underlying profit performance, PBTu(A) up significantly (+£13.9m) YoY to £30.9m reflecting the impact of operational leverage"

  1. FY guidance reiterated — conservative framing: Full year PBTu(A): £43–50m range. Company consensus: £47.3m (within range, near top). Midpoint £46.5m. H1 £30.9m already delivered = 65.3% of company consensus. Implied H2: £12.1m (floor) to £19.1m (ceiling) vs prior H2 £13.8m. Floor requires only −12.3% H2 YoY decline vs prior H2.

"we are comfortable reiterating our guidance of full year PBTu(A) in the range of £43-50m"

  1. Gross margin — approaching target: 57.8% (+110bps YoY). 4th consecutive year of expansion. Bridge: Volume +£24.0m (0bps rate), Product margin +30bps (+£1.4m), FX +30bps (+£1.9m), Freight +50bps (+£2.7m). 30bps below 58% target.

"Gross margin increased 110bps to 57.8%, approaching our 58% target. This is the fourth consecutive year of margin expansion"

  1. Net bank debt — major improvement: £60.6m vs £116.7m H1 FY25 = [−£56.1m / −48.1% YoY]. Leverage 0.8x (1.0x WC-adjusted) — now within 0.5x–1.0x target range. Peak debt was £164.8m at FY24; total reduction of £104.2m over 18 months.

"Strong free cash flow generation and cash discipline reducing net bank debt to £60.6m, down over £100m over the last eighteen months"

  1. Dividend reinstated: Interim dividend 1.0p/share declared. First dividend reinstated after pause. To be paid 29 May 2026.

"Recognising the Group's improved financial position an interim dividend of 1.0 pence / share has been declared"

  1. Order intake: Group +2.3% YoY (DFS +2.0%, Sofology +3.4%) vs +10.1% prior year comparator. Market broadly flat. Home (non-upholstery) +14% YoY. Post-period: softening in footfall linked to adverse weather.

"2.3% YoY order intake growth achieved in a subdued market and against a strong comparator of +10.1%"

  1. Operating leverage: Underlying operating costs 49.1% of revenue (H1 FY25: 49.5%) — improved despite volume, marketing and wage/NIC cost increases. Finance costs £16.7m vs £20.3m (−£3.6m) — lower debt + lower SONIA.

DFS Furniture's H1 FY26 results are emphatically better than consensus had modelled, with the definitive catalyst being the H1 underlying EPS of 9.8p — nearly double the ~5.0p seasonal expectation derived from the 33% historical H1 split, and a deviation of +31.5pp above the seasonal baseline. This single figure forces every broker model to be rebuilt. H1 underlying PBT(A) of £30.9m already represents 65.1% of the Sharescope FY1 PBT consensus of £47.5m — delivered with the less profitable H1 seasonality. Revenue of £547.7m was essentially in-line (+0.3pp above baseline, narrowly missing the +1.5pp buy trigger), confirming the earnings beat is an operational leverage and margin story rather than a volume surprise. Gross margin of 57.8% (+110bps YoY) is the fourth consecutive year of expansion and sits just 30bps below the stated 58% target, with the bridge attributing gains to product margin improvements (+30bps), FX (+30bps) and freight normalisation (+50bps). The H1 print directly confronts the 34% share price sell-off from the 256p peak to 169p that occurred in the 6 weeks prior to today's announcement.

The STRONG BUY signal from H1 EPS tracking (+31.5pp) is structural, not seasonal. The H2 EPS burden is 5.4p (FY1 consensus 15.2p − H1 actual 9.8p) versus the 3-year historical H2 average of 6.9p — the H2 burden is 1.5p lower than the consensus implies, providing meaningful downside protection even if H2 disappoints. The full-year PBT guidance range of £43–50m is deliberately wide: the floor of £43m requires only £12.1m of H2 PBT (−12.3% vs prior H2 £13.8m), while the ceiling of £50m requires £19.1m (+38.4%). Post-period footfall softening linked to adverse weather is the primary risk to the top end of the range, but provides no threat to the floor. The structural driver is the combination of operational leverage (40% revenue-to-profit drop-through on market recovery), four consecutive years of gross margin expansion, finance cost reduction from £56.1m of debt paydown, and the completed £50m Cost-to-Operate programme. Market volumes remain ~20% below pre-pandemic levels — the leverage story is nowhere near peak. The dividend reinstatement (1.0p interim) is a symbolic but important confirmation that management views the balance sheet improvement as durable.

Broker revisions will be material. FY1 EPS (currently 15.2p) is expected to be upgraded to the 17–18p range (+10–20%) as models are rebuilt with H1 actual 9.8p and a conservatively modelled H2. FY1 Revenue is unlikely to move materially (+0–2% to ~£1,095–1,105m). FY2 EPS (currently 18.6p) is expected to be revised to the 20–22p range (+8–18%) as the structural margin and leverage thesis rolls forward. The consensus target price of 256p is expected to be raised to the 270–300p range — and at a current share price of 169p, the stock is trading at a 34% discount to even the unrevised consensus TP, with 51.5% implied upside. The main constraint on the score — and why this is a constructive/moderate upgrade rather than a full re-rating — is the unchanged and deliberately wide guidance range and the post-period footfall softening disclosure. Upgrade cycle probability: high. The H1 EPS beat is the most powerful number DFS has reported since pre-pandemic levels, the balance sheet is the cleanest it has been in years, and the stock is at a 34% discount to a TP that will itself be revised upward today. The weather/footfall caveat and conservative guidance framing are the only governors on a stronger reaction.

scorecards.analysisHtml:
PHASE 0A — ROUTING
  • Routing: pre-FY mode (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as pre-FY trading update (year ending 31 March 2026). Sharescope data reflects pre-RNS state.
PHASE 0B — FX
  • RNS references "currency headwinds" in North America and Latin America. No explicit single-currency percentage disclosed exceeding 30%. No Currency Movements table present. Phase 0B skipped — FX headwind noted qualitatively, no formal penalty applied.
PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT
  • Routing: pre-FY mode (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as pre-FY trading update. Sharescope data reflects pre-RNS state.
  • FY1 consensus: EPS 2.7p · Revenue £83.6m
  • FY2 consensus: EPS 3.1p · Revenue £87.4m
  • Forecast momentum: EPS net change +1.1p (+68.8%), from 1.6p to 2.7p — substantial upgrade cycle. Major step-up Jul–Aug 25 (1.6p → 2.8p), partial reversal Dec 25 (3.0p → 2.6p), recovery to 2.7p. Last-4-week trend: FLAT. Revenue net change +£0.8m (+1.0%).
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 41.7% of FY = £34.8m · EPS: H1 avg split n/a (historically negative H1 EPS)
  • Prior-year H1 actuals: Revenue £33.2m · EPS −3.7p
  • Implied H2 YoY (pre-FY mode): Revenue: FY1 £83.6m − H1 £39.4m = implied H2 £44.2m vs prior H2 £46.4m = [−4.7% YoY] · EPS: FY1 2.7p − H1 (−0.5p) = implied H2 3.2p vs prior H2 5.2p = [−38.5% YoY] (prior H2 5.2p must be read in context — full-year FY25 was only 1.5p due to H1 loss of −3.7p)
  • FX: Qualitative headwind noted; not formally penalised.
PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

RNS type: Pre-FY Trading Update (year ending 31 March 2026)

  1. FY revenue — slight beat: Expected YoY increase of c.8% vs FY25 £79.6m = implied FY26 ~£85.9m. Disclosed consensus: £83.5m. Beat of ~£2.4m (+2.9%). Sharescope FY1 consensus £83.6m: beat of ~£2.3m (+2.7%).

"an expected year-on-year increase in revenue of c.8%, slightly ahead of market expectations (2025: £79.6 million)"

  1. Adjusted EBITDA — materially ahead: "Material increase" over prior year (£7.3m) and "materially ahead" of consensus (£7.6m). Implies EBITDA of approximately £9.0–10.5m (+18–38% vs consensus). No specific figure given.

"The combined effect of the stronger revenue and margins is expected to result in a material increase in adjusted EBITDA over the prior year (2025: £7.3m) with adjusted EBITDA also materially ahead of market expectations"

  1. Gross margin improvement: Structural positive — improved product pricing + cost of goods. Not described as one-off. Durability implications for FY27 base.

"The Company also expects to report improved gross margins for the year, primarily driven by improved product pricing and cost of goods"

  1. EPS (implied): No explicit figure. EBITDA materially ahead + H1 actual −0.5p = implied H2 EPS carries full profit load. Implied FY EPS range ~3.2–4.0p vs consensus 2.7p = potential beat of +19–48%.
  1. Geographic strength: North America and Latin America particularly strong despite currency headwinds and tariff challenges. Implies volume/price gains outweighed FX drag.

"Revenue growth has been particularly strong in North America and Latin America, despite currency headwinds and tariff challenges"

  1. H1 actuals (from Sharescope): H1 revenue £39.4m · H1 EPS −0.5p · H1 EBITDA £3.0m. RNS confirms continued strong trend to year end.
  1. Audit caveat: "Usual audit process, including the customary assessment of balance sheet provisioning." Standard language but explicitly flagged in trading update.

"The final outcome for the full year will be subject to the usual audit process, including the customary assessment of balance sheet provisioning"

  1. Results timing: Audited full year results expected early July 2026.
PHASE 3 — HISTORICAL BENCHMARKING

Half-on-Half Table

H2 FY23: Rev £50.5m / EPS −0.5p

H1 FY24: Rev £38.0m (+8.9%) / EPS −1.9p

1. Half-on-Half Growth Pattern

  • H2 derivation: FY implied ~£85.9m − H1 £39.4m = H2 ~£46.5m
  • Revenue trajectory: 🟢 Accelerating — H2 FY25 −9.7%, H1 FY26 [+18.7%], H2 FY26 (implied) +0.2%. Sharp H1 FY26 reversal from two consecutive declining halves is a strong signal.
  • EPS trajectory: 🟡 Volatile — structurally H2-weighted; H1 improving meaningfully (−3.7p → −0.5p); implied H2 3.2p+ on more normalised trajectory vs the −3.7/+5.2 extreme of FY25.

2. Seasonal H1 Tracking (pre-FY mode — informational)

  • Revenue: H1 actual £39.4m ÷ FY1 consensus £83.6m = 47.1% vs 3yr avg baseline 41.7% → [+5.4pp] → 🟢 STRONG BUY signal fired in H1
  • Buy trigger: H1 Rev > [£34.8m × 1.015] = £35.3m → £39.4m ✓ (by £4.1m)
  • EPS H1 tracking: UNTRACKABLE (H1 avg split n/a due to historically negative H1 EPS)

3. Implied H2 Momentum (pre-FY mode)

  • Implied H2 revenue ~£46.5m vs last 3 H2 avg £49.4m = flat classification (−5 to +5% range; actual +0.2% YoY vs prior H2)
  • EBITDA beat context: if full-year EBITDA £9–10.5m and H1 EBITDA £3.0m, implied H2 EBITDA £6–7.5m — broadly in line with prior H2 £6.9m. Beat is from structural margin improvement flowing through the year, not H2 volume surge.

4. Forecast Momentum Overlay

  • EPS trend: +1.1p (+68.8%) net — major upgrade Jul–Aug 25, partial Dec 25 reversal, recovered to 2.7p. FLAT last 7 weeks — market has not yet reacted to today's beat.
  • Revenue: broadly flat at £83–84m throughout. 2.7% revenue beat vs consensus is modest; EBITDA leverage is the story.
  • Divergence: Price −39.3% (164p → 99.5p) while EPS consensus +68.8% higher. Severe disconnect — today's RNS directly addresses the market's scepticism. High conviction re-rating setup.

5. Structural Flags

  • [H2-loading pattern]: EAH structurally H2-weighted in revenue and profit (pig/poultry seasonal demand). H1 has historically been loss-making at EPS level. H1 FY26 loss narrowing to −0.5p from −3.7p is material structural improvement.
  • [Margin step-change]: Pricing + COGS improvement not described as one-off. If durable, changes FY27 base. "primarily driven by improved product pricing and cost of goods"
  • [Currency headwind in growth markets]: GBP vs USD/LatAm FX ongoing risk. No quantification. Ongoing monitoring required.
  • [Audit/provisioning caveat]: Explicit mention in trading update. Inventory provisioning and receivables can be material in animal health sector. Moderate but real risk.
PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION
  1. #1 and #2 Drivers: #1 = EBITDA "materially ahead" of £7.6m consensus — implies ~£9–10.5m, a +18–38% positive surprise. "Material" in UK small-cap convention signals a genuine deviation, not a rounding difference. Brokers will raise EBITDA and EPS estimates significantly. #2 = Gross margin structural improvement (pricing + COGS) — durability of margin step-up changes the forward earnings base. Brokers modelling EAH on thin margins will need to step up structural assumptions for FY27+.
  1. Forecast revisions: FY1 Revenue: upward ~2–4% to ~£85.9m (from £83.6m). FY1 EPS: significant upgrade expected — from 2.7p to approximately 3.5–5.0p range (+30–85%). FY2 Revenue: upward 2–5% to ~£87–92m. FY2 EPS: current 3.1p likely upgraded to 3.8–5.5p on higher structural margin assumptions.
  1. Target price / recommendation: Current consensus TP 157p vs close 99.5p (58% upside). Material EBITDA beat likely drives TP upgrades toward 180–220p range. Some Hold → Buy upgrades probable. Stock 40% below peak despite improving fundamentals makes this high-conviction for momentum-focused brokers.
  1. Conservative guidance read-through: "Materially ahead" is the opposite of conservative guidance — this is strong positive signal language. Company is setting market expectations above consensus. Classic upgrade cycle language; increases probability of sustained re-rating.
  1. Key risk: Audit provisioning caveat is the primary risk. "Customary assessment of balance sheet provisioning" explicitly opens the door to balance sheet adjustments that could reduce reported profitability vs trading update. In animal health, inventory provisioning and receivables can be material. "The final outcome for the full year will be subject to the usual audit process, including the customary assessment of balance sheet provisioning"
  1. Overall tone: Strongly positive / upgrade cycle starting — "materially ahead" EBITDA, structural margin improvement, 40% share price discount to pre-upgrade level, 58% discount to consensus TP. Textbook re-rating setup.
Phase 5 — Final Score & Verdict
81
/100
Confidence range: 74–88 · No FX adjustment (headwind noted qualitatively)
EBITDA materially ahead of consensus (+18–38% implied)+22
Revenue beat vs consensus (~+2.7%, c.8% YoY growth)+10
Structural gross margin improvement (pricing + COGS)+12
H1 revenue tracking +5.4pp above seasonal baseline (STRONG BUY trigger fired)+10
Strong upgrade momentum in consensus (+68.8% EPS net change)+8
North America + Latin America growth despite FX headwinds+5
Net cash position (ND/EBITDA −2.8x) — strong balance sheet+5
Audit/provisioning caveat — risk of modest pullback on finalisation−8
FX headwind in key growth markets (qualitative, unquantified)−6
H2 revenue implied flat YoY (+0.2%) — revenue momentum limited−4
Share price −40% from peak — negative sentiment partially baked in−3
EPS H1 avg split n/a; small data gaps on EPS tracking−2

ECO Animal Health's pre-FY trading update for the year ending 31 March 2026 delivers a clear and decisive beat on the most watched metric. Full-year revenue is expected to grow approximately 8% YoY from £79.6m to approximately £85.9m, versus the disclosed consensus of £83.5m — a beat of approximately £2.4m (+2.9%). Against the Sharescope FY1 consensus of £83.6m, the beat is nearly identical. More significantly, adjusted EBITDA is guided to be "materially ahead of market expectations" against a consensus of £7.6m — language that in UK small-cap convention implies outperformance of ≥15–20%, pointing to an implied EBITDA figure of approximately £9.0–10.5m. The #1 metric driving broker reaction will be this EBITDA beat, which represents a 18–38% positive surprise against a consensus that was itself already above the prior year (£7.6m vs £7.3m FY25 actual). This is not a modest beat — this is a material positive step-change in profitability.

In pre-FY mode, the H1 tracking signal (informational) confirms the strength visible in the FY guidance: H1 revenue of £39.4m represented 47.1% of the FY1 consensus, against a 3-year average seasonal baseline of 41.7% — a deviation of +5.4pp which clears the STRONG BUY threshold with significant margin. The buy trigger fired (H1 Rev £39.4m >> trigger of £35.3m by £4.1m). The structural driver behind the beat is gross margin improvement from pricing discipline and cost-of-goods reduction — not a one-off mix effect. This matters for durability: if the margin step-up is structural, FY27 estimates are too low. The implied H2 revenue of approximately £46.5m is broadly flat YoY (+0.2%), confirming the beat is entirely a margin and H1-momentum story rather than H2 volume. The balance sheet is a further positive — net cash (ND/EBITDA −2.8x) removes any financial leverage risk. The audit provisioning caveat is the single material downside risk that constrains the score below 90.

Broker revisions will be significant. FY1 EPS is expected to be upgraded from the current 2.7p consensus to approximately 3.5–5.0p — a +30–85% revision, with the wide range reflecting uncertainty in the EBITDA-to-EPS walk and the provisioning caveat. FY1 Revenue upgrades will be modest: approximately £83.6m → £85.9m (+2.7%). FY2 EPS (currently 3.1p) is likely upgraded to the 3.8–5.5p range as brokers roll forward the higher structural margin base. The consensus target price of 157p is expected to be raised materially — likely into the 180–220p range by the most constructive brokers — while the stock at 99.5p represents a 58% discount to current consensus TP and would still sit at a 45–55% discount even to the upgraded TP range. Upgrade cycle probability: high. The combination of "materially ahead" EBITDA language, structural margin improvement, a 40% share price decline from peak, and a 58% discount to even the unrevised consensus TP creates a textbook upgrade cycle setup. The July results presentation will be the confirmation catalyst.
