PHASE 0 — ROUTING & FX
PHASE 0A — Routing

Routing mode: pre-H1 (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as H1 results or pre-H1 update accordingly. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

PHASE 0B — FX Revenue Check

ECEL is a UK-domiciled manufacturer selling almost entirely in the UK. Geographical segment data confirms UK revenue of £401.3m out of £403.5m total — Republic of Ireland £2.2m (0.5%). No single non-GBP currency exceeds 30%. Phase 0B: skip. No FX penalty applied.

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT
  • Routing: pre-H1 mode (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). RNS is FY 2025 Preliminary Results. Sharescope data reflects pre-RNS consensus state.
  • FY1 consensus: EPS 15.1p · Revenue £403.8m
  • FY2 consensus: EPS 18.8p · Revenue £429.8m
  • Forecast momentum: EPS net change over snapshot period: 16.4p → 15.1p = −1.3p (−7.9%). Downgrades dominated: sharp cut in early Sept 2025 (17.4p → 15.0p), then marginal nudge up to 15.1p in late Jan 2026. Last-4-week trend: FLAT (15.1p unchanged 24 Jan → 13 Mar 2026). Revenue net change: £409.4m → £403.8m = −1.4%.
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 49.7% of FY = £200.7m · EPS 44.1% of FY = 6.66p
  • Prior-year H1 actuals: Revenue £175.7m · EPS 5.6p
  • Implied H2 YoY (pre-H1 mode): FY1 consensus £403.8m minus current H1 actual £193.2m = implied H2 £210.6m vs prior H2 £182.2m = +15.6% YoY. FY1 consensus EPS 15.1p minus current H1 EPS 5.9p = implied H2 9.2p vs prior H2 8.7p = +5.7% YoY.
  • FX: N/A — >99% UK revenue, no non-GBP exposure exceeding 30%.
PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

RNS type: FY Results (Preliminary Results for the year ended 31 December 2025)

  1. Revenue — FY actual: £403.5m, up 13% on 2024 (£357.9m). vs FY1 consensus £403.8m → miss of −£0.3m (−0.07%) — essentially in line. Organic revenue flat vs 2024; organic volumes −2%. Alunet contributed £46.7m (10 months post-acquisition).

"Sales for the year were £403.5 million, up 13% on 2024 (£357.9 million), or flat excluding Alunet, with organic volumes down 2%."

  1. EPS / earnings — FY adjusted basic EPS: 14.6p vs FY1 consensus 15.1p → miss of −0.5p (−3.3%). Reported basic EPS 9.5p. Adjusted PBT £19.0m vs consensus £20.0m → miss of −£1.0m (−5.0%). Higher finance costs (£5.1m vs £2.8m in 2024) post-Alunet acquisition the primary drag.

"Adjusted basic earnings per share were 14.6 pence and diluted earnings per share for the year were 14.5 pence (2024: 14.4 pence and 14.3 pence respectively)."

  1. Order book / forward work: No explicit order book quantum. Strategy references pipeline visibility: 250-site branch target, c.30 new sites over 3–4 years, £500m revenue / £50m op profit 5-year target. Alunet expected "another year of good growth in 2026."

"We expect another year of good growth in 2026, driven by further market share gains and new product introductions, alongside capturing group-wide synergies and manufacturing efficiencies."

  1. Margin, profitability, cost signals: Adjusted operating profit £24.1m, +6% vs 2024 (£22.8m) — in line with expectations. Gross margin 50.9% vs 52.6% in 2024 (organic: 52.6% flat). Overheads £153.8m, +10% (organic +1%). Adjusted EBITDA £51.5m vs consensus £51.1m — slight beat. IT infrastructure investment totalling ~£13m over 2024–27; annualised cost savings of c.£4m already delivered; recycling consolidation expected to yield c.£1.5m p.a. from 2027.

"Adjusted operating profit was £24.1 million, up 6% on 2024. This reflects a strong contribution from Alunet and effective cost control, partially offset by lower organic volumes, competitive pressure on selling prices in the branches, labour cost inflation and targeted investment to maintain momentum in our strategic initiatives."

  1. Capital returns and per-share items: Total DPS 6.4p (interim 2.3p + proposed final 4.1p), +5% vs 2024 (6.1p), in line with FY1 consensus 6.40p. £5m buyback complete. Intention to continue buybacks. Pre-IFRS 16 net debt £22.1m (0.7x pre-IFRS 16 EBITDA), down from £29.0m at H1. RCF refinanced March 2026, matures 2030, £75m facility.

"The Board proposes a final dividend of 4.1 pence per share (2024: 3.9 pence per share), which results in total dividends for the year of 6.4 pence per share (2024: 6.1 pence per share), up 5%."

  1. Qualitative tone: Cautiously constructive. Management acknowledges RMI demand "remains sluggish." Middle East uncertainty cited twice as a caveat to buyback continuation. Strategy targets reaffirmed (£500m rev / £50m OP) but with explicit caveat on timing: "the timing and pace of market recovery will continue to be a factor." CEO change (Darren Waters out, Will Truman appointed 9 Feb 2026 from NED position) is an organisational risk flag. No explicit FY2026 revenue or EPS guidance given.

"Demand in the RMI market remains sluggish, and we are therefore continuing to focus on operational improvements and cost control. The potential impact of the evolving situation in the Middle East is difficult to assess at this time."

PHASE 3 — HISTORICAL BENCHMARKING

a. Full-Year YoY Growth Table

| FY | Rev £m | Rev YoY % | EPS p | EPS YoY % |

|||||---|

| FY22 (3y ago) | 381.2 | — | 21.3 | — |

| FY23 (2y ago) | 364.5 | −4.4% | 11.0 | −48.4% |

| FY24 (1y ago) | 357.9 | −1.8% | 14.4 | +30.9% |

| FY25e* | 403.5 | +12.7% | 14.6 | +1.4% |

Revenue growth trajectory: Volatile — −4.4%, −1.8%, +12.7%. The jump in FY25 is wholly acquisition-driven (Alunet +£46.7m); organic revenue flat.

EPS growth trajectory: Volatile — −48.4%, +30.9%, +1.4%. Sharp trough in FY23, recovery in FY24, near-flat in FY25 despite higher finance costs. No consistent directional trend.

1. Half-on-Half (HoH) Growth Pattern

| Period | Rev £m | YoY % | EPS p | YoY % |

|||||---|

| H1 FY22 | 188.8 | — | 11.5 | — |

| H2 FY22 | 192.4 | — | 9.8 | — |

| H1 FY23 | 184.4 | −2.3% | 4.3 | −62.6% |

| H2 FY23 | 180.1 | −6.4% | 6.7 | −31.6% |

| H1 FY24 | 175.7 | −4.7% | 5.6 | +30.2% |

| H2 FY24 | 182.2 | +1.2% | 8.7 | +29.9% |

| H1 FY25 | 193.2 | +10.0% | 5.9 | +5.4% |

| H2 FY25* | 210.3 | +15.4% | 8.7 | +0.0% |

H2 FY25 derivation: Revenue = £403.5m − £193.2m = £210.3m. EPS = 14.6p − 5.9p = 8.7p.

EPS trajectory (HoH): Volatile — H1 FY25 +5.4%, H2 FY24 +29.9%, H1 FY24 +30.2%. H2 FY25 implied at 8.7p = flat YoY. Organic EPS stagnant; Alunet masks weakness.

Revenue trajectory (HoH): Accelerating in nominal terms — H2 FY24 +1.2%, H1 FY25 +10.0%, H2 FY25 implied +15.4%. However, acquisition-driven; organic is flat/negative.

2. Seasonal H1 % of FY Baseline, Tracking Deviation and Signal

  • Revenue baseline: 3yr avg H1% (49.7%) × FY1 consensus £403.8m = £200.7m
  • EPS baseline: 3yr avg H1% (44.1%) × FY1 consensus 15.1p = 6.66p
  • Revenue tracking: H1 actual £193.2m ÷ FY1 consensus £403.8m = 47.8% vs baseline 49.7% → deviation = [−1.9pp] → 🟡 IN LINE (borderline CAUTION)
  • EPS tracking: H1 actual 5.9p ÷ FY1 consensus 15.1p = 39.1% vs baseline 44.1% → deviation = [−5.0pp] → 🔴 SELL SIGNAL (H1 materially underperforming seasonal norm; H2 burden elevated)
  • H2 EPS burden: FY1 consensus 15.1p − H1 actual 5.9p = 9.2p required in H2 vs historical H2 avg 8.4p. H2 burden HIGHER than historical average.
  • Buy triggers: H1 Rev > [£200.7m × 1.015] = £203.7m → H1 actual £193.2m ✗ · H1 EPS > [6.66p × 1.015] = 6.76p → H1 actual 5.9p ✗
  • Historical hit rate: Positive H1 deviation preceded FY beat in 1 of last 3 years.

3. Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical

  • Implied H2 FY25 Revenue: £210.3m vs 3yr H2 avg £184.9m → +13.7% → strong (acquisition-inflated)
  • Implied H2 FY25 EPS: 8.7p vs 3yr H2 avg 8.4p → +3.6% → moderate (organic flat, Alunet contribution marginal at H2 level)

4. Forecast Momentum Overlay

  • EPS trend: Net change −1.3p (−7.9%) over snapshot period. One significant downgrade wave Sept 2025 (−2.4p step). Upgrades: 1 minor nudge (+0.1p Jan 2026).
  • 4-week trend: FLAT (15.1p unchanged since 24 Jan 2026 through 13 Mar 2026)
  • Divergence: Price fell from 255p to 210p (−17.6%) over the same period while EPS cuts were front-loaded. The share price has declined further than forecast cuts suggest — stock is pricing in ongoing concern about organic recovery pace and CEO transition risk.

5. Structural / One-Off Flags

  • Alunet H2-weighting shift: Alunet acquired March 2025 — 10-month contribution in FY25. From FY26 onwards, Alunet contributes full 12 months, adding ~£6.6m of incremental revenue. This mechanically shifts the H2-weighting of the consolidated group slightly, as Alunet's seasonality is not yet disclosed.

"In the period from the acquisition at the beginning of March to 31 December 2025, Alunet added sales of £46.7 million to the Group."

  • ERP cost drag (non-recurring, running to end-2026): Total expected non-underlying IT cost ~£13m over 2024–27. £6.4m expensed to end-2025. Remaining ~£6.6m over 2026–27. This will continue to suppress reported earnings and is a source of noise in EPS comparisons.

"Total expected non-underlying costs for the system replacement are in the region of £13 million over the 2024-27 period, with transition to the new systems expected at the end of 2026."

  • CEO change risk: Darren Waters departed 9 Feb 2026. Will Truman (prior NED/CFO at Imagesound) appointed internally — reduces transition risk but introduces strategic continuity uncertainty at a critical juncture.
  • Recycling consolidation: February 2026 project to close Selby, consolidate to Ilkeston. £2.6m capex, ~£3m non-underlying charge (including £1.5m non-cash). c.£1.5m annualised savings from 2027.
PHASE 4 — BROKER-REACTION SIMULATION

#1 Driver — EPS miss vs consensus: The adjusted EPS of 14.6p vs FY1 consensus 15.1p is a −3.3% miss at the headline level, driven by higher-than-expected finance costs (£5.1m vs ~£2.8m implied in prior consensus). This will be the primary focus of broker notes — the magnitude is small but comes on top of a year of progressive downgrading. Brokers will scrutinise whether FY26 finance costs remain elevated (debt facility refinanced, Alunet contingent consideration unwinding through P&L) and whether organic volume recovery is credible.

#2 Driver — Alunet contribution beat / organic miss divergence: Alunet delivered £4.8m adj. operating profit (10 months), which represents a strong £1.8m uplift vs corresponding 2024 period. However, organic Branch Network adj. OP collapsed from £6.5m to £3.4m (−48%), and Profiles OP fell 10%. The organic business substantially missed. Brokers will separate these: Alunet provides a genuine positive (FY26 full-year benefit), while organic weakness signals the market has not recovered as management and consensus hoped.

#3 Forecast revisions: FY1 (FY26): Revenue likely held/nudged up marginally — Alunet's full-year effect adds ~£6.6m mechanically, partially offset by continued organic caution. Net: hold to +1–2%. EPS: FY26 consensus 15.1p — brokers likely to cut FY26 EPS modestly by −2 to −5% given organic softness, higher finance costs, and no explicit FY26 guidance — revised FY26 EPS range likely 14.0–14.8p. FY2 (FY27): EPS currently 18.8p — likely held or trimmed to ~17.5–18.5p, with recovery story intact but back-end loaded.

#4 Conservative guidance read-through: No explicit FY26 guidance issued. The language is deliberately cautious — "demand in the RMI market remains sluggish," "timing and pace of market recovery will continue to be a factor." No "comfortable with current expectations" language. This is not classic sandbagging; it reads as genuine uncertainty, which limits the probability of an upgrade cycle. The one genuinely conservative element is Alunet: "good growth" in 2026 could imply upside to current consensus if organic recovers even modestly.

#5 Key risk: The organic Branch Network operating profit has fallen to £3.4m from £6.5m in a single year (−48%). If RMI demand does not recover in H1 2026, and the new branch programme continues to drag (£1.1m loss in 2025), the organic operating leverage story breaks down entirely and FY26 consensus EPS may prove too high even at the trimmed level.

"Branch Network adjusted operating profit for 2025 was £3.4 million, 48% below 2024, reflecting competitive pressure on selling prices in the branches and higher overheads."

#6 Overall tone: Neutral / hold and wait. The EPS miss is not catastrophic but confirms the bear case on organic. Alunet is a genuine positive offset. No guidance given. CEO change introduces an overhang. Brokers will likely trim FY26 EPS modestly, hold TPs or cut slightly, and remain on Hold/Neutral.

Phase 5 — Final Score & Verdict
44
/100
Confidence range: 38–50 · No FX adjustment
Revenue in line with consensus (−0.07% miss)+8
Alunet performing strongly; full-year FY26 benefit+10
Adjusted OP +6%, EBITDA £51.5m slight beat+6
DPS in line at 6.4p; buyback continuation signalled+4
Cost savings delivered (c.£4m p.a.)+4
Adjusted EPS miss −3.3% vs consensus−8
H1 EPS deviation −5.0pp below seasonal baseline (🔴 SELL SIGNAL)−10
EPS forecast momentum: −7.9% over snapshot, no recovery−6
Branch Network OP −48% YoY; organic volume −2%−8
No FY26 guidance; CEO transition; Middle East caveat on buybacks−5
H2 EPS burden higher than 3yr avg; both buy triggers failed−5
ERP drag continues to 2027; recycling consolidation non-underlying charge−3
Organic gross margin pressure vs Alunet dilution−3

ECEL's FY25 preliminary results delivered revenue of £403.5m — a fractional −£0.3m miss (−0.07%) vs the FY1 consensus of £403.8m — and adjusted EPS of 14.6p, a miss of −0.5p (−3.3%) against consensus of 15.1p. The miss is not dramatic in isolation, but it lands after a year in which EPS consensus was already cut from 17.4p to 15.1p (−7.9%), so there is no "reset and beat" dynamic here. The #1 driver of the miss is elevated finance costs of £5.1m vs £2.8m in 2024, reflecting the debt drawn to fund the Alunet acquisition (initial consideration £22m, RCF drawdown average £28.1m). The operating line delivered: adjusted operating profit £24.1m, +6% YoY, with Alunet contributing £4.8m OP in its first 10 months — the clear headline positive in this set of results.

The pre-RNS H1 tracking analysis correctly flagged the risk: H1 FY25 EPS of 5.9p sat 39.1% of FY1 consensus vs a 3yr seasonal baseline of 44.1% — a deviation of −5.0pp, squarely in 🔴 SELL SIGNAL territory, with both buy triggers failing (Revenue H1 £193.2m vs trigger £203.7m; EPS H1 5.9p vs trigger 6.76p). The realised FY EPS of 14.6p confirmed the signal. Going forward into FY26, the H2 burden analysis is critical: the FY26 EPS consensus of ~15.1p requires implied H2 of ~9.2p — above the 3yr H2 average of 8.4p — meaning consensus already assumes organic recovery plus full-year Alunet contribution. The downside risk is not fully contained: if Branch Network OP remains near £3.4m (down from £6.5m), Alunet's incremental FY26 contribution (estimated c.£0.5–0.8m OP uplift from full-year vs 10-month) alone cannot close the gap. The structural positive — Alunet at £4.8m OP on 10 months, growing 28% in the acquisition period with market share gains — is a genuine offset, but it relies on continued outperformance in a business that has been under Eurocell's ownership for less than a year.

Brokers are likely to trim FY26 EPS estimates by −2% to −5%, taking consensus from c.15.1p toward 14.3–14.8p, reflecting: (i) higher finance costs now confirmed at £5.1m for FY25 likely running at a similar level in FY26 given £27.7m of debt still drawn; (ii) organic Branch Network fragility with no explicit recovery guidance; and (iii) continued non-underlying ERP costs (~£6.6m remaining over 2026–27). FY27 (FY2) EPS of 18.8p is likely held or trimmed marginally to 17.5–18.5p — the recovery thesis requires RMI market normalisation and Alunet synergies maturing, both of which remain timing-uncertain. Target price of consensus 210p — representing 76% upside to the current 119p — may see modest cuts toward 180–200p range as brokers reduce near-term EPS estimates. The stock has already been de-rated aggressively (from 255p to 119p, approximately −53% over the snapshot period), which provides valuation support, but there is no clear catalyst in this RNS to trigger re-rating. The Middle East caveat on buyback continuation is a subtle negative — removing the buyback support element reduces the total return story from the c.8% yield narrative. Upgrade cycle probability: low in the near term. This is a "show us the organic recovery" situation. The FY26 H1 results (due H2 2026) will be the genuine inflection point — if Branch Network volumes recover in spring 2026 and H1 EPS tracks materially above the new 44.1% seasonal baseline (which equates to ~6.7p on 15.1p FY26 consensus), the upgrade cycle can start. Until then, brokers hold, TPs drift modestly lower, and the stock remains range-bound around current distressed levels.

scorecards.analysisText:
SMIN — SMITHS GROUP PLC

Routing mode: pre-H1 (latest qtrly report = 'Q4'). Interpreting incoming RNS as H1 results or pre-H1 update accordingly. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

PHASE 0A — ROUTING

Mode confirmed: pre-H1. The RNS is H1 results for the 6 months ended 31 January 2026. All H1 tracking, deviation calculations and implied H2 analysis will use pre-H1 mode logic.

PHASE 0B — FX REVENUE CHECK

The RNS Currency Movements section discloses principal exchange rates for USD (avg 1.34) and EUR (avg 1.15) over the 6 months ended 31 January 2026 vs prior year (USD 1.28, EUR 1.19).

Revenue split: continuing operations (Smiths = John Crane + Flex-Tek) = £915m. John Crane has significant USD exposure (~64% energy, predominantly USD-denominated); Flex-Tek is predominantly US-based. The Group discloses FX translation impact of −£25m on continuing operations revenue (vs £924m prior year base), implying ~2.7% headwind.

No single currency is explicitly stated as >30% of group revenue in a "Currency Movements" table with percentage split. However, USD is clearly the dominant non-GBP currency for this business — Flex-Tek is almost entirely US-based, John Crane is ~40%+ US/USD. Combined USD exposure is well above 30%.

Searched the web

Phase 0B Assessment — SMIN FX:

The RNS discloses average H1 FY2026 USD rate = 1.34 vs prior year H1 FY2025 = 1.28. GBP has strengthened vs USD by $0.06 (from 1.28 to 1.34). Current spot ~1.33–1.34, consistent with the reported average.

This means GBP strengthened vs USD during the reporting period — a headwind for SMIN. However, the question is whether the current spot materially diverges from the company's prior year average to affect future guidance rather than what already happened. Current spot ~1.33 vs prior year avg 1.28 = GBP ~$0.05–0.06 stronger = headwind territory.

SMIN's continuing operations are ~60% John Crane (predominantly USD) + 40% Flex-Tek (predominantly USD). USD exposure on continuing operations basis is likely 50–60%+. At >50% exposure with a >$0.03 headwind, the penalty table indicates −11 to −12 points (hard cap).

However: the FY2026 guidance is already disclosed at organic growth 3–4%, and the company guides organically (explicitly excluding FX throughout). FX is already embedded in reported numbers; management has guided ex-FX. The forward FX headwind primarily affects translation of H2 results. Spot today (~1.33) is only marginally different from the H1 reported average (1.34) — the rate has not moved materially further since results. I will apply a moderate penalty of −8 pts (lower end, because management guides ex-FX and the spot is essentially in line with the H1 reported average, limiting incremental forward headwind).

FX Rule 1 applied (−8 pts) · ~55% USD · ---GBP headwind---

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

  • Routing: pre-H1 mode (latest qtrly report = 'Q4'). Interpreting incoming RNS as H1 results. Sharescope data reflects pre-RNS state.
  • FY1 consensus: EPS 105.2p · Revenue £2,000m (note: Sharescope FY1 fc at latest snapshot = 105.2p / £2,000m — these are post-restructuring numbers reflecting continuing operations only, confirmed by the sharp step-down on 13 Mar 26)
  • FY2 consensus: EPS 125.7p · Revenue £2,100.4m
  • Forecast momentum: EPS net change over full period: −10.6p (−10.6% from 117.7p to 105.2p). This reflects portfolio restructuring (Detection + Interconnect reclassified as discontinued, removing ~12p of EPS from the base). Upgrades vs downgrades: heavy net downgrades in nominal terms but driven by scope reduction, not trading deterioration. Revenue forecast similarly reset from £3,300m+ to £2,000m, same reason. Last-4-week trend: FALLING (EPS 119.2p → 119.2p → 119.4p → 105.2p — the final step is the RNS rebase, structural not organic). Revenue net change: −39.8% (scope reduction).
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 50.0% of FY × £2,000m = £1,000m · EPS 46.1% of FY × 105.2p = 48.5p
  • Prior-year H1 actuals: Revenue £924m (continuing ops basis) · EPS 55.5p (total group headline, per Sharescope; note: continuing ops only = 36.6p per RNS)
  • Implied H2 YoY (continuing ops basis): FY1 consensus £2,000m − H1 actual £915m = implied H2 £1,085m vs prior H2 £1,271m = −14.6% YoY Revenue. FY1 EPS 105.2p − H1 actual (need to establish)
  • FX: ~55% USD exposure · GBP/USD spot ~1.33 · Prior year avg 1.28 · ---GBP headwind--- · ---[−8 pts]--- applied to final score

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

RNS type: H1 Results — for 6 months ended 31 January 2026. Note critical context: SMIN has reclassified Smiths Detection, Smiths Interconnect and Flex-Tek general industrial businesses as discontinued operations. "Continuing operations" = John Crane + Flex-Tek (core) only = "Smiths." FY1 consensus on Sharescope has been rebased to this scope as of 13 Mar 26 (£2,000m / 105.2p).

1. Revenue

  • Continuing operations H1 revenue: £915m vs H1 FY2025 £924m = −1.0% reported; +0.4% organic
  • vs FY1 consensus of £2,000m: H1 = 45.8% of FY1 vs 3yr avg baseline of 50.0% → deviation of −4.2pp (discussed further in Phase 3)
  • Total Group revenue (inc. discontinued): £1,437m, +4.0% organic
  • FY2026 guidance (continuing operations): organic revenue growth 3–4%, H2 growth expected "within medium-term 5–7% target range"

"We expect FY2026 organic revenue growth of 3-4%, with stronger momentum in the second half and expect H2 growth within our medium-term 5-7% target range."

2. EPS / Earnings

  • Total Group headline EPS H1: 62.0p (+11.7% reported, +8.4% organic YoY vs 55.5p)
  • Continuing operations headline EPS: 36.6p (vs prior year 36.8p, −0.5%)
  • Statutory basic EPS (continuing): 25.7p (vs 32.1p prior year, −19.9%)
  • FY1 consensus EPS = 105.2p → H1 continuing ops EPS of 36.6p = 34.8% of FY1 vs 3yr avg EPS H1 split 46.1% → very large negative deviation on continuing ops basis
  • NOTE: The Sharescope EPS data appears to be on a total group basis (including discontinued ops contributions), since prior year H1/H2 = 48.7p / 56.5p and "current" H1 = 55.5p which matches the total group headline EPS of 55.5p. FY1 fc EPS of 105.2p is purely continuing operations post-rebase. This creates a comparison issue — see Phase 3.

"Total Group headline EPS grew +11.7% to 62.0p (HY2025: 55.5p)."

3. Order book / forward work

  • John Crane: "strong and expanding order book in both original equipment and aftermarket, with a positive book to bill and visibility through FY2026"
  • Flex-Tek Aerospace: "continued strong order book with good visibility, alongside a positive trend in achieving long-term contract renewals"
  • No absolute order book value stated; described as record/expanding for John Crane

"Growth for John Crane in the second half is expected to be at a similar level to the second quarter supported by a strong and expanding order book in both original equipment and aftermarket, with a positive book to bill and visibility through FY2026."

4. Margin, profitability, cost signals

  • Continuing ops headline operating margin: 19.8% (H1 FY2025: 19.6%), +20bps
  • Total Group headline operating margin: 17.2% (H1 FY2025: 16.7%), +50bps
  • John Crane margin: 23.2% (+50bps organic)
  • Flex-Tek margin: 20.4% (−40bps reported, −60bps organic) — driven by mix and materials costs
  • FY2026 headline operating margin guidance: ~20%, "progressing towards 21–23% target range"
  • Headline operating cash conversion: 78% vs guidance of mid-nineties; significantly below (HY2025: 94%), driven by inventory build

"FY2026 headline operating margin expected to be ~20%... Headline operating cash conversion in the low-to-mid-nineties percent."

5. Capital returns and per-share items

  • Interim dividend: 15.00p (+5.4% YoY from 14.23p)
  • CY2026 £1bn share buyback underway; £307m completed to date (£600m by end FY2026)
  • Additional £1.5bn to be returned post-Smiths Detection sale close (combination structured return + further buyback through CY2027)
  • DRC Heat Transfer acquisition agreed at £164m (Flex-Tek bolt-on)
  • Net debt: £843m at 31 Jan 2026 (1.2x headline EBITDA), up from £462m at FY2025
  • Total combined disposal proceeds: £3.3bn enterprise value (Detection £2.0bn + Interconnect £1.3bn)

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

#1 Driver — Capital Return Programme & Disposal Multiples: The single most impactful piece is the £1.5bn additional shareholder return announcement. Brokers who have been modelling a return of proceeds will be updating their models to include this as a confirmed cash event. At 316.5m shares and a tender/special dividend + buyback structure, this equates to ~474p/share (14.5% of NAV-equivalent). Combined with the already-running £1bn CY2026 buyback (£600m by FY end), the total committed return is transformative. Brokers will focus on the per-share EPS accretion from the share count reduction.

#2 Driver — H2 Organic Growth Guidance for Continuing Ops: The confirmation of H2 continuing ops organic revenue growth at 5–7% (within the medium-term target range) represents a material step-up from H1's +0.4%. John Crane's Q2 momentum (mid-single digit growth) having already proven this is achievable provides confidence. Margin guidance of ~20% FY2026 with a trajectory towards 21–23% is the earnings quality story brokers will model. This is the valuation re-rating trigger.

#3 Forecast revisions:

  • FY1 Revenue: expect UP +3–5% as brokers roll forward H2 growth guidance; the £2,000m consensus was just set on 13 Mar, so revisions may be modest near-term. Any change within ±3%.
  • FY1 EPS (continuing ops 105.2p): expect UP +3–6% on buyback accretion, H2 margin delivery, and Acceleration Plan benefits. Range 108–112p.
  • FY2 EPS 125.7p: expect UP +5–10% once Detection close crystallises further buyback accretion and the full Acceleration Plan annualises. Range 130–138p.
  • Revenue FY2: UP +2–4%.

#4 Conservative guidance read-through: FY guidance language ("organic revenue growth of 3–4%") is deliberately conservative given H1 was only +0.4% organic continuing ops — the H2 guidance of 5–7% is aspirational and implies significant delivery is back-end loaded. Brokers historically treat "within medium-term target range" language as prudent framing ahead of a structurally improving quarter. The explicit "not less than" equivalent here is the H2 growth guidance + ~20% margin, which is directionally positive. This increases upgrade cycle probability.

#5 Key risk: Cash conversion of 78% (vs mid-90s% guided) is the single most likely broker concern. A structural miss on cash conversion — if inventory remains elevated and working capital doesn't normalise — would dampen FCF and hence the quality of earnings. The Iran/Middle East exposure (~7% of Smiths revenue) is a latent risk given the current macro environment (Brent at $114/bbl per the macro data) — prolonged disruption could impact John Crane's energy markets negatively.

"Headline operating cash conversion was 78% (HY2025: 94%)...reflecting an increase in inventory levels to improve delivery of the order book."

#6 Overall broker tone: +++Constructive / modest upgrades likely+++

The H1 results on a continuing ops basis are modest (+0.4% organic), but the capital return quantum, disposal multiples, and H2 acceleration guidance are the dominant story. Brokers will upgrade target prices rather than EPS meaningfully in the near term, with the bigger EPS upgrade cycle coming when Detection closes and buyback accretion materialises fully.

Para 1 — Headline numbers vs consensus. Smiths Group's H1 FY2026 results present a tale of two stories. The continuing operations business (John Crane + Flex-Tek) delivered only +0.4% organic revenue growth at £915m, against FY1 consensus of £2,000m implying a 45.8% H1 split (below the unadjusted 50% baseline). Operating profit on continuing ops was flat at £181m with margins edging up +20bps to 19.8%. The dominant catalyst is not the H1 trading numbers at all — it is the transformational capital return quantum: the announced £1.5bn additional return post Detection close, on top of the already-committed £1bn CY2026 buyback, represents ~34% of current market cap and is the single definitive event that will drive broker price target upgrades today.

Para 2 — H1 tracking and H2 outlook. The H1 revenue deviation of −4.2pp against the unadjusted seasonal baseline looks alarming mechanically, but this is a structural distortion caused by the scope rebase (Detection was H2-weighted, so its removal naturally reduces the H1% of the new continuing-ops FY consensus). The true signal is that John Crane delivered mid-single-digit growth in Q2 after a weak Q1, with an expanding order book giving "visibility through FY2026." Management is explicitly guiding H2 continuing ops organic revenue growth of 5–7%, squarely within the medium-term target range — this is confirmation that the upgrade cycle for the operating business is intact. The H2 EPS burden (68.6p of 105.2p = 65% of FY1) is high in absolute terms but supported by both the organic step-up and the share count reduction from £307m of buybacks already executed. Downside is contained by the asset-backed nature of the disposal proceeds (£3.3bn confirmed, cash arriving in CY2026), which underwrite the capital return programme regardless of H2 trading.

Para 3 — Broker revisions and closing verdict. Brokers will raise FY1 continuing ops EPS from 105.2p towards 108–112p on Acceleration Plan delivery and buyback accretion. FY2 EPS of 125.7p is likely to move to 130–138p once the Detection close crystallises the remaining £1.5bn return and share count falls further. Consensus target price of £28.29 (versus current close £23.66, implying 19.6% upside pre-results) is likely to be upgraded by £2–4 to £30–32 range as brokers model the full buyback accretion into NAV. The main constraint on the score is the cash conversion miss (78% vs mid-90s% guidance) and the modest continuing ops H1 organic performance — brokers will note that the investment thesis now rests heavily on capital allocation execution rather than organic trading momentum. Overall upgrade cycle probability: moderate-to-high. The capital return story dominates; the operating business needs to deliver the H2 acceleration to sustain re-rating momentum beyond the near term.

Year-end change Aug→Feb: full consensus reset required−8

Structural/transitional complexity depresses scoring confidence−5

Focusrite's pre-H1 trading update for the 18-month transition period delivers a net miss on revenue against the company's own disclosed consensus range. The 12-month revenue of approximately £164 million falls at or below the bottom of the disclosed sell-side range of £165.0–168.1m (midpoint miss approximately −1.5%), while the critical 6-month figure (the H1 equivalent) of approximately £76 million comes in below the bottom of its own disclosed range of £77.0–80.1m. The single definitive catalyst — and it is a negative one — is the confirmation that H2 (September 2025–February 2026) saw a 5% revenue decline YoY, driven by US distribution channel destocking following pre-tariff loading. The #1 metric is the H2 revenue figure, which at £76m is the weakest 6-month print since at least FY24 H1, signalling that the tariff/inventory disruption is taking longer to clear than the market had priced.

The mechanical H1 tracking calculation produces a revenue deviation of −8.4pp against the 3-year seasonal baseline — nominally a SELL SIGNAL — but this figure is heavily distorted by the year-end change from August to February. The Sharescope FY1 consensus of £186.6m was built on the old August year-end and includes the next H2 period (March–August 2026) which has not yet traded. Stripping out this distortion and measuring H1 revenue of £76m against the company's own disclosed 6-month consensus of £77–80.1m produces a real-world deviation of approximately −1.3 to −5pp — more consistent with IN LINE to CAUTION rather than a SELL SIGNAL. The single credible positive that contains downside risk is the EBITDA in-line message: despite the revenue miss, gross margins are "slightly ahead" of the prior year and operating margins are stable. The Martin Audio recovery is a secondary positive. The US tariff and channel inventory unwinding are explicitly presented as known, temporary, and manageable; if this characterisation holds, the H1 FY27 comparator will be clean.

Brokers face an unusual task: the entire consensus framework needs to be restructured around the new February year-end before any meaningful revision can be made. The current FY1 EPS consensus of 18.0p and FY1 revenue of £186.6m are not directly comparable to today's figures and are likely to be rebased to a Feb 2027 year-end consensus settling in the range of £170–180m revenue and 16–18p EPS — implying a 5–10% net downward revision on a like-for-like basis. The consensus target price of 340p vs a current price of 210p represents 62% implied upside that will not survive the reset; target prices are likely cut to the 260–285p range. The main constraint on the score — and the reason it sits at 42 rather than lower — is the EBITDA in-line message and the margin story, which prevent a full downgrade cycle. Upgrade cycle probability: low in the near term (3–6 months) until the new consensus framework is established and the next trading update confirms destocking is complete.

JDW — J D WETHERSPOON PLC

Routing mode: pre-H1 (latest qtrly report = 'Q4'). Interpreting incoming RNS as H1 results or pre-H1 update accordingly. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

PHASE 0A — ROUTING

Mode confirmed: pre-H1. The RNS is H1 Interim Results for the 26 weeks ended 25 January 2026. All H1 tracking and H2 calculations use pre-H1 mode.

PHASE 0B — FX REVENUE CHECK

JDW is a UK & Irish pub operator. Revenues are overwhelmingly GBP/GBP-equivalent (Republic of Ireland ~5% or less of total). No single non-GBP currency exceeds 30% of revenues. FX Rule 1 does not apply. No penalty. N/A — proceed to Phase 1.

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

  • Routing: pre-H1 mode (latest qtrly report = 'Q4'). Interpreting incoming RNS as H1 results. Sharescope data reflects pre-RNS state.
  • FY1 consensus: EPS 51.4p · Revenue £2,229.5m
  • FY2 consensus: EPS 57.4p · Revenue £2,340.4m
  • Forecast momentum: EPS net change over full period: +6.4% (48.3p → 51.4p). Upgrades dominated: October 2025 step-up from 49.3p to 54.1p; since then modest drift down to 51.4p. Net positive. 4-week trend: FLAT (51.4p unchanged last 4 weeks). Revenue net change: +5.3% (£2,117m → £2,229m).
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 47.6% × £2,229.5m = £1,061.2m · EPS 22.3% (2yr avg) × 51.4p = 11.5p
  • Prior-year H1 actuals: Revenue £1,029.5m · EPS (before separately disclosed) 21.5p
  • Implied H2 YoY: Revenue: FY1 £2,229.5m − H1 actual £1,087.8m = implied H2 £1,141.7m vs prior H2 £1,098.0m = +4.0% YoY. EPS: FY1 51.4p − H1 actual 15.5p = implied H2 35.9p vs prior H2 27.5p = +30.5% YoY
  • FX: N/A — GBP/GBP domestic business, no material non-GBP exposure

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

RNS type: H1 Results — for the 26 weeks ended 25 January 2026.

1. Revenue

  • H1 revenue: £1,087.8m (vs H1 FY2025: £1,029.5m) = +5.7% reported
  • LFL sales +4.8% (bar +7.0%, food +1.3%, slots +8.9%, hotels −0.6%)
  • vs FY1 consensus £2,229.5m: H1 = 48.8% of FY1 vs 3yr avg baseline 47.6% → deviation = +1.2pp
  • Full FY implied: no explicit FY guidance — Chairman flags "profits slightly below current market expectations"

"Total sales in the half year FY26 were, as indicated above, £1,088 million, an increase of 5.7%, compared to the same period last year."

2. EPS / Earnings

  • H1 EPS before separately disclosed items: 15.5p (vs prior year 21.5p = −27.9% YoY)
  • H1 EPS after separately disclosed items: 18.7p (vs prior year 27.8p = −32.7% YoY)
  • vs FY1 consensus EPS 51.4p: H1 = 30.2% of FY1 vs 2yr avg baseline 22.3% → deviation = +7.9pp (see Phase 3 note — the 2yr avg baseline is very low due to prior loss years in the EPS history)
  • Profit before tax (before separately disclosed): £22.4m vs prior year £32.9m = −31.9%
  • Operating profit: £52.9m vs prior year £64.8m = −18.4%

"Profit, before tax and separately disclosed items, was £22.4 million (2025: £32.9 million)."

3. Order book / forward work

  • Not applicable to a pub operator. No forward order book metric.
  • LFL post-period: last 7 weeks to 15 March 2026 LFL +2.6%; vs CGA RSM Hospitality Business Tracker −0.2% in February 2026 = outperformance for the 42nd consecutive month

"In the last seven weeks, to 15 March 2026, like-for-like sales increased by 2.6%."

4. Margin, profitability, cost signals

  • Operating margin before separately disclosed items: 4.86% (vs 6.30% prior year = −144bps)
  • Profit decline driven by: wages +£28m, repairs +£10m, business rates +£9m
  • Cost headwinds for FY2026: NI + labour costs ~£60m pa, non-commodity energy +£7m, EPR packaging levy +£2.4m (£1.6m incremental)
  • Chairman guidance: "This may result in profits that are slightly below current market expectations"
  • Free cash flow: outflow of £0.2m (vs outflow £0.5m prior year) — essentially breakeven
  • Net debt (excl. IFRS-16): £772.9m (vs £724.3m at FY2025)

"As previously indicated, increases in national insurance and labour rates will result in cost increases of approximately £60 million per annum, and non-commodity energy costs will add £7 million."

5. Capital returns and per-share items

  • Interim dividend maintained at 4.0p (unchanged YoY)
  • Share buybacks: 2,770,750 shares cancelled (2.5% of start-year capital) at average 724p per share, cost £20.1m
  • Net debt excl. IFRS-16: £772.9m (up from £724.3m); IFRS-16 debt: £1.15bn
  • No special dividend or additional return announced

"The board declared an interim dividend of 4.0p (2025: 4.0p) per share."

6. Qualitative tone

  • Explicit profit warning language: "may result in profits that are slightly below current market expectations"
  • Net debt guidance maintained: "The forecast for year-end net debt remains unchanged"
  • Franchise rollout progressing (16 franchised pubs; 15–20 more expected this FY)
  • Structural tailwind if VAT reform materialises (Reform party proposal for 10% hospitality VAT) — speculative but flagged by Chairman
  • Labour cost pressures are structural (NI, minimum wage increases) — permanent cost base step-up
  • H2 faces comparison against a stronger second half (prior H2 revenue £1,098m)

"There is clearly considerable pressure on consumer finances, combined with higher taxes, wages and energy costs for the hospitality industry."

PHASE 3 — HISTORICAL BENCHMARKING

a. Full-Year YoY Growth Table

Revenue growth trajectory: +10.6%, +5.7%, +9.5%e → +++Steady+++ (consistent single-digit organic growth) EPS growth trajectory: n/m recovery → +89.5% → +9.8%e → Volatile (recovery from loss base distorts; underlying trend is now +++Steady+++ at the current stage of recovery)

1. Half-on-Half (HoH) Growth Pattern

*Prior H2 FY2025: Revenue = FY2025 £2,073.5m − H1 £1,029.5m ≈ £1,044m; EPS: FY2025 actual 46.8p − H1 21.5p (before SDI) = 25.3p (statutory); but Sharescope shows 'current' H2 27.5p — using 27.5p as Sharescope prior H2 EPS.

H2 derivation: FY1e £2,229.5m − H1 £1,087.8m = H2 implied £1,141.7m. FY1e EPS 51.4p − H1 15.5p = H2 implied 35.9p.

Revenue trajectory: +12.4%, +5.7%, +9.3%e → +++Steady+++ growth trend EPS trajectory (before SDI): H1 sharply down −27.9%, H2 required to be +31.5%. This implies the EPS mix is sharply H2-weighted and the H2 implied EPS (35.9p) seems achievable only if H2 costs normalise. Volatile — cost headwinds are concentrated in H1 (NI/wage rises effective April 2025 onwards), and H2 prior year comparison is a lighter comp.

2. Seasonal H1 % of FY Baseline, Tracking Deviation and Signal (pre-H1 mode)

Revenue:

  • Baseline: 47.6% × £2,229.5m = £1,061.2m
  • H1 actual: £1,087.8m = 48.8% of FY1
  • Deviation: +++[+1.2pp]+++
  • Signal: 🟡 IN LINE (between −1.5pp and +1.5pp threshold)
  • Buy trigger: H1 Rev > [£1,061.2m × 1.015] = £1,077.1m → £1,087.8m +++✓+++ (beats by £10.7m)

EPS:

  • Baseline: 22.3% × 51.4p = 11.5p
  • H1 actual: 15.5p = 30.2% of FY1
  • Deviation: +++[+7.9pp]+++ — massively above baseline
  • Signal: +++🟢 STRONG BUY+++ (≥+2.5pp)
  • Buy trigger: H1 EPS > [11.5p × 1.015] = 11.7p → 15.5p +++✓+++

CRITICAL CAVEAT — EPS signal distortion: The 2yr avg EPS H1 split of 22.3% (from Sharescope) was calculated over recovery years when H1 EPS was 0.7p (2y ago) and 21.5p (1y ago) against full years of 24.7p and 46.8p — giving very low H1%s due to the H2-weighted recovery. The 22.3% baseline is misleadingly low. The true normalised H1% for JDW at steady state is closer to 40–45% of FY. Against a 40% baseline: 15.5p / 51.4p = 30.2% vs 40% → deviation = −9.8pp → ---🔴 SELL SIGNAL---. This is the correct directional read.

True signal (adjusted): The EPS +++🟢 STRONG BUY+++ from the mechanical calculation is entirely a baseline artefact. The correct assessment is that H1 EPS of 15.5p versus the FY1 consensus of 51.4p requires H2 EPS of 35.9p — that is an implausible step-up given the Chairman has just guided "slightly below market expectations" and operating profit fell 18.4% in H1. H2 EPS of 35.9p would be +31.5% YoY vs prior H2 of 27.5p — achievable only if wage/NI cost headwinds (£60m annualised = ~£30m H2) are fully absorbed and like-for-like sales accelerate. Given LFL of only +2.6% in the post-period, the £35.9p H2 implied EPS looks optimistic.

H2 EPS burden: FY1 51.4p − H1 15.5p = 35.9p required in H2. Historical H2 avg (1yr and 2yr): 27.3p and 24.0p avg = ~25.7p. Implied H2 burden of 35.9p is HIGHER than historical H2 average by ~10p. This is elevated.

Historical hit rate (revenue): H1 Rev above baseline for 2 of last 2 trackable years → positive H1 deviation did precede FY beat in 1 of 2 years.

3. Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical

Pre-H1 mode — implied H2 vs average last 3 historical H2 figures:

H2 revenue implied: £1,141.7m Prior 3 H2 revenues: £1,044.5m (1y ago), £1,009.1m (2y ago), £933.1m (3y ago) → avg £995.6m YoY vs most recent H2: £1,141.7m vs £1,044.5m = +9.3% → ~~~moderate~~~ (at upper end)

H2 EPS implied: 35.9p Prior 3 H2 EPS: 27.5p, 24.0p, −0.3p → avg ~17.1p (excluding loss year: ~25.8p) YoY vs most recent H2 (27.5p): +30.5% → +++strong+++ (>+10%)

BUT this is driven by a need for the FY consensus to be met. The Chairman's profit warning suggests consensus may need to fall. If FY1 EPS cuts to, say, 43–46p (−10% to −15%), implied H2 = 27.5–30.5p → flat to modest growth vs prior H2.

H2 revenue classification: moderate (+9.3% vs prior H2) H2 EPS classification (pre-warning): +++strong+++ (implied +30.5%) — but consensus needs to fall, making this moderate to ---weak--- post-downgrade

4. Forecast Momentum Overlay

  • EPS trend: Net change +6.4% (48.3p to 51.4p) over the full snapshot period. This includes a jump in October 2025 (+4.8p) followed by a modest drift lower (−2.7p). Underlying trend has been positive over 12 months.
  • 4-week trend: FLAT (51.4p unchanged for 4 weeks)
  • Divergence: Price has been broadly stable at 741–745p (consensus TP level) for several months, with a slight drift down to 653p at latest. Forecast EPS has barely moved recently. The RNS profit warning will force a downward revision, creating a negative divergence — price likely to fall further from consensus TP.

5. Structural / One-Off Flags

  • £60m pa NI/wage headwind: Structural, permanent cost base increase effective from April 2025 budget. This is not a one-off — annualised burden continues into FY2027. Brokers have been partially modelling this but the scale (£60m pa) confirmed in results is the biggest structural negative.

"Increases in national insurance and labour rates will result in cost increases of approximately £60 million per annum."

  • Franchise growth: 16 franchised pubs now open (expected 15–20 more this FY). This is a capital-light margin-accretive model — a structural positive that the market has not yet fully priced. Franchised pubs performing "well, with encouraging sales levels."
  • VAT reform speculative upside: Chairman's lengthy discussion of Reform party's 10% hospitality VAT proposal. Not in any model. If it materialised, it would be transformational. Zero probability in current forecasts.
  • Buyback: 2.5% of share capital cancelled in H1 at 724p average. Modest EPS uplift.

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

#1 Driver — Profit warning language (explicit): "May result in profits that are slightly below current market expectations" is the dominant item. Brokers will treat this as a mandatory downgrade trigger. The current FY1 EPS consensus of 51.4p implies H2 EPS of 35.9p — a +30.5% step-up from prior H2 27.5p. Given H1 operating profit fell 18.4% and costs are structurally higher, this is being signalled as undeliverable. Brokers will cut FY1 EPS to the 43–46p range.

#2 Driver — Cost inflation magnitude confirmed: The £60m pa NI/labour + £7m energy + £2.4m EPR = ~£70m annualised cost headwind is now confirmed and fully quantified. This impacts both FY1 and FY2 modelling. The question brokers will ask is: can 4.8% LFL revenue growth absorb £35m of incremental H2 costs? The answer appears to be: barely, and not fully.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY1 Revenue: HOLD — revenue tracking is solid (+5.7% H1, +4.8% LFL). Revenue consensus unlikely to change materially; range −1% to +1%.
  • FY1 EPS (51.4p): expected DOWN by −10% to −15%, to 43–46p range. The profit warning combined with the mechanically implied H2 EPS burden and confirmed cost headwinds drives this.
  • FY2 EPS (57.4p): expected DOWN by −5% to −10%, to 52–54p range, as the £60m pa cost headwind persists in full.
  • Target price: likely CUT from 741p consensus. New TP range estimate: 640–680p. Current close 653p = at/below revised TP, limiting further relative downside but removing upside case.

Conservative guidance read-through: "Slightly below current market expectations" is rarely interpreted as conservative by brokers — it is a direct profit warning. There is no language suggesting deliberate under-guidance; the Chairman is explicit about the cost pressures. This does not increase upgrade cycle probability.

Key risk: The medium-term debt trajectory is a concern. Net debt (excl. IFRS-16) rose to £772.9m from £724.3m — with IFRS-16 total debt at £1.15bn — and interest cover of only 2.3x. If LFL momentum slows below 4%, FCF will deteriorate and the balance sheet becomes a constraint. The note that "private placement notes of £98m mature in August 2026" adds near-term refinancing risk.

"There is clearly considerable pressure on consumer finances, combined with higher taxes, wages and energy costs for the hospitality industry."

Overall broker tone: ---Cautious / downgrades or target cuts probable---

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

Score: 38/100 · Confidence range: 33–43 · No FX adjustment

42 consecutive months of CGA tracker outperformance+5

VAT reform speculative upside (not in model)+2
Dividend maintained at 4.0p (stability signal)+2
Total38

Para 1 — Headline numbers vs consensus. JDW's H1 FY2026 results delivered a direct profit warning that will force FY1 EPS consensus cuts of 10–15%. The headline numbers tell the story starkly: operating profit of £52.9m was down −18.4% YoY (vs £64.8m), profit before tax fell −31.9% to £22.4m, and EPS before separately disclosed items dropped to 15.5p from 21.5p — a decline of 27.9%. Revenue was the bright spot: +5.7% to £1,087.8m with LFL sales of +4.8%, outperforming the CGA industry tracker (−0.2%) for the 42nd consecutive month. But the revenue growth is being swamped by a structural cost step-up of ~£70m pa in wage costs, NI contributions, energy and regulatory levies — the most significant structural margin headwind the company has faced in recent years.

Para 2 — H1 tracking and implied H2 burden. The H1 EPS deviation signal mechanically fires as a +++STRONG BUY+++ due to the distorted 2-year average baseline (recovery years when H1 EPS was near zero). Adjusting for a normalised ~40% H1 split, the true signal is a ---CAUTION--- to ---SELL--- — H1 EPS of 15.5p covers only 30.2% of FY1 consensus (51.4p), requiring H2 EPS of 35.9p, a +31% step-up from prior H2 of 27.5p. With cost headwinds running at ~£30m in H2 (half of the £60m pa annualised NI/wage burden) and LFL sales running at only +2.6% post-period versus the +4.8% H1 average, this step-up appears undeliverable at current consensus. Post-period LFL decelerating to +2.6% from +4.8% in H1 is a material deterioration. The net debt guidance being maintained unchanged is a modest positive — but at 1.2× EV/EBITDA basis debt and only 2.3× interest cover, the balance sheet leaves little room for further earnings compression.

Para 3 — Broker revisions and closing verdict. FY1 EPS consensus of 51.4p is set to be cut to 43–46p (−10% to −15%), with FY2 EPS of 57.4p likely falling to 52–54p as the £60m pa cost burden persists. The consensus TP of 741p will likely be revised down to 640–680p — the current close of 653p is already near or below revised TP on many broker models, suggesting the shares may be finding support but that upside is limited in the near term. The main watch point is whether H2 LFL accelerates beyond the 2.6% post-period rate — every 100bps of LFL above this level adds approximately £11m of revenue and roughly 3–4p of EPS. The VAT reform story is a speculative upside call option that no model includes but which the Chairman is actively lobbying for. Upgrade cycle probability: low. This is a downgrade cycle driven by confirmed structural cost headwinds and the explicit profit warning. The stock requires evidence of LFL acceleration above 4% and/or cost relief (VAT, energy) before the investment case re-establishes itself.

Para 1 — Headline numbers: TND delivered FY25 revenue of £26.15m (+6.2% YoY), landing essentially spot-on consensus of £26.2m. The headline EPS of 15.4p vs consensus 10.3p appears a dramatic +49% beat, but the definitive catalyst beneath the surface is the gross margin expansion to 31.1% (+120bps), which is the genuine operational outperformance. The EPS beat is materially inflated by a £282k deferred tax credit that pushes statutory net profit to £850k. Strip this out and underlying EPS aligns with consensus at ~10.3p. Bicycles was the standout division at +37.5% revenue growth to £10.2m, outperforming the broader sector.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: The business is structurally improving — net debt halved from £4.3m to £1.9m, inventory reduced by £1.5m, and gross margin expanded for a second consecutive year. The implied H2 FY25 revenue of £15.0m (+1.4% vs H2 FY24) confirms the seasonal H2-weighting is intact and growing. The bear case is the Toys Sports & Leisure division, which declined 17.5% YoY (a £2.2m revenue shortfall), driven by retailer purchasing pattern changes and softer discretionary demand. This drag was known to brokers (consensus revenue came down from £27.3m to £26.2m in mid-Feb) and is already in the base. The dividend reinstatement at 3.0p and early FY26 trading described as TSL "ahead of prior year" in both FOB and domestic channels is the key reason the downside risk is contained — the TSL recovery appears underway.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: With single-broker coverage (Cavendish), the revision dynamics are muted. Expect FY26 (now FY1) EPS to be revised to 11.0–12.0p as brokers model the 31.1% gross margin into the forward and recognise the underlying operating leverage. Revenue for FY26 likely moves to £26.5–27.0m. TP likely held at 350p — already representing 109% upside and reflecting the significant discount to net assets (NAV £26.1m vs market cap ~£9.2m). The main watch-point is whether TSL's positive early momentum sustains through H1 FY26; if it does, FY26 revenue could surprise to the upside. 🏁 TND is a hold: the results are solid and in line operationally, the balance sheet improvement is real, and the dividend reinstatement is encouraging — but the EPS beat is largely a tax artefact and the upgrade cycle is structurally limited by single-broker coverage and micro-cap illiquidity.

  2. EPS / Earnings: Adjusted basic EPS 6.2p (+47.6% vs H1 FY25: 4.2p). Statutory EPS 6.2p (+77.1% vs H1 FY25: 3.5p). Adjusted PBT £20.9m (+53.7%). vs FY1 H1 proxy baseline of 5.3p = +0.9p / +17% beat vs implied seasonal norm. Implied H2 EPS burden = 11.4p − 6.2p = 5.2p (vs prior H2 4.9p — burden moderately higher but manageable given FY guidance held). "Adjusted basic and diluted EPS...6.2p...H1 FY25: 4.2p...47.6%"
  3. Order book / forward work: No explicit order book figure. FY guidance of ~£140m confirmed and unchanged post period-end. Company notes H1-weighted profile explicitly flagged — management anticipate H2 lower than H1 due to elevated retailer stock levels and H1 product launch pull-forward. "due to a better than expected peak trading period and accelerated demand for a number of H1 FY26 product launches, this is expected to result in a more H1‑weighted revenue profile than in prior years"
  4. Margin / profitability: Gross margin 46.7% (H1 FY25: 46.8%) — virtually flat, down only 10bps despite revenue +57%. Adjusted EBITDA margin 28.9% (H1 FY25: 29.0%). Admin expenses 18.9% of revenue (held flat despite listed-company cost step-up). Whey protein headwind absorbed. "total gross margin was stable moving down 10bps to 46.7% (H1 FY25: 46.8%)"
  5. Capital / cash / per-share: Net cash £26.4m (H1 FY25: £10.9m). No dividend declared or anticipated before FY27. Capex H1 £0.2m; major capex (£2.0–2.5m manufacturing; £3.5–4.0m distribution facility) falls H2 FY26 / FY27. Construction commenced on global distribution facility post period-end; revenue capacity to increase to ~£300m. "Net cash4 at period end of £26.4m (H1 FY25: £10.9m)" "The Company does not anticipate declaring a further dividend before FY27"
  6. Qualitative tone: Explicitly H1-weighted revenue profile guided. H2 expected to see Middle East volume softness. Management confident FY £140m unchanged. New Morrisons out-licensing deal, Tesco ABE launch, Latin America +110%. Structural: manufacturing extension to ~£300m capacity underway — multi-year capacity headroom removes a key constraint. "Although we expect some reduction in volumes into the region during the second half, at this stage there is no change to FY26 guidance of full year revenue of approximately £140 million"

2. Seasonal H1 % of FY Baseline, Tracking Deviation and Signal

  • Revenue baseline: 52.7% (1yr avg) × £140.3m = £73.9m
  • EPS baseline (proxy): 46.2% (1yr proxy) × 11.4p = 5.3p
  • Revenue tracking: £74.5m ÷ £140.3m = 53.1% vs baseline 52.7% → deviation = 🟢 [+0.4pp]
  • EPS tracking: 6.2p ÷ 11.4p = 54.4% vs baseline 46.2% → deviation = 🟢 [+8.2pp]

  • Buy triggers: H1 Rev > [73.9m × 1.015] = £75.0m → actual £74.5m → 🔴 ✗ · H1 EPS > [5.3p × 1.015] = 5.4p → actual 6.2p → 🟢 ✓
  • Historical hit rate: Insufficient history (1 year of H1/H2 data) — cannot calculate

Revenue signal: +0.4pp deviation → 🟡 IN LINE (barely above seasonal norm; management has deliberately guided H1-heavy profile so this is almost exactly as anticipated)

EPS signal: +8.2pp deviation → 🟢 STRONG BUY — H1 EPS materially outperforming seasonal norm; H2 burden of 5.2p well below what the EPS beat implies consensus assumed

Important structural note: Management has explicitly flagged the H1-weighted revenue profile as a function of peak-season retailer stock-up and H1 product launch pull-forward. The EPS STRONG BUY signal is genuine — H1 adj EPS of 6.2p vs 5.3p baseline is a real beat — but the revenue IN LINE signal reflects management's own pre-signalling rather than underperformance.

3. Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical

Pre-H1 mode: compare implied H2 vs prior-year H2:

  • Revenue: implied H2 £65.8m vs prior H2 £59.5m = +10.6% → 🟢 moderate (0–10% band nearly breached; sits just above; classify moderate-to-strong)
  • EPS: implied H2 5.2p vs prior H2 4.9p = +6.1% → 🟡 moderate (+0–10%)

Despite the H1-weighting narrative, H2 is still expected to grow meaningfully YoY. This is consistent with FY guidance held.

4. Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

  • EPS trend: net change +34.1% over full period (8.5p → 11.4p). 3+ distinct upgrade rounds. Upgrades: multiple; downgrades: zero
  • 4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING (flat 11.4p/291p since 21 Feb 26 — results were today so upgrades not yet reflected)
  • Divergence: Price at 220.5p vs TP 291p = 32% upside to consensus TP pre-results. Strong upgrade cycle has outpaced price move. Broker momentum has been consistently ahead of price action — positive divergence favouring further re-rating on today's beat.

5. Structural / One-Off Flags

H1-weighting shift: This year's revenue profile is explicitly more H1-weighted than prior years due to peak retailer stock-building and accelerated NPD demand. Brokers must model a lower H2 run-rate than H1 — this is not a negative flag, it is management-guided.

"due to a better than expected peak trading period and accelerated demand for a number of H1 FY26 product launches, this is expected to result in a more H1‑weighted revenue profile than in prior years"

Capacity expansion: New global distribution facility and manufacturing phase 3 targeting £300m revenue capacity — multi-year structural driver. Capex of £5.5–6.5m falling FY27, so no near-term EPS drag.

Middle East softness: Some H2 volume reduction expected in Middle East but no guidance change. Risk quantified and contained.

APN — PHASE 4

#1 Driver — H1 EPS beat vs expectation: The adjusted EPS of 6.2p vs the implied seasonal baseline of ~5.3p is an ~17% beat on the half. Brokers will lead with this in notes. The statutory EPS of 6.2p vs H1 FY25 statutory 3.5p (+77%) is eye-catching but adj-to-adj is what matters for revision models.

#2 Driver — FY guidance confirmation at £140m despite H1-weighting flag: The explicit maintenance of FY revenue guidance even while flagging Middle East softness and a more H1-heavy profile is the second key signal. Brokers will view this as deliberately conservative — the "no change to FY26 guidance" language after beating H1 is a classic de-risking statement that typically triggers modest upward pressure on H2 estimates.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY1 Revenue: consensus already at £140.3m and management guided £140m — expect hold with slight tightening of range. Some brokers may nudge to £141–143m given the H1 beat.
  • FY1 EPS: consensus 11.4p — with H1 adj at 6.2p implying H2 of 5.2p, most brokers will hold or nudge +2–5%. Expect FY1 EPS to move to 11.5–12.0p.
  • FY2 Revenue: expect +3–5% upgrades as capacity expansion and new channel wins (Morrisons out-licensing, Tesco launch, LATAM +110%) are factored into out-year models. FY2 to move towards £160–165m.
  • FY2 EPS: expect +5–8% upgrades on FY2 as operating leverage kicks in at higher revenue base. FY2 moves from 12.6p towards 13.0–13.5p.

Target price / recommendation: Consensus TP at 291p vs price 220.5p = 32% upside. Expect brokers to raise TPs to 300–325p range. No recommendation change warranted — stock already on buy ratings across the board. Upgrading to strong buy unlikely given the H1-weighting caveat and Middle East risk, but conviction on existing buys will increase.

Conservative guidance read-through: The maintenance of £140m guidance despite a materially better H1 and with Middle East headwinds acknowledged is classic under-promise language. The combination of "no change to guidance" + "some reduction in Middle East volumes" implies the underlying business ex-Middle East is running ahead of the full-year number. This increases the probability of an upgrade cycle into H2 results.

Key risk: H2 revenue shortfall from Middle East. International was 46% of H1 revenue (£34.2m), with Middle East a significant constituent alongside LATAM. If Middle East disruption is worse than anticipated, H2 revenue could undershoot the implied £65.8m. "we expect some reduction in volumes into the region during the second half" — the lack of quantification is a watch point.

Overall tone: 🟢 Constructive / modest upgrades likely

Para 1 — Headline numbers: Applied Nutrition delivered a genuinely outstanding H1, with adjusted EPS of 6.2p against an implied seasonal baseline of ~5.3p — a +17% beat on the half and a +48% YoY improvement. Revenue of £74.5m grew +56.5% YoY, beating the seasonal norm of £73.9m by 0.6pp. The single definitive catalyst is the EPS STRONG BUY deviation of +8.2pp, which confirms that H1 earnings are materially outperforming the pattern implied by the FY consensus — even accounting for the company's own H1-weighting guidance. Gross margin of 46.7% is essentially flat YoY despite a £27m revenue uplift, which demonstrates genuine operating leverage and pricing power even as whey protein costs rose.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: The H1 tracking signal on EPS (+8.2pp) is the strongest signal in the scorecard. Implied H2 EPS of 5.2p represents only +6.1% YoY growth against prior H2 of 4.9p — a deliberately soft H2 embedded in FY consensus that management has explicitly guided via the H1-weighting narrative. The bear case is straightforward: Middle East volumes soften, H2 comes in at £60–62m revenue rather than the implied £65.8m. But FY guidance has been held at £140m precisely because management knew this when they confirmed it. The structural driver — new distribution facility targeting £300m revenue capacity, plus the Morrisons out-licensing, Tesco ABE, and LATAM +110% growth — ensures the FY27 upgrade story is firmly in place even if H2 FY26 is managed conservatively. The H2 burden of 5.2p is actually lower than it appears: the 4-week stalling in broker estimates means some brokers have already embedded a mildly conservative H2, so the actual revision gap is narrower than the +17% H1 EPS beat implies.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: FY1 EPS is likely to move from 11.4p to 11.5–12.0p (range +1–5%), with FY1 revenue held near £140–143m. FY2 EPS revisions are more interesting: expect upgrades from 12.6p towards 13.0–13.5p (+3–7%) as new channel wins and operating leverage are modelled through. Consensus target price of 291p should move to 300–325p, representing 36–47% upside from the 220.5p close. The main watch-point is H2 Middle East quantification — if the company provides any colour at the full-year stage, that will determine whether FY2 gets a more aggressive upgrade. 🏁 APN is a clear hold-and-add on results: the H1 EPS beat is material, FY guidance is conservative, and the upgrade cycle has further to run into FY27 as capacity comes on stream.

This is the contracted order book as at 30 April 2025 — not the "workload" figure of £287m (which includes probable but not yet contracted work). £201.5m of performance obligations is audited and firm. The within-1-year tranche of £69.5m at 30 April 2025 grew to £330m workload by December and £288m by February 2026. The scheduled SSB deliveries (237 contractually awarded of potential 747, 90 shipped to date at FY25) are in the >1-year tranches.

Revenue recognition note — critical for FY27

The accounts state explicitly: "The Mechanical Engineering segment of the Group contains large non-seasonal contracts, and therefore significant variations are to be expected year on year in the trade receivable, contract assets, work in progress and contract liabilities balances."

Contract liabilities at FY25: £34.75m (from £14.86m in FY24) — this is cash received from customers for work not yet delivered. A rising contract liability is a leading indicator of future revenue recognition. The £19.9m YoY increase in contract liabilities signals significant work front-loaded in payments that will flow through the P&L in FY26.

Dividend policy — the actual wording

The FY25 annual report contains the formal 58% payout policy, with the Board stating: "the Board is confident that the alteration of the dividend policy from 38% to 58% of post-tax profits plus depreciation and amortisation is a safe and viable change for now and the foreseeable future."

The March 2026 trading update then signals a potential reversion. The phrase used in the update ("considering whether to revert") against this language is jarring — the policy was confirmed as "safe and viable for the foreseeable future" only 8 months ago. This is the crux of the market's reaction.

Defence alone = 57% of a £287m workload = £163m of contracted/probable future work. This is what makes the Sellafield loss (nuclear, not defence) more containable than the market may be pricing — the defence backlog is enormous and multi-decade. Nuclear is only 9% of workload (£26m), so losing one Sellafield tender doesn't decimate the nuclear contribution as much as feared.

Goodwin International — the Sellafield SSB context

The Chairman states: "237 SSBs have been contractually awarded and 90 of these have been manufactured and shipped. However, it is reported that up to 747 of these SSBs could be required and, with no one else in the UK able to supply the product."

This is crucial. The Sellafield tender lost in the March 2026 update is for a new contract (the "unexpectedly" lost tender), but the existing SSB programme (237 contracted, 147 still to deliver) continues. The trading update says the Sellafield loss is on a new competitive tender — not on the existing SSB programme. The 147 remaining SSBs to be delivered (90 of 237 shipped) represent substantial ongoing work at premium margins.

The SSB programme alone (147 units × implied £150–200k per unit contribution) = £22–29m of residual revenues still to flow from the existing contract. This was not cancelled — only the new tender was lost.

Revised score — incorporating annual report data

Changes from the new information

1. Sellafield loss — less severe than initially modelled (score: +3 pts back)

The lost tender is a new competitive tender, not cancellation of the existing SSB programme. 147 SSBs remain to be delivered under existing contract. The nuclear workload is only 9% of the total £287m workload. Revenue impact of the new tender loss is spread over multiple years, and the existing work continues. I overpenalised this.

2. Performance obligations secured backlog — more visibility than I credited (+2 pts)

£201.5m audited performance obligations at April 2025, with the 2–5 year book growing materially (£125m vs £114m prior year). This structural backlog visibility supports FY27 earnings better than my initial model assumed. The £69.5m within-1-year tranche at April 2025 alone exceeds FY24 half-year revenue.

3. Contract liability increase — FY26 revenue more assured (+2 pts)

The £19.9m YoY increase in contract liabilities (cash already received, work still to deliver) is a leading indicator confirming FY26 revenue recognition will be strong. This further supports the >£71m trading PBT guidance reliability.

4. Mechanical Engineering margin base — FY25 was only 16.3%, H1 FY26 30.1% (+0, confirms step-change)

The H1 FY26 margin is extraordinary because FY25's 16.3% was itself a step-up from sub-15% in prior years. The FY27 question is whether margins revert to FY25's 16% or settle somewhere between 16% and 30%. Given the SSB deliveries continue, Northrop ramps, and Easat builds, a FY27 Mechanical margin of 20–22% (vs H1 FY26's 30%, vs FY25's 16%) is more realistic than my bear case of 16% reversion. This lifts the central FY27 PBT estimate.

5. Dividend policy — wording confirms severity of reversal (−2 pts, net of above)

The formal FY25 annual report policy language ("safe and viable for the foreseeable future") makes the March 2026 "considering reverting" signal a genuine governance negative — the Board contradicted its own stated confidence within 8 months. This is a trust issue, not just a financial one. Modestly increases the penalty.

6. Defence = 57% of workload — structural underpinning confirmed (+1 pt)

The £163m of defence backlog (57% of £287m workload) is materially larger than I had modelled. Multi-decade submarine programmes (Astute, Virginia, Columbia, Dreadnought, Type 26, Gerald R Ford, AUKUS) provide genuine long-cycle revenue visibility. This makes the FY27 downside less severe.

The positives are now better-grounded (SSB continuity, defence workload proportion, secured backlog). The negatives are more precisely calibrated (Sellafield loss contained to new tender only; dividend reversal confirmed as severe; FY27 margin compression central case ~20–22%, not full reversion to 16%).

What actually changes vs original 62

The original 62 was built without: the precise Mechanical margin at FY25 (16.3%), the SSB programme detail (147 units remaining on existing contract — not lost), the performance obligations breakdown (£201.5m audited, 2–5yr book expanding), the contract liability leading indicator, or the exact dividend policy language.   • Dividend reversal is more bad than scored (−2 pts severity increase)
  • Structural backlog and defence concentration is better than scored (+2 pts)

  • EPS trend: Net −2.6% over full period (15.4p → 15.0p). Revenue cut −4.8% (£330m → £314m). TP cut from 297p to 248p (−16.5%). Steady stream of modest downgrades reflecting Germany photobooth regulatory headwind, FX, and strategic review uncertainty.
  • 4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING (flat at 15.0p/£314m/248p since late Jan 26)
  • Divergence: Price 136.6p vs TP 248p = 81.5% upside to consensus TP. Extraordinary discount — reflects: (1) shares suspended pending annual report publication; (2) terminated strategic review; (3) declining EPS estimates; (4) declining TP. This is a recovery/re-listing catalyst, not a fundamental upgrade cycle.

5. Structural / One-Off Flags

Share suspension and re-listing: Shares were suspended pending publication of the annual report. Today's announcement triggers restoration of listing. This is a technical re-listing event, not a fundamental change, but it removes an overhang.

"the Company will apply for the restoration of the listing and trading of its shares"

Germany photobooth regulatory change (permanent): Government regulation requiring ID photos at official offices or certified photographers — introduced May 2025. Revenue impact £3.0m in H2 2025. Group developing new-gen biometric booths for compliance (deployment H2 2026). This is a structural negative for German photobooth revenue until new machines deployed.

"The Group expects the impact to continue in FY 2026, with revenue recovering thereafter."

Strategic review terminated — no offer received: The Board confirmed in Dec 2025 that no acceptable offer was received and discussions terminated. Removes M&A premium from price, removes uncertainty — but also confirms no near-term exit catalyst.

£18m share buyback: Announced alongside results. At 136.6p, £18m buys approximately 13.2m shares (~3.5% of shares outstanding). Positive for EPS accretion in FY26.

MEGP — PHASE 4

#1 Driver — Laundry estate growth (+17.7% machines, EBITDA £55.5m +18.1%): This is the core thesis. Laundry now 46.1% of Group EBITDA. The roll-out momentum (1,326 gross installs in FY25 vs 1,168 in FY24) and FY26 target of 1,300+ machines confirms the structural growth engine is intact. Brokers will lead with laundry unit economics and trajectory.

#2 Driver — £18m buyback + 9.5% dividend increase: The capital return package is the second-order catalyst. At 136.6p the shares trade at a significant discount to intrinsic value (consensus TP 248p). The £18m buyback is ~3.5% of market cap, providing meaningful EPS accretion and signalling Board confidence at the current price.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY1 (FY26) Revenue: consensus £314m — expect hold or slight trim to £310–315m as Germany photobooth headwind continues and laundry growth partially offsets. No material revision.
  • FY1 EPS: consensus 15.0p — with FY25 actual 14.91p and buyback accretion (+0.15–0.2p), expect hold to slight upgrade 15.1–15.5p.
  • FY2 Revenue: £326.2m — hold, consistent with ~3–4% growth as laundry mix continues to increase.
  • FY2 EPS: 15.5p — expect upgrade to 15.8–16.2p as buyback accretion folds in and Germany normalises.
  • TP: Consensus 248p vs price 136.6p. Expect hold at 248p or possible slight increase to 255–265p as re-listing removes discount. Brokers may revisit sum-of-parts given laundry's high EBITDA margin (49.4%) and growth rate.

Conservative guidance read-through: "In line with expectations" for FY26 YTD is neutral — not a "comfortable with current forecasts" or "not less than" statement. It does not increase upgrade probability but de-risks the FY26 start, especially given the listing restoration uncertainty.

Key risk: Germany photobooth regulatory impact continuing into FY26. The new biometric machines are not deploying until H2 2026, meaning the £3m+ revenue headwind continues for at least 9 months of FY26. Additionally, JPY weakness (1.9% depreciation vs GBP in FY25) will persist as a structural translation drag on Asia Pacific.

"The Group expects the impact to continue in FY 2026, with revenue recovering thereafter."

Overall tone: 🟡 Neutral / hold and wait — results are essentially in line, the structural laundry story is excellent, but the growth rate is decelerating, Germany is an ongoing headwind, the strategic review failed, and the stock was suspended. Re-listing removes the overhang but the underlying upgrade dynamics are muted.

MEGP — PHASE 5

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

Raw score: 60 → After FX penalty: 55/100 · Confidence: 48–62 · FX Rule 1 applied (−5 pts) · ~68% EUR · neutral rate · 🟡 Neutral / hold and wait

Adjusted for FX penalty (−5 pts): 55/100

Para 1 — Headline numbers: ME Group delivered a solid FY25 with PBT of £78.2m (+6.5% YoY), a +2.6% beat vs consensus at the operating profit level. Revenue of £315.4m (+2.4%) was essentially in line with the £314.0m forecast. The definitive catalyst in this announcement is not the in-line trading result but the dual shareholder return package: a 9.5% dividend increase to 8.64p and the launch of an £18m share buyback at a time when the stock sits 82% below consensus TP. The #1 metric for broker notes is laundry EBITDA of £55.5m (+18.1%), which now constitutes 46.1% of Group EBITDA and demonstrates the structural shift away from legacy photobooths is working.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: The HoH revenue growth has decelerated from +24.7% (H1 FY24) to +2.6% in H2 FY25, reflecting the Germany photobooth headwind (£3.0m revenue impact), the H1 printer supplier issue (now resolved), and FX translation. Laundry vending revenue grew +10.2% despite the warm summer dampening demand — testament to the estate expansion. The Germany headwind is the most significant structural risk to the upgrade case: new biometric booths will not deploy until H2 FY26, meaning the negative impact on photobooth revenue persists for the first ~9 months of FY26. Against this, the £18m buyback (≈3.5% of shares) will provide +0.15–0.3p of EPS accretion in FY26, partially offsetting the Germany drag. The "in line with expectations" FY26 opening statement de-risks the near-term but provides no positive deviation.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: FY1 (FY26) EPS is expected to be held at 15.0–15.3p (very modest +0–2% revision as buyback accretion is offset by Germany continuation). FY2 EPS may see a slightly more positive revision to 15.8–16.2p (+2–5%) as Germany normalises post H2 2026 and laundry growth compounds. The consensus TP of 248p is likely to be held or marginally increased to 255–265p following re-listing — the stock at 136.6p already offers 82% upside and the buyback signals the Board agrees the discount is excessive. The main watch-point is Germany: if the new biometric photobooth rollout (H2 2026) meets its schedule, the FY27 recovery becomes a meaningful catalyst. 🏁 MEGP is a neutral-to-cautious hold on results: the underlying business is structurally sound with an excellent laundry engine, but the decelerating top-line, ongoing Germany headwind, failed strategic review and post-suspension re-listing dynamic keep a lid on near-term upgrade expectations. The buyback and dividend increase are positives but do not change the fundamental growth trajectory.

#1 Driver — Order book expansion to £23.3m (+46.5%): This is the one metric that brokers will cite as justification for maintaining the recovery thesis. The return to break-even PBT guided by management is credible if the contracted work delivers on schedule.

#2 Driver — Going concern uncertainty: The auditor's material uncertainty flag overshadows everything. Brokers will note that the HSBC facility has been renewed post-period (only £1m limit) and the shareholder loan (£0.3m, due April 2026) requires repayment. If new business conversion is delayed, the Group may need further equity raises. At 22p this is partially priced in, but it is the dominant risk.

Conservative guidance read-through: "Return to break-even adjusted PBT in FY26" — affirmative and specific. Not typical cautious language. But set against a going concern flag, the credibility requires order book execution.

Key risk: Going concern — new business conversion timing. The Group explicitly states the auditors have flagged this for both FY24 and FY25. "scenarios whereby the levels of forecast new business converted...may cast significant doubt upon the company's ability to continue as a going concern."

Overall tone: 🔴 Cautious / downgrades or target cuts probable — the results missed consensus slightly, the adj loss was deeper than expected, going concern flag persists, and the company remains dependent on new contract wins to survive.
