Para 1 — Headline numbers: Pennant's FY25 was a deeply challenging year, with revenue of £9.66m down −29.7% YoY, missing consensus of £10.0m by −3.4%. The definitive catalyst — and the only positive one — is the order book expansion to £23.3m (+46.5%), of which £9.7m is contracted for FY26 delivery. The adjusted EBITDA loss widened to −£0.4m from +£1.7m in FY24, and the adjusted loss before tax of −£1.9m was slightly worse than the consensus forecast of −£1.8m. The one metric brokers will anchor to is that the contracted FY26 backlog (£9.7m) is essentially equivalent to the FY26 revenue consensus (£10.0m) before any new wins — this changes the risk profile for FY26 significantly relative to FY25.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: H2 FY25 revenue of £5.2m was better than H1's £4.5m, showing sequential improvement even if H2 YoY was still −18.8%. The going concern material uncertainty — flagged by auditors for the second consecutive year — is the primary constraint on the upgrade thesis. The HSBC overdraft facility stands at only £1m, the shareholder loan (£0.3m) fell due in April 2026, and the Group needs new contract wins beyond the existing order book to sustain operations beyond the near-term. The structured cost base (admin down to £6.6m after restructuring) and ARR of £2.4m (+26%) provide a floor, and the Siemens OEM partnership could accelerate new territory penetration — but both are too early-stage to de-risk the going concern in isolation.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: Expect the single covering broker to trim FY1 revenue slightly (from £10.0m to £9.5–10.0m) and widen the FY26 adj loss range (from −2.8p towards −1.5 to −3.0p range). The TP of 40p is likely held or marginally trimmed to 35–40p; at 22p the stock already prices significant execution risk. The main watch-point is order book conversion: if the £9.7m of FY26 contracted work delivers on schedule and two to three Training Systems wins arrive in H1 2026, the break-even PBT guide becomes credible. If conversion is delayed by even one quarter, the going concern risk becomes acute. 🏁 PEN is a speculative recovery play: the order book transformation is genuine and the software ARR is growing, but the going concern flag, minimal liquidity, and consecutive year of deteriorating broker estimates make this unsuitable for anything other than a very high risk appetite. Cautious hold at best pending FY26 H1 trading confirmation.

The definitive positive is the planning pipeline: with 19,580 plots in the planning system (up from 13,146) and continued NPPF tailwinds, Hallam Land's medium-term capacity to sustain 3,500+ plot sales per annum is building credibility.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: The upgrade resilience is structurally weak for FY26. SBH's reservation rate improvement (0.43 vs 0.34 prior year) is the only near-term positive signal, but even guiding 200–220 completions in FY26 is below the 240–250 target that itself was below the 600 medium-term ambition. The gearing at 25.7% (above the preferred 10–20%) creates financial constraint on investment pace.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: FY1 EPS (rolling to FY26) likely to be revised DOWN from the current FY2 consensus of 13.1p toward 11–12p to align with the £20.2m PBT guidance. The bull case is the Hallam Land pipeline (medium-term, FY27+) and the eventual SBH recovery — but these are 1–3 year stories, not FY26. 🏁 Verdict: FY25 in-line delivery masks a significant FY26 earnings step-down; brokers need to cut FY26 estimates, and the SBH serial underperformance undermines the growth thesis. Score 38/100.

No explicit upgrade signal; confirms consensus but notably guidance is flat-to-slightly-below FY25 actuals at midpoint.

5. Germany — key growth driver Gamma Germany revenue +103% to £110.2m, gross profit +197% to £78.4m. Organic GP growth 11% constant currency. Cloud seats reached ~600k.

"Gamma Germany increased gross profit by 197% to £78.4m (2024: £26.4m), led by our acquisitions of Placetel in September 2024 and Starface in February 2025."

6. UK SME — headwinds Gross profit declined 3% to £146.5m. PSTN switch-off headwind of ~£4m in FY25, further ~£4m expected in FY26. Ethernet pricing pressure reduced Enterprise GP by ~£2m in FY25, further ~£3m impact expected in FY26.

"We estimate that gross profit will be further reduced by a similar amount in FY 2026, with the full-year financial impact of FY 2026 migrations expected to be felt until the end of FY 2027."

"Gross Margin: 54% (2024: 52%)"

8. Cash returns / capital allocation £64m returned to shareholders in FY25. FY26+FY27 buybacks of up to £85m announced (£42.5m per year), plus dividend fixed at FY25 levels for two years (22.2p/share). Total ~£125m aggregate return over two years.

"We intend to continue to return substantial amounts of cash to shareholders through FY 2026 and FY 2027, balancing investment in organic growth with enhanced cash returns."

9. Net debt Net debt of £9.3m at year-end (2024: net cash £153.7m). Driven by Starface acquisition (£152.2m) and buybacks. RCF £97m undrawn.

10. Restructuring savings UK restructuring completed in H2 2025, delivering £7m p.a. savings from FY26.

"Restructuring programme…will deliver annual operating expense savings of £7m across both Gamma Business and Gamma Enterprise from FY 2026."

4. Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

  • EPS: +1.7% net change over full period (92.7p to 94.3p).
  • Revenue: −1.9% net change (£657.8m to £645.8m).
  • Target price: declined steadily from £17.27 to £14.83 — a -14.1% TP cut over the period.
  • 4-week trend: 🟡 STEADY (flat for ~3 months)
  • Divergence: EPS estimates held or crept up slightly while TP was cut significantly — suggests brokers repriced the growth multiple downward while not cutting numbers materially. The in-line result does not reverse the TP trajectory; FY26 guidance "in line with consensus" rather than ahead removes the catalyst for TP recovery.

5. Structural Flags

  • PSTN headwind (structural but temporary): ~£4m GP drag per year expected through end of 2027. Not a permanent structural change but a multi-year drag.
  • German margin dilution: Starface/Placetel have higher GP margins but also higher opex, meaning EBITDA margin growth is constrained despite GP expansion. "They structurally have higher operating expenses."
  • Interest income reversal: Move from net cash £153.7m to net debt £9.3m eliminates ~£7m annual interest income tailwind vs FY24.
  • CFO transition: Gap between Castell departure (31 March 2026) and new CFO arrival (by September 2026) = 6-month leadership gap.
  • FY26 guidance at midpoint below FY25: Consensus EBITDA midpoint £141.3m vs FY25 actual £141.7m implies flat-to-slight decline. EPS midpoint ~93.3p vs 94.5p actual = slight decline. This is a structural de-rating signal.

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

#1 Driver — FY26 guidance "in line" (not ahead) The single most influential broker note item will be that FY26 guidance is explicitly "within the consensus range" at the exact midpoint, with consensus EPS actually below FY25 actuals (93.3p midpoint vs 94.5p). After a year of 11% EPS growth, guidance for flat-to-down FY26 EPS is the dominant signal. Brokers expecting a re-acceleration narrative will be disappointed. This is the #1 driver of broker tone.

#2 Driver — FY25 in-line delivery + Germany strength FY25 came in spot on — revenue and EBITDA within 0.3% of consensus. Germany's 197% GP growth shows the acquisition thesis is working. This is a positive "beat and confirm" on FY25 but since the bar was exactly met, upgrade risk from this alone is limited. It prevents downgrades on the FY25 number but doesn't catalyse upgrades.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY1 (now FY26) revenue: consensus already at £665.5m; guidance language "in line" means estimates hold; possible minor downside 0–2% if PSTN and ethernet headwinds are explicitly modelled.
  • FY1 EPS: consensus 94.3p (pre-RNS for FY25, now rolling to FY26 at ~93.8p); FY26 guidance "in line with consensus range" of 90.0p–96.6p confirms midpoint ~93.3p — no revision needed, hold.
  • FY2 (FY27) EPS: £93.8p consensus; likely held or very modest trim as PSTN headwinds expected to resolve by end 2027.

Target price and recommendation: Brokers are likely to hold target prices or trim marginally (−5% range) given the steady TP decline from £17.27 to £14.83 already underway. Current upside to £14.83 from 866p is +71%. Despite high numerical upside, the TP drift lower suggests brokers are unwilling to call a recovery catalyst. No recommendation change likely; hold with cautious tone dominates.

Conservative guidance read-through: The RNS says "within the consensus range" — not "comfortable with" or "not less than." This is the most neutral guidance language possible, essentially confirming midpoint expectations. It does not trigger an upgrade cycle; if anything it confirms flat EPS growth for the year ahead, removing the momentum-based bull case.

Key risk: The single largest counter-argument is the multiple compression risk from flat FY26 EPS at the same time as the market is repricing growth stocks. With EPS guidance flat-to-slightly-down and ongoing TP cuts, there is no earnings growth catalyst to arrest de-rating. "We estimate that gross profit will be further reduced by a similar amount in FY 2026." — the PSTN and ethernet headwinds are explicitly quantified and recurring.

Overall tone: 🟡 Neutral / hold and wait

Para 1 — Headline numbers: GAMA delivered FY25 results that were essentially spot on consensus — revenue of £645.8m (+11%, exactly matching FY1 forecast) and adjusted EPS of 94.5p (+11%, a 0.2p beat). Adjusted EBITDA of £141.7m (+13%) landed at the top of the £138–£144.6m consensus range. The definitive catalyst is Germany: Gamma Germany gross profit surged 197% to £78.4m, transforming the group's earnings mix and validating the Starface/Placetel acquisition thesis. This is an unambiguously clean delivery — no misses, no hidden charges, audited results with an unqualified opinion.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: H2 implied revenue of £329.2m and EPS of 46.6p are both roughly 20% above the three-year historical H2 average, confirming that the German contribution is genuinely structural rather than a one-off. However, the H1 seasonal tracking deviation was only +0.2pp on revenue and +1.0pp on EPS — solidly IN LINE rather than ahead, meaning the FY25 beat was earned proportionally rather than through H1 front-loading. The upgrade resilience argument rests on FY26 structural cost savings (£7m UK restructuring annualised) and the Germany growth trajectory, which management guides to "double-digit revenue growth" continuing. The downside risk is contained by the two-year dividend and buyback commitment (up to £125m), which provides a hard floor for the share. The PSTN headwind (~£4m GP drag repeating in FY26) and ethernet pricing pressure (~£3m further in FY26) are explicitly flagged and already in consensus — so they represent known rather than surprise negatives.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: Brokers should make negligible revisions to FY26 EPS (~93.3–93.8p range already in consensus, confirmed by "within the range" guidance). FY1 revenue may be trimmed modestly (0–2%) to reflect the UK headwind quantification, but this is already substantially embedded in the £645.8m→£665.5m FY26 consensus. The consensus TP has been on a steady decline from £17.27 to £14.83 over the past ten months — this reflects a P/E and growth-multiple re-rating rather than earnings estimate cuts. At 866p against a £14.83 TP, there is 71% upside on paper, but broker willingness to chase that gap is limited without a growth re-acceleration narrative. The main watch point is whether brokers feel the FY26 flat-EPS guidance removes the remaining bull case or whether the capital return programme (and potential share count reduction) is sufficient to hold or marginally lift EPS. 🏁 Verdict: In-line FY25 delivery with clean numbers, but flat FY26 guidance and ongoing TP compression make this a neutral hold — brokers will affirm estimates, not upgrade them. Score 57/100.

Para 1 — Headline numbers: MBH delivered FY25 results that were better than the market feared on EPS but not better in quality terms. Adjusted EPS of 7.50p beat the 6.7p consensus by 12%, but this was substantially driven by a 15.9% effective tax rate (vs 25% normalised) due to prior-year tax credits — stripping this out, underlying EPS was closer to 6.1p. Revenue of £68.9m missed £69.0m consensus marginally and declined 1.7% YoY. The primary operational driver of underperformance was a two-week extended Carlton shutdown in Q1 (costing ~3m manufacturing units) and Floren Belgium revenue declining ~20% as housing activity in Belgium remained ~40% below 2022 peak. Adjusted EBITDA of £12.4m was 2.4% below the £12.7m consensus.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: H2 implied revenue of £33.1m is 4.9% below the three-year H2 average (borderline flat classification), reflecting the ongoing market malaise. H2 implied adj EPS of ~4.2p is roughly 19% below the three-year H2 average, though this is distorted by the tax benefit falling in the year. The seasonal tracking deviation was only −0.2pp on EPS and +0.4pp on revenue — IN LINE rather than signalling any directional breakout. The upgrade resilience rests on: (1) Carlton production delay is non-recurring; (2) Watlington closure removes cash-consuming overhead; (3) management's explicit "growth in 2026" statement. However, the FX headwind (GBP stronger vs EUR) is a tangible, ongoing drag on Floren's GBP-reported contribution that is absent from historical baselines. The CFO transition risk is the most unpredictable variable.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: FY26 EPS consensus of 8.4p should be held or modestly trimmed to 7.5–8.5p range once brokers normalise the tax rate — the 7.50p FY25 EPS at a 15.9% tax rate becomes approximately 6.1p on a like-for-like 25% tax basis, making "growth in 2026" against a normalised base more demanding than the headline implies. TP of 135p likely maintained or cut marginally to 125–130p. At 75p, there is 73% upside to TP on paper but the low price reflects sustained earnings disappointments and a challenging European market backdrop. The main watch point is Belgium housing recovery timing and whether the FX headwind persists. 🏁 Verdict: EPS beat is tax-distorted; underlying performance continues to disappoint against pre-2022 peak; Floren structural headwind + CFO instability + FX drag make this a cautious hold. FX-adjusted score 32/100.

PHASE 0B — FX Revenue Check

Bytes Technology Group is a UK/Ireland IT software business. Revenues predominantly GBP. Skip — no FX threshold breach.

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

  • Routing: pre-FY mode (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY results / full-year trading update for FY26 (year ended 28 February 2026). Sharescope data reflects pre-RNS state.
  • FY1 consensus: EPS 21.8p · Revenue £223.6m (note: this is Bytes' "gross profit" equivalent — Bytes reports Revenue as gross profit/net revenue rather than billings)
  • FY2 consensus: EPS 22.7p · Revenue £242.7m
  • Forecast Broker momentum: EPS net change −11.4% (24.6p → 21.8p) — persistent downgrades driven by Microsoft incentive changes. Last-4-week trend: 🔴 FALLING (22.7→21.9→21.9→21.8p — slowly declining). TP cut from 604p to 459p (−24.0%).
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 50.6% of FY = £113.1m · EPS 45.3% of FY = 9.9p
  • Prior-year H1 actuals: Revenue £108.1m · EPS 11.6p (Sharescope current H1 = FY26 H1 = 6mo to Aug 2025)
  • Implied H2 YoY: H2 implied = £223.6m − £108.1m = £115.5m vs prior H2 (FY25 H2): FY25 total = £105.5m+£111.7m = £217.2m implied; H2 = £111.7m → H2 YoY £115.5m vs £111.7m = +3.4%. EPS H2: 21.8p − 11.6p = 10.2p vs prior H2 EPS (FY25 H2 = 24.2p... wait Sharescope shows "1y ago H1/H2 = 12.2/24.2" which looks too high).
  • Note: Sharescope "1y ago H2 = 24.2p" appears to include the R&D/accounting one-off. Per the RNS the FY26 gross profit guidance is c.£167m and operating profit c.£62m. These are the operative figures.
  • FX: N/A

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

RNS type: FY Trading Update (year ended 28 February 2026) — not full results; full results on 12 May 2026

1. Gross profit — in line with October guidance "gross profit of c.£167m" — vs prior year FY25 gross profit. Note: Bytes' Sharescope Revenue consensus £223.6m = gross profit in Bytes' terminology. Actual c.£167m vs consensus £223.6m — this appears to be a substantial miss. However the consensus likely includes billings not gross profit. Need to reconcile: Bytes' Revenue (gross profit) prior year = £108.1m (H1) + £111.7m (H2) = £219.8m — close to the £223.6m consensus. Actual £167m vs £223.6m = −25.3% miss? This can't be right.

Re-reading: The RNS says "double-digit gross invoiced income growth, gross profit of c.£167m and operating profit of c.£62m." The £167m is gross profit. The Sharescope Revenue consensus £223.6m is almost certainly gross invoiced income (total billings/revenue), not gross profit. Bytes reports both. Consensus "revenue" in Sharescope = gross invoiced income (billings). So: gross profit actual c.£167m — needs comparison to consensus gross profit separately from revenue.

From prior year context: FY25 gross profit was £105.5m + £111.7m = £217.2m? No — that's the Sharescope H1/H2 revenue data which for Bytes IS gross profit (net revenue). So actual FY26 gross profit c.£167m vs FY25 gross profit (which = revenue £217.2m approx) = a significant decline? This implies FY26 gross profit DECLINED vs FY25.

The RNS says "double-digit gross invoiced income growth" — so billings grew. But gross profit c.£167m — what was FY25 gross profit? From Sharescope H1 prior = £108.1m (H1 FY26 actual) and FY25 H2 = £111.7m → FY25 total revenue/gross profit = c.£219.8m. So FY26 £167m vs FY25 £219.8m = −24% gross profit decline?

Wait — I need to reconsider the Sharescope data interpretation. The "Current H1" of £108.1m and "1y ago H1/H2 of £105.5m/£111.7m" in Sharescope likely refer to Bytes' own gross profit metric. So FY25 gross profit = £105.5m + £111.7m = £217.2m and FY26 projected £167m would be a −24% decline. But this contradicts the "double-digit gross invoiced income growth" language.

The resolution is: Bytes' "Revenue" in Sharescope = gross invoiced income (billings/revenue per IFRS 15), not the gross profit. So FY1 consensus Revenue £223.6m = gross invoiced income. And gross profit (what matters for earnings) = c.£167m per RNS.

From FY25 reported gross profit (from FY25 annual results): Bytes H1 FY26 = gross profit per their own metric; and "1y ago H1/H2 = 12.2/24.2" are EPS, not revenue. The prior year (FY25) gross profit would be disclosed in the FY25 annual — but from the RNS text: "FY26 was impacted by changes to Microsoft enterprise incentives and the phasing effects of the private sector sales realignment." This implies FY26 gross profit is LOWER than FY25. The "c.£167m" is below what the market was expecting.

Given prior period context and the explicit statement that FY26 was "in line with the outlook provided in October 2025" — the October trading update had already guided to this lower level. So brokers will have already incorporated c.£167m gross profit into their estimates. The Sharescope EPS consensus of 21.8p reflects the October guidance, not the original 24.6p.

"For FY26, BTG delivered results in line with the outlook provided in October 2025 with double-digit gross invoiced income growth, gross profit of c.£167m and operating profit of c.£62m."

2. Operating profit — in line c.£62m — vs FY1 consensus operating profit implied from EPS. Previous FY25 operating profit would be ~£77m (based on prior EPS). So FY26 c.£62m represents a significant decline.

3. Cash conversion — strong "Cash conversion exceeded 100%, with a year-end cash balance of over £98m." Excellent liquidity position.

4. H2 recovery — "performance strengthened in the second half" H2 (Sep 2025–Feb 2026) gross profit grew c.6% YoY against a "strong comparator" — the inflection point after the Microsoft incentive changes stabilised.

"Encouragingly, performance strengthened in the second half, with gross profit growing c.6% year-on-year in January and February 2026 against a strong comparator."

5. FY27 guidance — return to growth "high single-digit to low double-digit percentage growth in gross profit" in FY27 (March 2026–Feb 2027). Operating profit "broadly flat" due to c.£4.5m of cost normalisation. So FY27 gross profit ~£182–185m and operating profit ~£62m.

"For FY27, we expect high single-digit to low double-digit percentage growth in gross profit, with operating profit broadly flat as the Group absorbs c.£4.5m of cost normalisation"

6. Go-to-market realignment from July 2026 Bytes Software Services → private sector; Phoenix Software → public sector. Structural clarity improving. "From July 2026, the Group will further align its go-to-market approach."

Let me use what the company discloses: FY26 (ending Feb 2026) = gross profit c.£167m, operating profit c.£62m. FY27 guidance: gross profit £182–188m (+8–12%), operating profit ~£62m.

The gross profit decline from what appears to be FY25 (ending Feb 2025) gross profit. From the RNS context: "FY26 was impacted by changes to Microsoft enterprise incentives and the phasing effects of the private sector sales realignment." The decline was flagged in October 2025 revised guidance.

Gross profit trajectory: +12.1% (FY24→25) → +4.9% (FY25→26 context) → −23.1% (FY26→27 implied) — this trajectory is 🔴 Decelerating severely.

But FY27 guidance reverses this: +8–12% gross profit growth from FY26 base. So the FY26 year is the trough.

2. Seasonal H1% Baseline and Tracking Deviation (pre-FY mode)

Since this is a FY trading update (not H1 results for next year), the H1 tracking is against FY26 actuals.

H1 FY26 actual = £108.1m (current H1 Sharescope). FY26 actual gross profit c.£167m → H1 represents 64.7% of FY total. vs baseline 50.6% → deviation = 🟢 [+14.1pp] — but this is the FY that just ended, not a forward signal.

For forward H1 FY27 tracking: UNTRACKABLE — no H1 FY27 actuals yet.

3. Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical (pre-FY mode)

H2 FY26 implied = £167m − £108.1m = £58.9m vs H2 FY25 £98.3m → −40.1% — but this reflects the known Microsoft incentive headwind. H2 recovery signal: January/February 2026 showed c.6% gross profit growth YoY — this is the forward indicator for FY27 H1.

For FY27 implied H2: Using FY27 guidance of £182–188m gross profit and assuming similar H1 split: H2 FY27 implied ~£90m vs H2 FY26 £58.9m = +52.7% — but this is from a depressed H2 FY26 base.

🟢 strong H2 FY27 recovery implied by guidance

4. Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

  • EPS: −11.4% over full period — consistent downgrade cycle driven by Microsoft changes
  • TP: −24.0% (604p → 459p) — significant broker confidence reduction
  • 4-week trend: 🔴 FALLING (21.9p → 21.8p — small but directionally negative)
  • Divergence: The declining EPS and TP contrast with the positive recovery narrative in FY27 guidance. The market (300p) vs TP (459p) gap = 53% upside — but the TP has been falling.

5. Structural Flags

  • Microsoft incentive changes — one-time reset completed: The FY26 impact is now fully crystallised. FY27 grows from the new lower base. The c.6% H2 FY26 growth in gross profit signals the bottom has been reached.
  • Operating profit flat in FY27 despite gross profit growth: £4.5m cost normalisation (higher tech costs, return to normal bonus levels) absorbs the gross profit recovery. This limits EPS recovery in FY27.
  • Go-to-market restructuring risk: The July 2026 private/public sector split creates execution risk during transition.

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

#1 Driver — FY26 in line with October guidance — no surprise (positive or negative) Results exactly match the October 2025 pre-announced guidance. No new information on FY26 fundamentals. The broker focus is entirely on FY27: "high single-digit to low double-digit gross profit growth" is the key number.

#2 Driver — FY27 gross profit recovery (+8–12%) but operating profit flat The £4.5m cost normalisation in FY27 means gross profit growth does NOT flow through to operating profit. This constrains EPS recovery — FY27 EPS likely similar to FY26 (~21–23p). Brokers will not significantly upgrade FY27 EPS despite the top-line recovery.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY1 (FY27) EPS: consensus 22.7p — likely maintained or very minor uplift (0–3%) given operating profit flat guidance.
  • FY1 gross profit: FY2 consensus £242.7m likely maintained (consistent with +8–12% guidance on £167m base = £180–188m — FY2 consensus appears to be FY27 as a higher base).
  • TP: Currently 459p; likely to be maintained. Some recovery from 300p stock price toward 400–450p as the trough is confirmed.

Key risk: The "broadly flat operating profit" for FY27 despite gross profit recovery is the critical constraint. And the go-to-market restructuring in July 2026 introduces execution uncertainty.

Overall tone: 🟡 Neutral / hold and wait

  • PSTN headwind (structural but temporary): ~£4m GP drag per year expected through end of 2027. Not a permanent structural change but a multi-year drag.
  • German margin dilution: Starface/Placetel have higher GP margins but also higher opex, meaning EBITDA margin growth is constrained despite GP expansion. "They structurally have higher operating expenses."
  • Interest income reversal: Move from net cash £153.7m to net debt £9.3m eliminates ~£7m annual interest income tailwind vs FY24.
  • CFO transition: Gap between Castell departure (31 March 2026) and new CFO arrival (by September 2026) = 6-month leadership gap.
  • FY26 guidance at midpoint below FY25: Consensus EBITDA midpoint £141.3m vs FY25 actual £141.7m implies flat-to-slight decline. EPS midpoint ~93.3p vs 94.5p actual = slight decline. This is a structural de-rating signal.

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

#1 Driver — FY26 guidance "in line" (not ahead) The single most influential broker note item will be that FY26 guidance is explicitly "within the consensus range" at the exact midpoint, with consensus EPS actually below FY25 actuals (93.3p midpoint vs 94.5p). After a year of 11% EPS growth, guidance for flat-to-down FY26 EPS is the dominant signal. Brokers expecting a re-acceleration narrative will be disappointed. This is the #1 driver of broker tone.

#2 Driver — FY25 in-line delivery + Germany strength FY25 came in spot on — revenue and EBITDA within 0.3% of consensus. Germany's 197% GP growth shows the acquisition thesis is working. This is a positive "beat and confirm" on FY25 but since the bar was exactly met, upgrade risk from this alone is limited. It prevents downgrades on the FY25 number but doesn't catalyse upgrades.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY1 (now FY26) revenue: consensus already at £665.5m; guidance language "in line" means estimates hold; possible minor downside 0–2% if PSTN and ethernet headwinds are explicitly modelled.
  • FY1 EPS: consensus 94.3p (pre-RNS for FY25, now rolling to FY26 at ~93.8p); FY26 guidance "in line with consensus range" of 90.0p–96.6p confirms midpoint ~93.3p — no revision needed, hold.
  • FY2 (FY27) EPS: £93.8p consensus; likely held or very modest trim as PSTN headwinds expected to resolve by end 2027.

Target price and recommendation: Brokers are likely to hold target prices or trim marginally (−5% range) given the steady TP decline from £17.27 to £14.83 already underway. Current upside to £14.83 from 866p is +71%. Despite high numerical upside, the TP drift lower suggests brokers are unwilling to call a recovery catalyst. No recommendation change likely; hold with cautious tone dominates.

Conservative guidance read-through: The RNS says "within the consensus range" — not "comfortable with" or "not less than." This is the most neutral guidance language possible, essentially confirming midpoint expectations. It does not trigger an upgrade cycle; if anything it confirms flat EPS growth for the year ahead, removing the momentum-based bull case.

Key risk: The single largest counter-argument is the multiple compression risk from flat FY26 EPS at the same time as the market is repricing growth stocks. With EPS guidance flat-to-slightly-down and ongoing TP cuts, there is no earnings growth catalyst to arrest de-rating. "We estimate that gross profit will be further reduced by a similar amount in FY 2026." — the PSTN and ethernet headwinds are explicitly quantified and recurring.

Overall tone: 🟡 Neutral / hold and wait

The main watch point is whether brokers feel the FY26 flat-EPS guidance removes the remaining bull case or whether the capital return programme (and potential share count reduction) is sufficient to hold or marginally lift EPS. 🏁 Verdict: In-line FY25 delivery with clean numbers, but flat FY26 guidance and ongoing TP compression make this a neutral hold — brokers will affirm estimates, not upgrade them. Para 1 — Headline numbers: MBH delivered FY25 results that were better than the market feared on EPS but not better in quality terms. Adjusted EPS of 7.50p beat the 6.7p consensus by 12%, but this was substantially driven by a 15.9% effective tax rate (vs 25% normalised) due to prior-year tax credits — stripping this out, underlying EPS was closer to 6.1p. Revenue of £68.9m missed £69.0m consensus marginally and declined 1.7% YoY. The primary operational driver of underperformance was a two-week extended Carlton shutdown in Q1 (costing ~3m manufacturing units) and Floren Belgium revenue declining ~20% as housing activity in Belgium remained ~40% below 2022 peak. Adjusted EBITDA of £12.4m was 2.4% below the £12.7m consensus.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: H2 implied revenue of £33.1m is 4.9% below the three-year H2 average (borderline flat classification), reflecting the ongoing market malaise. H2 implied adj EPS of ~4.2p is roughly 19% below the three-year H2 average, though this is distorted by the tax benefit falling in the year. The seasonal tracking deviation was only −0.2pp on EPS and +0.4pp on revenue — IN LINE rather than signalling any directional breakout. The upgrade resilience rests on: (1) Carlton production delay is non-recurring; (2) Watlington closure removes cash-consuming overhead; (3) management's explicit "growth in 2026" statement. However, the FX headwind (GBP stronger vs EUR) is a tangible, ongoing drag on Floren's GBP-reported contribution that is absent from historical baselines. The CFO transition risk is the most unpredictable variable.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: FY26 EPS consensus of 8.4p should be held or modestly trimmed to 7.5–8.5p range once brokers normalise the tax rate — the 7.50p FY25 EPS at a 15.9% tax rate becomes approximately 6.1p on a like-for-like 25% tax basis, making "growth in 2026" against a normalised base more demanding than the headline implies. TP of 135p likely maintained or cut marginally to 125–130p. At 75p, there is 73% upside to TP on paper but the low price reflects sustained earnings disappointments and a challenging European market backdrop. The main watch point is Belgium housing recovery timing and whether the FX headwind persists. 🏁 Verdict: EPS beat is tax-distorted; underlying performance continues to disappoint against pre-2022 peak; Floren structural headwind + CFO instability + FX drag make this a cautious hold. FX-adjusted score 32/100.

  • New dividend policy (1x EPS): The 23.3p/share dividend at a 294p stock price = 7.9% dividend yield — exceptional for a growth company. This fundamentally changes the investor base and re-rates the valuation framework.
  • Claims ratio improvement: 27.1% (2024: 29.1%) — lower-than-expected claims directly boost underwriting profit margin. This is partially structural (better risk selection) and partially volatile.

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

#1 Driver — EPS 23.3p vs consensus 20.2p: +15.3% beat This is a material beat that will dominate broker notes. The combination of higher insurance premiums, lower claims ratio, R&D tax credit, and operating leverage drove the outperformance. Brokers will need to upgrade FY26 EPS estimates materially — prior FY2 consensus of 24.8p now looks too low given the 23.3p base.

#2 Driver — 41% dividend increase + ARR £48.6m exit run rate The dividend raise to match EPS (23.3p/share = 7.9% yield at 294p) is a powerful capital return statement. Combined with ARR at £48.6m already exceeding FY25 revenue, brokers will upgrade their FY26 revenue estimates with high confidence. The Simplyhealth partnership post-period provides an additional new distribution channel catalyst.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY1 (FY26) EPS: consensus currently ~24.8p (FY2 pre-results); given FY25 base of 23.3p and ARR growth of 12% supporting similar revenue trajectory, FY26 EPS likely upgraded to 27–28p (+8–15% vs prior FY2 consensus).
  • FY1 (FY26) revenue: prior FY2 consensus £54.5m. ARR exit of £48.6m + expected new business growth implies £52–55m; broadly confirmed.
  • TP: Currently 416p; likely to move toward 450–500p post-results given the earnings upgrade cycle and yield re-rating.

Conservative guidance: Company provides no specific FY26 numerical guidance, but "entered 2026 with strong momentum" + ARR visibility + Simplyhealth partnership = strongly constructive qualitative guidance. The 2030 aspirations (£100m revenue, £30m EBITDA) anchor a long-term upgrade path. This is an emerging growth upgrade cycle.

Also, the UK insurance market is competitive and new digital insurance products (hospital cover, death plan) being tested are not yet in revenue.

Para 1 — Headline numbers: PGH delivered an exceptional FY25 with adjusted EBITDA of £12.1m (+22%), explicitly "ahead of market expectations" of £11.6m, and EPS of 23.3p — a 15.3% beat against the 20.2p consensus. The #1 catalyst was the combination of a record insurance sales year (API +12% to £40.5m, new sales +11% to £15.4m), a claims ratio improvement to 27.1% from 29.1% boosting underwriting margin, and operating leverage across both Insurance and Benefits & Reward. Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: The structural driver protecting the upgrade thesis is ARR of £48.6m exiting FY25 — higher than FY25's total reported revenue of £48.4m. This means over 90% of FY26 revenue is already contractually secured, making the upgrade story a matter of how much growth is added on top of a highly visible base. H2 implied EPS of 14.1p (+48% above the 2yr historical H2 average) confirms the earnings power has structurally stepped up. The insurance business reached penetration of 14.5% in top 100 sites (up from 13.0%), a key operational KPI showing continued organic progress. The Simplyhealth partnership (post-period end) adds access to 12,000 business relationships as a new distribution channel not in any current FY26 estimate.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: FY26 EPS should be upgraded from the current FY2 consensus of ~24.8p toward 27–28p range, reflecting the higher 23.3p base, the ARR growth trajectory and the Simplyhealth incremental opportunity. The FY26 revenue consensus of £54.5m is broadly achievable — ARR growing at 12% against a £48.6m exit base implies ~£54m naturally before new sales. TP should move from 416p toward 450–500p range. At 294p, the stock offers an estimated 7.9% yield plus earnings growth — an unusual and compelling combination for an AIM-listed growth company. The key watch point is FY26 guidance confirmation and the success of the new digital insurance products in testing. 🏁 Verdict: Exceptional beat across all metrics with ARR visibility making FY26 upgrades a near-certainty; dividend re-rating and Simplyhealth partnership add incremental positive drivers. Score 88/100.

Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY results. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

PHASE 0B — FX Revenue Check

S4Capital generates ~80% of revenue from the Americas (USD exposure) and ~15% from EMEA (EUR). USD exposure ~80% of revenue > 30% threshold. Running FX check.

Searched the web

GBP/USD spot rate today: ~1.3413. S4Capital's FY25 RNS discloses results in GBP. The key FX question is whether GBP was stronger or weaker vs USD in FY25 vs prior year average rate.

From the RNS: S4Capital's financial statements show results in GBP sterling. The RNS mentions the like-for-like FX impact on net revenue was −£19.7m (restating FY24 at FY25 rates), meaning GBP was stronger vs prior year average rates in FY25 on a net basis — a headwind. The RNS states like-for-like net revenue declined 8.4% vs reported 10.8% — the FX impact was ~2.4% additional reported drag. This confirms GBP strengthened vs USD during FY25 on average.

S4Capital's FY25 average rate not explicitly disclosed but the Americas (~80% USD) exposure is clear. Prior year FX adjustment of £19.7m on £754.6m net revenue ≈ 2.6% — modest. However, the FX impact on FY26 guidance matters more for the scorecard. GBP/USD is currently ~1.34; in early 2025 it was ~1.25–1.27. So GBP has strengthened ~5–7% YoY. With 80% Americas USD exposure: GBP stronger >3c vs prior avg → this is a headwind scenario.

Exposure: 80% (Americas USD) → 50%+ band → headwind (GBP stronger >3c) = −11 to −12 pts. However, management guides ex-FX and the business reports like-for-like, so reducing the boost calculation is standard. But the PENALTY band applies. Given GBP is around 5–7% stronger on average and exposure is 80%+, applying −11 pts (50%+ / headwind >3c, at the conservative end since the company guides ex-FX).

FX Rule 1 applied (−11 pts) · 80% USD · 🔴 GBP headwind

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 47.6% of FY = £328.7m · EPS H1% cannot be reliably calculated (consistent H1 losses in PBT; use EBITDA-based). Using adjusted EPS H1 baseline, H1 is typically ~23.7% of FY.
  • Prior-year H1 actuals: Revenue £422.5m (Sharescope 1y ago H1) · EPS ~1.2p adjusted (1y ago H1)
  • Implied H2 YoY (pre-FY — FY actual vs prior FY): Revenue actual £754.8m vs prior (FY24) £848.2m = −11.0% FY YoY. vs FY1 consensus £690.5m = revenue beat of +9.3% (significant). Adjusted EPS actual 5.0p vs FY1 consensus 4.2p = +0.8p beat (+19.0%).
  • FX: 🔴 GBP headwind — 80% USD exposure, GBP stronger ~5–7% vs prior avg. FX Rule 1 applied (−11 pts)

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

RNS type: FY Results (year ended 31 December 2025)

1. Revenue — FY actual Net revenue £673.0m (−10.8% reported, −8.4% like-for-like). vs FY1 consensus revenue £690.5m → −£17.5m miss (−2.5%) on net revenue. However, vs reported revenue £754.8m vs consensus £690.5m — the consensus appears to refer to net revenue (ex direct costs). Clarifying: FY1 Revenue consensus in Sharescope = £690.5m which matches "net revenue" in S4Capital's own metrics. Actual net revenue £673.0m vs consensus £690.5m = −2.5% miss. But the RNS says "ahead of the revised guidance issued on 24 November 2025" — so the miss is vs the original consensus, not the revised guidance.

"Reported net revenue £673.0 million, down 10.8%, ahead of the revised guidance issued on 24 November 2025."

2. Adjusted EPS — beats revised guidance, misses original consensus Adjusted basic EPS 5.0p (2024: 5.2p), −3.8%. vs FY1 original consensus 4.2p = +0.8p beat (+19.0%). Wait — Sharescope shows FY1 EPS consensus at 4.2p, but the Sharescope snapshot was updated during the year as estimates were cut. The actual 5.0p vs Sharescope's 4.2p = significant beat vs pre-RNS consensus.

"Adjusted basic earnings per share 5.0p, down 3.8% versus 5.2p per share in the prior year."

3. Operational EBITDA — in-line with revised guidance £81.2m (−7.5% reported, −3.2% LFL). vs revised guidance "in line." vs Sharescope FY1 EBITDA consensus £80.5m = +£0.7m beat (+0.9%) — essentially in-line.

"Operational EBITDA was in line with revised guidance at £81.2 million"

4. Operational EBITDA margin 12.1% vs 11.6% in FY24 — +50bps margin expansion. Like-for-like +70bps. Despite revenue decline, cost management improved margins.

"Operational EBITDA margin improved by 50 basis points on a reported basis and 70 basis points like-for-like, to 12.1%."

5. Net debt — significantly better than targeted range Year-end net debt £86.9m vs targeted range £100–140m. Better by £13–53m vs guidance. Leverage improved to 1.1x (vs targeted range).

"Year end net debt at £86.9 million, below targeted range of £100 million to £140 million with leverage improved to 1.1x net debt/operational EBITDA"

6. FY26 guidance — revenue slightly below 2025 LFL, margin +100bps "2026 like-for-like net revenue expected to be in line with current analyst consensus, slightly below 2025." Consensus shows FY2 (FY26) revenue £671.2m. Operational EBITDA margin targeted to increase by "at least 100 basis points." Implies FY26 EBITDA ~£87–90m vs FY25 £81.2m.

"2026 like-for-like net revenue expected to be in line with current analyst consensus, slightly below 2025, with operational EBITDA margin targeted to increase by at least 100 basis points"

7. Q1 FY26 — Middle East conflict impact "We expect like-for-like net revenue to be down for the first quarter, in part due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East." H1 FY26 EBITDA expected to be higher proportion of FY total vs H1 FY25 (due to annualised cost actions). H2 FY26 expected improvement.

8. Free cash flow — strong at £86.5m FCF £86.5m (FY24: £37.8m) — a £48.7m improvement driven by working capital discipline. This funds the debt buyback and supports FY26 deleveraging to £60–90m target.

"The Group generated free cash flow of £86.5 million, an increase of £48.7 million compared to 2024."

9. Tech client headwinds confirmed structural Technology clients (~41% of net revenue, down from 45% in FY24) continuing to prioritise AI capex over marketing opex. Technology Services net revenue −29.9% LFL.

1. HoH Growth Pattern

Due to S4Capital's consistent H1 losses on statutory PBT and the H2-weighted business, HoH analysis on EPS is not reliable. Revenue H1 split:

2. Seasonal H1% Baseline (pre-FY mode)

  • Revenue baseline: 47.6% × £690.5m = £328.7m. H1 actual £360.4m ÷ £673.0m = 53.5% — but this is H1 as % of actual FY, not consensus. H1 actual £360.4m ÷ £690.5m (consensus FY) = 52.2% vs baseline 47.6% → deviation = 🟢 [+4.6pp] → 🟢 STRONG BUY signal on revenue... but wait: in the context of a declining revenue business, this signals H1 beat vs consensus which is broadly what happened (full year £673m vs £690.5m consensus = miss, but H1 was front-loaded).

Actually for a declining revenue business the interpretation is complex. H1 was £360.4m vs consensus H1 implied £328.7m = H1 outperformed expectations materially, but H2 came in at £312.6m vs implied H2 £361.8m = H2 missed. Net effect: full year miss vs original consensus but beat vs revised guidance.

This metric is UNTRACKABLE in a clean sense for SFOR given the revenue trend — flagged accordingly.

  • EPS baseline: 23.7% × 4.2p = 1.0p. H1 actual ~0.2p (Sharescope current H1 EPS = 0.2p) → EPS UNTRACKABLE due to H1 losses on adjusted basis in S4Capital. Flag as UNTRACKABLE.

3. Implied H2 Momentum

H2 implied net revenue £312.6m vs 3yr avg H2 = (£623.1m + £494.4m + £332.1m) / 3 = £483.2m → −35.3% → 🔴 severe (though distorted by the scale decline from FY22 peaks)

Using just last 2yr avg H2: (£494.4m + £332.1m)/2 = £413.3m → H2 £312.6m = −24.4% → 🔴 weak/severe. However the rate of deterioration slowed vs H1 (−5.9% H2 vs −14.7% H1) which is the constructive read.

4. Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

  • EPS: −16.0% over full period — consistent series of downgrades
  • TP: −42.6% (47p → 27p) — material downgrade in broker confidence
  • 4-week trend: FLAT (stabilising after FY revision in November)
  • Divergence: No positive divergence — estimates and TP both declined, stock at 19.74p is already below the 27p TP, suggesting the market has priced in even worse than broker consensus.

5. Structural Flags

  • Technology client structural headwind: ~41% of revenue from tech clients prioritising AI capex. This shows no sign of reversing in FY26 guidance ("slightly below 2025").
  • Term loan maturity August 2028: €349.3m remaining after recent buyback. Refinancing risk is moderate given 2.5yr runway but material.
  • Margin recovery trajectory: The "at least +100bps" FY26 target and the longer-term 20% EBITDA margin aspiration are the bull case anchors.
  • Middle East conflict new risk: Q1 FY26 revenue expected down partly due to the conflict. Additional macro risk not in original FY26 estimates.

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

#1 Driver — Revenue miss vs original consensus (−2.5%) but beat revised guidance Brokers will focus on the divergence between: the November 2025 revised guidance (beaten) and the original consensus (missed). The market sentiment will depend on whether analysts had already adopted the revised guidance. Given Sharescope EPS consensus stabilised at 4.2p (vs actual 5.0p), and the net revenue consensus was £690.5m (vs actual £673.0m), the EPS beat (+19%) is more impactful than the revenue miss (−2.5%).

#2 Driver — FY26 guidance: revenue slightly below FY25, margin +100bps This is the tone-setter. Revenue guided "slightly below 2025" on LFL basis — the Sharescope FY2 consensus already shows £671.2m (−2.9% vs FY25 £673.0m LFL). No surprise on revenue. But the margin commitment (+100bps to ~13.2%) with free cash flow improvement creates an EBITDA upgrade story despite flat/declining revenue. FY26 EBITDA should move toward £85–88m from £81.2m.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY1 (FY26) adj EPS: FY2 consensus ~5.0p will be maintained or modestly upgraded toward 5.2–5.5p as margin expands.
  • FY1 revenue: £671.2m consensus confirmed by guidance. No change.
  • TP: 27p is current; likely to hold or see very modest uplift. The stock at 19.74p is below TP — some re-rating possible if management delivers on margin.

Conservative guidance: The "at least 100bps" margin improvement language could be read as conservative (cost actions already taken). But "slightly below 2025" revenue is not bullish. The net cash debt buyback (€25.7m at discount post-period) is a positive capital management signal.

Key risk: The Middle East conflict is explicitly cited as a Q1 FY26 headwind, and the statement that revenue is "in line with current analyst consensus" (not ahead) removes any near-term upside catalyst. "We expect like-for-like net revenue to be down for the first quarter, in part due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East."

Overall tone: 🟡 Neutral / hold and wait

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

Para 1 — Headline numbers: SFOR delivered FY25 results that beat the November-revised guidance but missed the original broker consensus: net revenue of £673.0m (−10.8%) missed the pre-RNS consensus of £690.5m by 2.5%, while adjusted EPS of 5.0p beat the Sharescope consensus of 4.2p by 19% due to better-than-expected margin delivery. The #1 broker focus will be the adjusted EPS beat, but it is tempered by the revenue disappointment. The dominant positive is net debt of £86.9m — well below the £100–140m guidance range — and FCF of £86.5m (+£48.7m YoY), demonstrating the business is a strong cash generator even in a declining revenue environment.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: The H2 revenue deceleration rate (−5.9% H2 vs −14.7% H1) confirms the business is bottoming out rather than accelerating downward — the new business wins with Asana, Samsung, T-Mobile, Amazon and others are phasing into H2. The EBITDA margin expansion (+50bps to 12.1% reported, +70bps LFL) is structural — reflecting headcount at 6,345 (−11.5% YoY) and disciplined cost management. The FX adjustment is significant: with GBP approximately 5–7% stronger vs USD in FY25 vs FY24 average, the 80% Americas exposure creates a structural earnings headwind in the reported numbers. FX adjusted raw score from 43 to 32. The "at least 100bps" FY26 margin target is achievable given annualised 2025 cost actions already implemented.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: FY26 adjusted EPS consensus of ~5.0p (FY2 pre-results) should be maintained or marginally upgraded toward 5.2–5.5p as the margin improvement flows through on flat revenue. The TP at 27p (down from 47p over the period) could see marginal recovery — target range 27–32p. Stock at 19.74p is already 27% below TP, suggesting the market has front-run the bad news. The Middle East conflict is the key new watch point for Q1 FY26 revenue; if it escalates and client spending further deteriorates, the +100bps margin target becomes the only upside lever. 🏁 Verdict: Revenue declining business with excellent cash management; FX headwind (-11pts) weighs heavily on the score despite the EPS beat. Cautious hold with modest upgrade potential on margin story. Score 32/100.

#2 Driver — Accounting reference date change complicates forecasting The move to a September year-end means FY26 is a 9-month stub period. Brokers will need to re-forecast on a different time basis. This introduces uncertainty and may delay analyst updates.

Key risk: The dividend suspension removes any income floor. The leverage at 2.8x (up from 2.2x) against a declining EBITDA is a financial risk. "The Board has made the decision to continue to pause dividend payments in light of the impact of the Group's weaker financial performance."

Para 1 — Headline numbers: TMG delivered FY25 results that missed the already-heavily-downgraded consensus: headline EPS from continuing operations of 2.0p vs the consensus 3.0p — a 33% miss. The headline operating profit of £5.1m (−34% YoY) and operating margin of 7.4% (2024: 10.3%) confirm the business has not yet stabilised. The reported loss of £18.8m was dominated by a £15.7m goodwill impairment — the largest single red flag, signalling that prior acquisitions are worth materially less than carrying value. Revenue at £68.5m is broadly in-line with the downgraded consensus but still −7.6% below the prior year.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: The upgrade resilience case is weak. The £4.0m annualised cost savings provide a mechanical earnings recovery in FY26 — adding approximately 3–4p of EPS on a 12-month basis. However, the 9-month FY26 stub period (September year-end) means only ~3p of this is captured in the next financial year. Revenue visibility is limited given the "Client caution" theme extends into early 2026. There is no order book or ARR equivalent to provide hard forward visibility, and the Sports & Entertainment segment (the only growth area in FY25, with +8% revenue) is modest in scale. The leverage ratio of 2.8x heading into FY26 on declining EBITDA is a constraint on investment and shareholder returns.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: FY1 EPS consensus of 3.0p will likely be cut toward 2.0–2.5p as brokers absorb the FY25 miss and the accounting reference date complexity. TP likely cut from 55p toward 40–50p. The stock at 18.5p already prices in significant distress — the 197% upside gap to TP will narrow as the TP is cut rather than the stock re-rating. The main watch point is whether the CEO's strategic reset (simplified structure, AI investment, US Sports growth) can deliver a meaningful FY27 profit recovery when comparing on a 12-month basis. 🏁 Verdict: Material miss vs revised consensus, goodwill impairment, suspended dividend and accounting year change create multiple headwinds; downgrades and possible TP cuts incoming. Score 22/100.

6. Full-year guidance — FY26 adjusted operating profit £52–56m vs FY1 consensus implied EBITDA £91.7m... wait. The £52–56m is adjusted operating profit, not EBITDA. Reconciling: Sharescope EPS consensus 33.0p implies PBT roughly £38.5m; adjusted operating profit £52–56m vs prior FY (FY25) adjusted operating profit £60.7m — the guidance implies a significant FY26 decline.

"Considering the incremental investment in Shopper of £6m, the Group expects FY26 adjusted operating profit to be £52-£56m."

"Combined impact of the first two waves expected to deliver annualised margin uplift in excess of 350bps"

"Board therefore continues to actively consider actions that could enhance the strategic positioning of Shopper and unlock long-term shareholder value."

If Shopper is sold (at FY24 acquisition price of ~£280m or even at a discount), the proceeds could fund debt repayment + buyback, dramatically simplifying the business and improving EPS quality.

The company acknowledges the £6m incremental FY26 investment explicitly and provides FY26 guidance of adjusted operating profit £52–56m — materially below the ~£62m implied by the FY1 consensus of 33.0p EPS.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: The upgrade resilience is extremely limited for FY26, with the EPS cut inevitable as guidance implies ~27–30p vs 33.0p consensus. PHASE 0B — FX Revenue Check

The primary driver is adjusted gross margin of 48.5% (+330bps YoY), which is already at the guided full-year range of 48–50% after just H1. Combined with total fixed cost reduction of >10% YoY and supply chain cost-to-serve improvement of 150bps, ASOS is demonstrating that its operating model restructuring is generating tangible financial leverage even while revenues remain under pressure. FY26 EBITDA guidance of £150m–£180m was reiterated (not raised) — suggesting management is deliberately conservative and the probability of a guidance upgrade at the H1 results (imminent) is material.

Para 2 — H1 tracking signal and upgrade resilience: The H1 revenue tracking signal of +2.9pp above the 51.5% seasonal baseline (£1,299.4m vs £1,230.8m expected) fired a Strong Buy signal — the first positive tracking signal for ASOS in several years. BMS — Braemar PLC

Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as pre-FY trading update (year ended 28 February 2026, results due end of May 2026). Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

PHASE 0B — FX Revenue Check

Braemar is a shipping broker — revenues denominated in USD (shipping commissions), GBP (some UK broking) and other currencies. The RNS does not contain a Currency Movements section with explicit percentage breakdowns. Revenue ~£135m; prior-year £141.9m. No formal Currency Movements table present. Braemar's forward order book is quoted in USD ($72.5m), suggesting significant USD exposure. However, without explicit disclosure of >30% single currency exposure, Phase 0B criteria are not met by the RNS disclosure rules. Phase 0B not triggered. No penalty. Note: USD strength/weakness will be relevant to broker modelling but not scorable here.

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

5. Structural/One-Off Flags

[Shipping market cyclicality]: Braemar's revenue is highly correlated to shipping market activity. Lower bulk carrier/tanker/LNG chartering volumes directly reduce commission income. The order book of $72.5m (down 11.8% vs $82.2m prior year) is a forward indicator of likely FY27 revenue pressure.

[Middle East conflict — asymmetric effects]: Increased rates benefit brokers via higher commission values; lower volumes reduce transaction count. Net effect uncertain — board acknowledges uncertainty.

#1 Driver — Operating profit exactly in-line at £13.2m, revenue +2.3% beat: For Braemar, after a year of downgraded estimates, an in-line result with a modest revenue beat is the best plausible outcome. No profit warning. H2 recovery materialised as guided (H2 stronger than H1). This is a "relief" note rather than an upgrade note.

#2 Driver — Forward order book −11.8% YoY ($72.5m vs $82.2m): The order book decline signals FY27 revenue will be under pressure. With FY26 revenue already declining −4.9% YoY, a further decline in FY27 is probable if the order book trend continues. This limits any TP or EPS upgrade.

Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY results accordingly. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

PHASE 0B — FX Revenue Check

Eurowag reports in EUR (€). The Sharescope consensus revenue figure is in EUR (€327.5m FY1). Revenue is pan-European with CZK, PLN, EUR, RON exposure. The company's functional currency is EUR. GBP-listed but EUR-reporting. From the RNS: net revenue €330.1m; no formal GBP Currency Movements section exists as the company reports entirely in EUR. The Sharescope EPS data is in pence (5.8p), implying a GBP/EUR translation into pence — the primary FX sensitivity is GBP/EUR for UK investors, but this is a translation effect, not a revenue exposure in the traditional sense.

No single non-GBP currency exceeds 30% in the traditional sense applicable to GBP-reporting companies. Phase 0B not applicable (EUR-reporting company). No penalty.

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

  • FY2 consensus: EPS 7.1p · Revenue €362.2m

  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 49.7% of FY = €162.7m · EPS 46.8% of FY = 2.7p
  • Prior-year H1 actuals (1y ago): Revenue €1,149.7m (gross; net not split) · EPS 2.5p. Note: Sharescope revenue data for EWG appears to show gross revenue (€1,149.7m H1 vs €327.5m FY net consensus) — the H1 split data is on a gross/net mixed basis. Using the net revenue basis from the RNS: FY25 net revenue = €330.1m; H1/H2 split not disclosed in this annual RNS.
  • Implied H2 YoY (pre-FY mode): Insufficient clean H1/H2 net revenue split available from Sharescope data (gross/net mismatch). EPS: FY1 consensus 5.8p − H1 actual 2.9p = implied H2 2.9p vs prior H2 2.1p → +38.1% YoY — H2 must deliver material step-up vs H1.
  • FX: N/A — EUR-reporting company, Phase 0B methodology not applicable.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

RNS type: FY Results (Preliminary results for year ended 31 December 2025)

1. Net Revenue — FY actual vs consensus

FY 2025 net revenue: €330.1m, up 12.9% vs €292.5m in FY2024.

vs FY1 consensus of €327.5m: beat of €2.6m (+0.8%) — small beat, in line.

Payment solutions net revenue: €200.4m (+20.1%). Mobility solutions: €129.7m (+3.3%).

"Total net revenue increased +12.9% to €330.1 million (FY 2024: €292.5 million)."

2. EPS / Earnings — FY actual vs consensus

Adjusted basic EPS: 4.83 cents per share (GBP pence equivalent ~3.6p at 1.35 EUR/GBP).

Basic statutory EPS: 0.30 cents.

vs FY1 consensus of 5.8p: The adjusted EPS of 4.83c = ~3.6p at current rates — a miss of ~−2.2p (−38%) vs Sharescope consensus. However, this requires careful reconciliation.

EPS quality check / Critical issue: The Sharescope EPS consensus of 5.8p is in pence. Eurowag's adjusted EPS is reported in euro cents (4.83 cents). At GBP/EUR of ~1.20 (implied by consensus translation), 4.83c = ~4.0p. At spot GBP/EUR of 1.17 (from RNS exchange note context): 4.83c / 1.17 = ~4.13p. Either way, the 4.83c adjusted EPS translates to approximately 4.0–4.2p vs Sharescope consensus 5.8p.

This appears to be a significant miss. However: (a) Sharescope consensus may have embedded a different GBP/EUR assumption, (b) the company distinguishes adjusted EPS (4.83c) from statutory (0.30c) — the windfall tax (€5.3m) is the key driver of the statutory miss. On adjusted basis at 4.83c this appears below the pre-RNS pence consensus. 🚨 Windfall tax €5.3m is one-off (Czech Republic, applicable 2023–2025 only) and excluded from adjusted EPS. However, adjusted effective tax rate is 34.8% vs prior 30.3% — high ongoing tax burden even ex-windfall. Restated adjusted EPS at 30.3% normalised rate: adjusted PBT €51.4m × (1−30.3%) = €35.8m ÷ 691.4m shares = 5.18c = ~3.8–4.3p in GBP pence. Still below the 5.8p consensus. The miss vs consensus appears genuine on an FX-adjusted basis.

3. Adjusted EBITDA

Adjusted EBITDA: €132.1m (+8.5% vs €121.7m). Margin: 40.0% (2024: 41.6%), -1.6pp — margin declined due to higher employee expenses (+19.3% adjusted). Cash EBITDA: €98.0m (+10.5%).

"Adjusted EBITDA increased +8.5% to €132.1 million (FY 2024: €121.7 million), with Adjusted EBITDA margin of 40.0% (FY 2024: 41.6%)."

4. Net debt / deleveraging

Net debt reduced to €216.2m (2024: €275.5m). Net leverage: 1.9x (2024: 2.3x) — now within target 1.5–2.5x range. Significant balance sheet improvement.

"Net leverage at 1.9x (FY 2024: 2.3x)."

5. FY26 guidance

Low double-digit net revenue growth (consistent with recent trajectory). Adjusted EBITDA margin ~40%. Adjusted cash EBITDA €105–115m (2025: €98m, +7.1–17.3%). Capex below €50m cap. Leverage <2.0x. Second special dividend of 1.5p per share (~€12m) pending AGM.

"We remain confident in our ability to deliver in line with market expectations for FY 2026."

6. Eurowag Office platform

35% of customers now actively using platform. Majority of customers to be migrated by end-2026. NPS improved to 43.8 (2024: 40.0). Total active trucks +6.4% to 321,500.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

  • Guidance phrase: "remain confident in our ability to deliver in line with market expectations for FY 2026" — explicit in-line language. Numeric: cash EBITDA €105–115m range. Covers one year. No upgrade language.
  • The FY25 results show EBITDA growth of 8.5% with margin -1.6pp; guidance for FY26 is in-line with market expectations — no upgrade trigger.
  • Classification: 🟡 In-line — management explicitly guides in-line with expectations; cash EBITDA range of €105–115m is quantified but as a range consistent with consensus. Provisional points: +1.
  • Divergence check: FY25 net revenue +0.8% beat, adjusted EPS apparent miss vs GBP consensus. Outlook in-line. The apparent EPS miss + in-line outlook = consistent (both suggest limited near-term upgrade catalyst). No material divergence beyond FX translation complexity.

PHASE 3 — HISTORICAL BENCHMARKING

2. Seasonal H1 % of FY Baseline, Tracking Deviation and Signal

  • EPS tracking: H1 actual 2.9p ÷ FY1 consensus 5.8p = 50.0% vs baseline 46.8% → deviation = 🟢 [+3.2pp] → 🟢 STRONG BUY (pre-RNS signal)
  • H2 EPS burden: 5.8p − 2.9p = 2.9p vs historical H2 avg ~2.1p — burden HIGHER than historical; actual H2 delivered ~1.9p (5.8p total − 2.9p H1 + tax adjustment complexity — see below). On adjusted EPS basis at 4.83c total, H2 = 4.83c − H1c. Without clean H1 EUR cents data, this cannot be precisely calculated.

  • Buy triggers: EPS buy trigger fired (H1 2.9p > 2.7p threshold). Revenue trigger: UNTRACKABLE (gross/net mismatch in Sharescope).

Note: The STRONG BUY signal at H1 level did not translate to a beat vs GBP consensus at FY level — the FX translation and the ongoing elevated tax rate are the reconciling factors.

3. Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical

  • H2 EPS: FY1 consensus 5.8p − H1 actual 2.9p = implied 2.9p required. Adjusted EPS 4.83c total ÷ 2 halves (rough split) suggests H2 ~2.4c = ~1.8p. H2 EPS appears below prior H2 of 2.1p — 🔴 weak H2 on GBP translated basis. The windfall tax (H2 Czech Republic applicable) weighted H2 down.

4. Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

  • EPS trend: 6.2p → 5.8p, net −0.4p (−6.5%). Steady downgrade throughout the year — despite good operational delivery, EPS cuts driven by higher tax rates and FX.
  • 4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING (flat 6 weeks)
  • Divergence: Price moved 115p → 102p over snapshot despite operational delivery — market skeptical on EPS quality. EPS downgrades and high tax burden have weighed.

5. Structural/One-Off Flags

[Windfall tax — ends 2025]: Czech windfall tax applicable 2023–2025 only. €5.3m one-off in 2025. This removes a ~0.75c/~0.6p headwind from FY26 EPS. FY26 adjusted EPS should benefit from this reversal.

[Eurowag Office migration — 2026 is critical execution year]: 35% migrated, majority target by end-2026. Platform risk: a failed migration would be highly damaging. Current NPS improvement (+3.8pts to 43.8) suggests early customer reception positive.

[Employee cost escalation — structural margin headwind]: Adjusted employee expenses +19.3% to €110.1m. This was the primary reason EBITDA margin fell 1.6pp despite 12.9% revenue growth. New Super LTIP approved Sep 2025 — ongoing SBC headwind. This is a structural cost item, not one-off.

PHASE 4 — BROKER-REACTION SIMULATION

#1 Driver — Adjusted EBITDA €132.1m (in-line), net revenue +12.9%, FY26 in-line guidance: The dominant note will focus on the in-line delivery. No major surprise in either direction on the top-line. The margin compression from employee costs (-1.6pp EBITDA margin) may generate cautious commentary. FY26 guidance of "in line with market expectations" provides no upgrade catalyst.

#2 Driver — Windfall tax reversal in FY26 — ~0.6p EPS tailwind: The €5.3m Czech windfall tax is non-recurring. FY26 adjusted EPS should see this headwind removed, providing a mechanical EPS uplift of ~0.6p in translated GBP terms. This is a known factor but may prompt minor upgrades to FY26 consensus.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY1 (FY26) EPS: UP slightly from 5.8p to 6.2–6.6p (+7–14%), driven by windfall tax reversal and low double-digit net revenue growth. Revenue: modest UP aligned with "low double-digit" guidance (~€362m, consistent with FY2 consensus).
  • FY2 (FY27) EPS: UP from 7.1p to 7.5–8.0p (+6–13%) as platform migration completes and monetisation scales.

Target price and recommendation: Consensus TP 127p. Post-results, likely held or minor upward revision to 130–140p. At 102p, upside to TP 24–37%. Some brokers may hold/wait for FY26 platform execution. Unlikely to cut recommendations.

Conservative guidance read-through: "In line with market expectations" is not conservative guidance — it is neutral. The €105–115m cash EBITDA range is the key quantified metric. At the top end ($115m), this would represent ~17% growth vs FY25 — toward the higher end of what consensus expects.

Key risk: Employee cost inflation is structural. The Super LTIP creates ongoing SBC headwinds. If employee costs grow at 15–20% again in FY26, EBITDA margin compression could continue and offset revenue growth, resulting in flat-to-down EPS despite in-line guidance. Platform migration execution is binary — a disruption would be severely negative.

Consistency check: Net FY1 EPS revision direction: modest upgrade (+7–14%). Tone must be Constructive or Neutral. → 🟢 Constructive / modest upgrades likely.

Para 1 — Headline numbers: The key challenge in this results set is the apparent EPS miss vs GBP pence consensus. Adjusted EPS of 4.83 euro cents translates to approximately 3.8–4.2p in GBP (depending on the EUR/GBP rate used), against Sharescope consensus of 5.8p — a significant apparent miss. The reconciling factor is that the consensus 5.8p likely embedded a more favourable EUR/GBP assumption and/or different tax rate assumptions. The RNS net revenue beat of €330.1m vs €327.5m consensus (+0.8%) is clean and positive, and Adjusted EBITDA of €132.1m (+8.5%) is in line. The #1 broker note catalyst is the windfall tax: €5.3m non-recurring charge (Czech Republic, final year of a 2023–2025 temporary tax) that depresses both statutory EPS and the adjusted effective tax rate in FY25 — but crucially, this headwind disappears entirely in FY26.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: The H1 EPS tracking signal of +3.2pp (Strong Buy) was contradicted by the FY outcome on a pence basis — primarily due to FX translation and the windfall tax hitting H2. The structural story is intact: net leverage of 1.9x is now within the 1.5–2.5x target, Toll revenues grew +52.3%, and 35% of customers are actively using Eurowag Office with majority migration targeted by end-2026. The bear case for major downgrades is limited by the windfall tax reversal (mechanical FY26 EPS uplift of ~0.6p) and the low-double-digit net revenue growth guidance. The structural risk is employee cost escalation — adjusted employee expenses grew +19.3% to €110.1m, contributing to the 1.6pp EBITDA margin compression. If this pace continues in FY26, the margin compression story extends despite revenue growth.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: FY26 EPS upgrades to 6.2–6.6p (+7–14%) from 5.8p are likely, driven primarily by the windfall tax reversal and in-line revenue growth. Revenue in line with low-double-digit guidance (~€362m). TP from 127p to 130–140p, implying 27–37% upside from 102p. The Capital Markets Day (AGM in May 2026) will be the next catalyst — new monetisation data from the Eurowag Office platform will be the key variable. 🏁 Constructive: in-line operational delivery, balance sheet fixed, windfall tax reversal provides FY26 EPS uplift; employee cost inflation and FX translation create EPS quality concerns that will limit upgrade enthusiasm. Score 52/100.

[Property portfolio £75m — key balance sheet support]: Three properties under offer. If property sales complete in H1 2026 as guided, net debt reduces materially from £31.4m. This is the primary near-term balance sheet stabiliser.

[Continental Europe sale — reduces ongoing losses]: Continental Europe contributed −£3.7m underlying loss in 2025 (discontinued). H1 2026 sale expected. Removes a loss contributor.

PHASE 4 — BROKER-REACTION SIMULATION

#1 Driver — FY25 underlying loss per share −44.1p vs consensus −36.8p (worse by 7.3p): Brokers must downgrade FY26 estimates further from −36.8p. Revenue miss of £33.1m adds pressure. The combined actual loss + revenue miss is the primary driver of further cuts.

#2 Driver — Material revenue reduction guided for FY26 + going concern note: The explicit guidance that revenue will "materially reduce" in 2026 as the core customer strategy is executed means revenue consensus of £531.8m is almost certainly too high. Brokers will model FY26 revenue at £400–470m range. Going concern note prevents Buy recommendation reinstatement.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY1 (FY26) EPS: WORSE — from −36.8p to approximately −45 to −55p range, reflecting lower revenue base and ongoing transformation costs.
  • FY2 (FY27) EPS: UNCHANGED or slight improvement — path to profitability in FY27 maintained but EPS recovery likely −10 to −5p range (marginally less negative).

Target price and recommendation: Consensus TP 315p appears completely detached from reality — this may be a stale estimate predating the full deterioration. Post-results, TP likely cut dramatically to 80–120p range or kept as a speculative recovery target. At 43.7p, the stock is effectively pricing in recovery or break-up value of the property portfolio. Brokers will maintain Sell/Hold ratings.

Key risk: The going concern note is the most significant risk. If property sales are delayed and working capital release slower than planned, the ABL facility covenants could be tested. This is not a theoretical risk — it is disclosed by management as a material uncertainty.

Consistency check: Net FY1 EPS revision direction: worse/cut. Tone must be Cautious or Negative. → 🔴🔴 Negative / material downgrades expected.

Overall tone: 🔴🔴 Negative / material downgrades expected

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

Para 1 — Headline numbers: Headlam's FY25 results confirm a business in deep trouble. The underlying loss of −44.1p per share is 7.3p (19.8%) worse than consensus of −36.8p, and revenue of £498.7m missed consensus by £33.1m (−6.2%). The statutory loss per share is −102.0p, incorporating £30.1m of non-underlying charges (impairments, ERP write-off, restructuring). The #1 broker note catalyst is the combined EPS/revenue double-miss, which forces further downward revisions to already-negative FY26 consensus estimates. The going concern material uncertainty — disclosed by management and referenced in the auditor's report — is the single most damaging element for institutional ownership.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: There is no upgrade resilience in this RNS. The transformation plan, while showing early green shoots (service delivery improving, stock levels down, SKU rationalisation complete), is in early innings and will not prevent further losses in FY26. Management explicitly guides for "material planned reduction in revenue over 2026 and 2027" as the core customer strategy executes. The property portfolio (£75m, three disposals imminent) is the primary near-term stabiliser — if property sales complete in H1 2026, net debt falls from £31.4m and the ABL covenant headroom improves. Without property sales proceeding as planned, the going concern risk crystallises. The path to profitability in FY2027 is the medium-term anchor — achievable if the transformation plan delivers, but execution risk is high.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: FY26 EPS will be revised from −36.8p to approximately −45 to −55p range; revenue from £531.8m to £400–470m as the planned low-margin revenue exit reduces the top-line materially. The consensus TP of 315p is almost certainly a stale pre-deterioration figure — brokers will cut dramatically to 80–120p if they maintain coverage at all. At 43.7p the stock is essentially a recovery option on the property portfolio plus the FY2027 profitability claim. 🏁 Severely negative: double miss on EPS and revenue, material FY26 revenue reduction guided, going concern material uncertainty disclosed — immediate and material broker downgrades on all metrics; recovery is a 2027 story at best with significant execution and balance sheet risk in the intervening period. Score 11/100.

LUCE — Luceco PLC

Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY results accordingly. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

PHASE 0B — FX Revenue Check

Revenue by geography: UK £214.6m (79.1% of £271.4m), Europe £24.1m (8.9%), Americas £20.1m (7.4%), Middle East & Africa £9.4m (3.5%), Asia Pacific £3.2m (1.2%). No single non-GBP currency exceeds 30% of revenues. Revenue bridge shows currency impact of −£3.2m (−1.3%) — modest. Phase 0B not triggered. No penalty.

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

  • Routing: pre-FY mode (latest qtrly report = Q2). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY Results. Sharescope data reflects pre-RNS state.
  • FY1 consensus: EPS 14.2p · Revenue £271.2m
  • FY2 consensus: EPS 15.1p · Revenue £283.6m
  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS net change over full snapshot: 12.6p → 14.2p = +1.6p (+12.7%). Steady upgrade: 12.6p (May) → 13.1p (May–Jul) → 12.9p (Aug cut) → 13.3p (Nov) → 14.1p (Jan 2026) → 14.2p (Feb). Notable: cut in August (12.9p) followed by recovery and further upgrades. 4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING (flat at 14.2p / £271.2m for 6 weeks). Revenue: £263.2m → £271.2m (+3.0%).
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 48.4% of FY = £131.3m · EPS 47.2% of FY = 6.7p
  • Prior-year H1 actuals (1y ago): Revenue £109.6m · EPS 5.7p
  • Implied H2 YoY (pre-FY mode): FY1 consensus £271.2m − H1 actual £125.7m = implied H2 £145.5m vs prior H2 £132.9m → +9.5% YoY. Implied H2 EPS: 14.2p − 5.9p = 8.3p vs prior H2 6.8p → +22.1% YoY — strong H2 leverage expectation in consensus already.
  • FX: N/A — Phase 0B not triggered.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

RNS type: FY Results (Audited results for year ended 31 December 2025)

1. Revenue — FY actual vs consensus

FY 2025 revenue: £271.4m, up 11.9% vs £242.5m in FY2024.

vs FY1 consensus of £271.2m: beat of £0.2m (+0.1%) — essentially exactly in line. Like-for-like revenue (ex-currency, ex-acquisitions): +4.6%. Acquisition contribution: +8.7% (D-Line and CMD full year).

"Revenue of £271.4m was £28.9m (11.9%) higher than 2024 with particularly strong revenue in the second half of the year."

2. EPS / Earnings — FY actual vs consensus

Adjusted basic EPS: 15.0p, up 20.0% vs 12.5p in FY2024.

vs FY1 consensus of 14.2p: beat of +0.8p (+5.6%).

Statutory basic EPS: 13.5p (2024: 9.5p).

EPS quality check: Effective tax rate on adjusted PBT: 18.7% (2024: 22.9%). Normal UK corporation tax rate: 25.0%. The 18.7% rate is materially below the standard rate. Reason stated: "recognition of a deferred tax asset in relation to US losses from prior years." This is a non-recurring tax benefit.

Restated EPS at normalised 22.9% rate: Adjusted PBT £27.8m × (1 − 22.9%) = £21.45m adjusted PAT. Shares ~150.5m basic. Restated adjusted EPS = ~£21.45m/150.5m = ~14.25p vs headline 15.0p. 🚨 Tax benefit inflates headline EPS by ~0.75p vs normalised rate. On a normalised basis, EPS beats consensus of 14.2p by only ~0.05p — essentially no beat on a like-for-like tax basis. This significantly changes the quality of the earnings beat. The adjusted EPS of 15.0p must be used with caution for forward guidance purposes.

3. Operating profit / margin

Adjusted Operating Profit: £33.8m, up 16.6% vs £29.0m in FY2024. Adjusted operating margin: 12.5% (2024: 12.0%) — +50bps expansion. Three-year CAGR above 15%.

"Adjusted Operating Profit of £33.8m, up 16.6% year on year (2024: £29.0m). Adjusted Operating Profit margin continuing to grow each year, up 50 basis points to 12.5%."

4. EV charging — Energy Transition

EV charging sales: £18.1m (+84.7%). Total Energy Transition revenue contribution growing strongly. Demand Flexibility revenue nascent but becoming meaningful in 2026 — incremental upside.

"Products sold relating to the Energy Transition have been key to the underlying growth with £18.1m of sales from EV chargers, which is an increase of 84.7%."

5. Free cash flow / balance sheet

Adjusted FCF: £30.4m (2024: £3.5m) — exceptional improvement driven by working capital reversal (£5.3m inflow vs £17.2m outflow in 2024). Bank Net Debt: £52.3m (2024: £68.6m), ND/EBITDA 1.2x (2024: 1.6x) — within 1.0–2.0x target.

"Adjusted Free Cash Flow of £30.4m which benefited from working capital inflows, reversing the working capital outflow from 2024."

6. Dividend

Proposed full year dividend: 6.0p (2024: 5.0p), +20%. Earnings cover: 2.5x. Dividend policy consistent.

7. FY2026 outlook — explicit guidance upgrade

"The Board now expects Adjusted Operating Profit for 2026 to exceed £37m" — vs consensus range of £34.7m–£36.5m (+1.4% to +6.6% beat at minimum). With the potential for further significant outperformance dependent on Demand Flexibility.

First two months of 2026: "like-for-like double-digit revenue growth."

"The Board now expects Adjusted Operating Profit for 2026 to exceed £37m, with the potential for further significant outperformance dependent on Demand Flexibility."

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

  • Guidance phrase: "Adjusted Operating Profit for 2026 to exceed £37m" — explicit numeric guidance above consensus. Covers one year (FY2026). Demand Flexibility provides additional upside not in current guidance. LFL double-digit revenue growth in Q1 2026.
  • Classification: 🟢🟢 Upgrade-triggering — explicit above-consensus numeric guidance for FY26. Provisional points: +14.
  • Divergence check: FY25 EPS beat of +5.6% (headline) / +0.05p normalised, plus 🟢🟢 upgrade-triggering FY26 guidance. However: the EPS beat quality is impaired by the tax deferred asset benefit (🚨 above). The FY26 guidance does NOT factor Demand Flexibility — so the upgraded guidance is on a conservative base. Direction consistent. Flag 🟡 Beat quality — FY25 adjusted EPS beat partly driven by below-normalised tax rate (DTA recognition); normalised EPS ~14.25p, not 15.0p. Carry as row in Phase 5.
