EPS trajectory (HoH YoY): H2: +9.7%, +33.8% — strong H2 acceleration. H1: +16.3%, +3.5% — H1 EPS growth modest in FY25 (partly due to restructuring charges in H1 per the RNS: £0.4m). 🟢 Accelerating on H2 basis; full year 🟢 Accelerating.

2. Seasonal H1 % of FY Baseline, Tracking Deviation and Signal (pre-FY mode)

  • Revenue baseline: 48.4% × £271.2m = £131.3m
  • EPS baseline: 47.2% × 14.2p = 6.7p
  • Revenue tracking: H1 actual £125.7m ÷ FY1 consensus £271.2m = 46.4% vs baseline 48.4% → deviation = 🔴 [−2.0pp] → 🔴 CAUTION
  • EPS tracking: H1 actual 5.9p ÷ FY1 consensus 14.2p = 41.5% vs baseline 47.2% → deviation = 🔴 [−5.7pp] → 🔴 SELL SIGNAL — H1 EPS materially behind seasonal norm; all resolved by H2 actual 9.1p (well above H2 norm of ~7.5p)
  • H2 EPS burden: FY consensus 14.2p − H1 actual 5.9p = 8.3p vs historical H2 avg ~6.5p — burden HIGHER than consensus assumed, yet delivered 9.1p. Excellent H2 execution.
  • Buy triggers: H1 Rev > [£131.3m × 1.015] = £133.3m → 🔴 ✗ (£125.7m < £133.3m) · H1 EPS > [6.7p × 1.015] = 6.8p → 🔴 ✗ (5.9p < 6.8p)
  • Historical hit rate: Both buy triggers missed at H1 stage. Yet FY delivered a beat — driven entirely by H2 outperformance. This is a company where H1 tracking signals were negative but H2 execution drove the outcome.

3. Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical

  • H2 Revenue actual: £145.7m vs prior H2 £132.9m → +9.6% YoY → 🟢 moderate/strong (approaching >+10%)
  • H2 EPS actual: 9.1p vs prior H2 6.8p → +33.8% YoY → 🟢 strong

4. Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

  • EPS trend: 12.6p → 14.2p, net +1.6p (+12.7%). One hiccup (Aug cut to 12.9p) followed by recovery and sustained upgrades through Jan/Feb 2026.
  • 4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING (flat at 14.2p for 6 weeks)
  • Divergence: Price flat at 163–204p range in last 6 months despite EPS upgrades — suggests the market was cautious on EV/Energy Transition delivery. Post-results, the explicit £37m+ FY26 guidance should re-rate the stock.

5. Structural/One-Off Flags

[Demand Flexibility — nascent but potentially transformative]: The EV charger installed base (10,000+ chargers enrolled in Demand Flexibility programme) creates a new recurring revenue stream with significant upside. Management says "significant potential upside to profit as more are enrolled" — not in current guidance. This is a genuine structural optionality item.

[FCF recovery — working capital normalisation]: £30.4m FCF (vs £3.5m in FY24) is partly a working capital reversal (Red Sea inventory build unwinding). Average 5-year FCF £20.3m — the 2025 figure is above-average and partly non-recurring. Sustainable FCF closer to £18–22m range.

[Deferred tax asset — one-off EPS boost]: As flagged in EPS quality check above — ~0.75p of the EPS beat is a non-recurring tax benefit. Forward guidance (£37m+ operating profit) is not subject to this distortion as it is an operating metric.

PHASE 4 — BROKER-REACTION SIMULATION

#1 Driver — Explicit FY26 AOP guidance of "exceeds £37m" vs consensus £34.7–£36.5m: This is the primary re-rating catalyst. An explicit "exceeds" guidance above the entire consensus range triggers mandatory estimate upgrades. With H1 2026 already delivering "like-for-like double-digit revenue growth" and the Demand Flexibility upside not included in guidance, the tone is as bullish as Luceco has communicated in years.

#2 Driver — H2 FY25 EPS acceleration (+33.8% H2 YoY, 9.1p) — execution quality confirmed: Despite H1 tracking signals being weak (sell signal on EPS), the H2 delivery was exceptional. This demonstrates the back-half-weighted earnings structure and validates brokers who held Buy ratings through the soft H1.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY1 (FY26) EPS: UP — from 14.2p to 15.5–16.5p (+9–16%), reflecting £37m+ AOP at ~18–20% tax rate normalised. Revenue: UP to £285–295m from £271.2m consensus.
  • FY2 (FY27) EPS: UP — from 15.1p to 17.0–18.5p (+13–23%), with Demand Flexibility now in scope for broker models.

Target price and recommendation: Consensus TP 204p likely revised to 220–250p range. At 163.4p, upside to revised TP: 35–53%. Brokers will reinforce Buy/reiterate Buy. No recommendation downgrades expected.

Conservative guidance read-through: "Exceeds £37m" with "potential for further significant outperformance" is classic two-tier conservative guidance. The floor is upgradeable. Demand Flexibility is explicitly called out as upside — this will feature prominently in broker notes.

Key risk: The deferred tax asset benefit in FY25 EPS creates noise. Brokers must normalise to ~14.25p FY25 EPS (not 15.0p) as the base — otherwise FY26 EPS comparatives will look disappointing when the DTA benefit unwinds. Americas/MEA revenue declining (Americas −10.7%, MEA −8.7%) — international headwinds persist.

Consistency check: Net FY1 EPS revision direction: upgrade (+9–16%). Tone must be Constructive or Strongly positive. → 🟢🟢 Strongly positive / upgrade cycle starting.

Overall tone: 🟢🟢 Strongly positive / upgrade cycle starting

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

76/100 · Confidence: 70–82 · No FX adjustment · 🟢🟢 Strongly positive / upgrade cycle starting

ComponentPts
🟢 Explicit FY26 AOP guidance "exceeds £37m" — above entire consensus range (£34.7–36.5m)+16
🟢 H2 FY25 EPS +33.8% YoY — exceptional H2 execution+10
🟢 EV charging +84.7%, Demand Flexibility nascent upside not in guidance+8
🟢 FCF £30.4m — strong cash generation, ND/EBITDA 1.2x+7
🟢 LFL double-digit revenue growth in Q1 2026 confirmed+7
🟢 EPS upgrade cycle +12.7% over year — sustained direction+5
🟡 Beat quality — FY25 adj EPS headline 15.0p; normalised ~14.25p after DTA benefit−5
🟡 H1 EPS tracking: −5.7pp sell signal (resolved by H2, but H1 was genuinely weak)−3
🔴 Americas −10.7%, MEA −8.7% — international revenue declining−4
🔴 FCF partly non-recurring (working capital reversal, one-year benefit)−3
🔴 EPS revenue beat essentially zero at normalised tax (£271.4m vs £271.2m)−3
🔴 Demand Flexibility regulatory uncertainty — "evolving framework, uncertain end-user response"−3
🔴 D-Line/CMD integration margin drag — Wiring Accessories margin 14.8% vs 17.5% prior−2

Para 1 — Headline numbers: The definitive catalyst is the explicit FY26 guidance: "Adjusted Operating Profit for 2026 to exceed £37m" — the entire analyst consensus range was £34.7–£36.5m, making this a minimum 1.4–6.6% beat before a single FY26 number is reported. Combined with "like-for-like double-digit revenue growth" in the first two months of 2026, this is the clearest upgrade-triggering language Luceco has used in several years. FY25 Adjusted Operating Profit of £33.8m (+16.6%, margin 12.5%) and adjusted EPS of 15.0p (+20%) met the headline beat vs 14.2p consensus — though on a normalised tax basis, the clean EPS is ~14.25p (🚨 deferred tax asset recognition boosted reported EPS by ~0.75p).

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: The H1 EPS tracking signal was a sell (−5.7pp), yet the FY beat was delivered entirely via H2 outperformance — H2 EPS was 9.1p (+33.8% YoY), comfortably exceeding the elevated H2 burden of 8.3p required vs consensus. This is a company structurally weighted to H2 (Energy Transition sales skew to autumn/winter via EV charging demand and contractor seasonality), and H2 execution confirmed the structural thesis. The bear case for downgrades is limited: Demand Flexibility is not yet in guidance but provides genuine upside optionality with 10,000+ chargers already enrolled generating nascent revenue — management targets this becoming "a more predictable, recurring and considerable long-term revenue stream" within 12–24 months.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: FY26 EPS upgrades from 14.2p to 15.5–16.5p (+9–16%) are likely, with revenue moving to £285–295m and operating profit to £37m+ (potentially £38–40m with Demand Flexibility). FY27 EPS moves from 15.1p to 17.0–18.5p (+13–23%) — the widest upgrade range for any single company today. Target price from 204p to 220–250p, implying 35–53% upside from 163.4p. The main watch point: normalise FY25 EPS to ~14.25p before comparing FY26 estimates to avoid making the FY26 growth rate look overstated. 🏁 Strongly positive: explicit above-consensus FY26 guidance, H2 execution vindicated, Demand Flexibility as material upside catalyst — upgrade cycle starting; normalise for DTA before modelling EPS growth rate. Score 76/100.

Para 1 — Headline numbers: The single definitive catalyst is the PBT beat of £1,158m vs consensus ~£1,070m (+8.2%), the largest single-year PBT overshoot NXT has delivered in recent years in absolute terms. EPS of 744.2p (+17.0% YoY vs 636.3p, +1.2% vs 735.2p consensus) appears modest on the consensus beat but the PBT figure is the broker anchor. Total Group sales of £7,004m (+10.8%) and full price sales +10.9% both comfortably exceeded the £6,802.8m revenue consensus by +3.0%. Stripping the 53rd week (£111m revenue, £24m PBT), comparable revenue was ~£6,790m and comparable PBT ~£1,134m — still +6.0% ahead of implied consensus on a like-for-like basis. International full price sales grew +35% CCY and WOBL expanded +49%, both platform-level structural outperformance metrics that brokers weight highly in their NXT models.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: H2 FY25 (ended 31 January 2026) delivered revenue ~£3,634m (+11.3% YoY) and EPS ~416p (+22.4% YoY) — both classified 🟢 strong (>+10% YoY). The Christmas period and January sale traded with particular strength, consistent with NXT's H2-weighting pattern. The FY26 guidance of £1,210m PBT (+4.5%) is ahead of FY2 consensus (~£1,195m) — the base is higher than expected and the growth rate beats consensus. The structural upgrade resilience comes from NXT's proven pattern of conservative guidance: FY25 was initially guided at +6.0% full price sales growth; actual was +10.9%. Brokers applying a standard NXT conservatism premium of 2-3pp arrive at an effective FY26 underlying assumption of +6.5-7.5% sales, embedding a high probability of mid-year upgrades. FY27 (FY2) EPS upgrades of +2-4% toward 820-835p are expected as the WOBL/International platform trajectory and conservative FY26 guidance embed further upside optionality. Target prices are expected to move from the ~£95-100 range toward £100-108, with the most bullish brokers reaching £110-112 on 14× forward EPS applied to 800p FY26 estimates. The principal constraint on a higher score is the consensus EPS deceleration from +16.9% (FY25) to +5.1% (FY26e) — structurally inevitable at NXT's scale — and the warehouse capex commitment (E3 £307m + E4 land) which pressures FCF modelling over FY26-28. 🏁 NXT has delivered a broad-based, clean, high-quality beat with upgrade-triggering forward guidance and a £500m capital return programme, earning a score of 87 — a clear and high-confidence upgrade cycle.

Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as pre-FY update accordingly. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

PHASE 0B — FX Revenue Check

The PINE RNS (Business Update, 25 March 2026) contains no Currency Movements section. Revenue base: FY1 consensus £44.7m. Operations are UK-headquartered with Netherlands reseller acquisition (£3.3m). North America rollout is in pre-revenue testing phase. No single non-GBP currency exceeds 30% of disclosed revenues — the Netherlands acquisition adds ~£0.75m EBITDA and is GBP-reported. Phase 0B not triggered. No penalty.

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

  • Routing: pre-FY mode (latest qtrly report = Q2). Interpreting incoming RNS as pre-FY update or trading update. Sharescope data reflects pre-RNS state.

Sustained step-down: first cut Sept 2025 (8.9p → 6.5p), second cut Nov 2025 (6.5p → 6.1p → 5.9p). 4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING (flat at 5.9p since Nov 2025). Revenue net change: £45.2m → £44.7m = −£0.5m (−1.1%). Direction of EPS revisions is firmly negative over the year.

FY1 consensus £44.7m minus H1 £19.6m = implied H2 £25.1m vs prior-year H2 £15.1m → +66.3% YoY — heavily H2-weighted, driven by Lookers rollout acceleration in H2. Implied H2 EPS: 5.9p − 0.6p = 5.3p vs prior-year H2 −3.3p — prior year H2 was loss-making, so H2 is the inflection point year.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

RNS type: Pre-FY Trading Update (Business Update, 25 March 2026, contains inside information)

1. Revenue / Guidance — FY26 EBITDA warning

FY26 underlying EBITDA will be lower than current market expectations due to Marshalls implementation delay from Q1 2026 to H2 2026. No numeric EBITDA or revenue figure provided. Implied downward revision to FY26 estimates — magnitude unquantified in the RNS.

"As a result of the change in timing of the Marshalls implementation, FY26 underlying EBITDA will be lower than current market expectations."

2. Marshalls — delay confirmed, not cancelled

Previously guided Q1 2026 commencement. Now commencement expected H2 2026. Planning process described as "approaching completion." Since October 2024 Marshalls has added Geely Auto, Omoda, Jaecoo, BYD and Genesis dealers — network has grown, not contracted.

"This planning process is approaching completion, and the rollout of the Pinewood.AI system is now expected to commence in the second half of 2026."

3. Lookers — on track

Lookers rollout commenced 21 July 2025, progressing to schedule. Simultaneous 13-store Mercedes-Benz go-live in February 2026. Remaining Lookers dealers scheduled to complete on time in Q4 2026.

"In February, we executed a simultaneous 13 store go-live across Lookers' Mercedes-Benz dealers. The rollout into the remaining Lookers dealers is scheduled to complete on time, in quarter four 2026."

4. North America — pre-revenue testing stage

System live in various stages, testing major functions with Lithia. Rollout expected to commence H2 2026.

"We are looking forward to commencing the system rollout in North America in the second half of 2026."

5. Netherlands reseller acquisition

Acquired for £3.3m cash. Expected to add £0.7–0.8m incremental annual EBITDA. Supports Central European growth.

"The acquisition is aligned with Pinewood.AI's strategy to fully control its international sales and customer service functions, and it will support the Group's growth ambitions in the Central European market."

6. FY28 EBITDA guidance reaffirmed

Board reaffirms £58–62m underlying EBITDA by FY28, underpinned by existing signed contracts and strong pipeline.

"The Board of Pinewood.AI also reaffirms its expectation that the Group will achieve underlying EBITDA of £58-62m by FY28."

7. FY25 results date

FY25 results to be released 22 April 2026. No FY25 guidance or figures disclosed in this RNS.

EPS quality check: No EPS figure disclosed. The RNS is a trading update only — no income statement. No tax rate deviation to check.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

  • Guidance phrase: "FY26 underlying EBITDA will be lower than current market expectations" — explicit below-consensus language for the current year. Numeric range: none. Forward coverage: one year (FY26). FY28 £58–62m reaffirmed (two years out).
  • The RNS is an explicit profit warning for FY26 combined with a reaffirmation of the medium-term (FY28) target. Current year delivery: Lookers on track, North America testing. Marshalls the sole source of miss.
  • Classification: 🔴🔴 Profit warning — explicit below-expectations EBITDA guidance for FY26. Provisional points: −12 to −15.
  • Divergence check: No current-year H1 results in this RNS (FY25 results due 22 April). FY26 guidance is the primary content. Lookers progress provides a partial offset to the Marshalls delay but does not neutralise the profit warning. No divergence — delivery and guidance are directionally consistent (both reflect a delay story). No separate divergence row required.

QTX — Quartix Holdings PLC

Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY results accordingly. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

PHASE 0B — FX Revenue Check

Revenue disaggregation from RNS: UK/EI £19.9m (55.7% of £35.7m), France £9.2m (25.8%), Other Europe £3.3m (9.3%), USA £3.3m (9.2%). No single non-GBP currency exceeds 30% of revenues (France EUR: 25.8%). Phase 0B not triggered. No penalty.

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

  • Routing: pre-FY mode (latest qtrly report = Q2). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY Results. Sharescope data reflects pre-RNS state.
  • FY1 consensus: EPS 11.6p · Revenue £36.4m
  • FY2 consensus: EPS 14.6p · Revenue £41.0m
  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS net change over full snapshot: 10.5p → 11.6p = +1.1p (+10.5%). Steady upgrade path: 10.5p (May) → 10.7p (Jul) → 10.9p (Oct) → 11.3p (Nov) → 11.6p (Jan 2026), then flat. 4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING (flat at 11.6p / £36.4m for 10 weeks). Revenue net change: £36.0m → £36.4m = +£0.4m (+1.1%). Direction positive throughout year.
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 49.0% of FY = £17.8m · EPS 31.0% of FY = 3.6p
  • Prior-year H1 actuals (1y ago): Revenue £16.1m · EPS 4.4p
  • Implied H2 YoY (pre-FY mode): FY1 consensus £36.4m − H1 actual £17.6m = implied H2 £18.8m vs prior-year H2 £16.3m → +15.3% YoY. Implied H2 EPS: 11.6p − 5.5p = 6.1p vs prior-year H2 9.8p → −37.8% YoY — note: H1 EPS (5.5p) already materially exceeds prior H1 (4.4p) and prior H2 (9.8p). The negative implied H2 YoY is an artefact of H1 being front-loaded this year vs prior year.
  • FX: N/A — Phase 0B not triggered.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

RNS type: FY Results (Audited results for year ended 31 December 2025)

1. Revenue — FY actual vs consensus

FY 2025 revenue: £35.7m, up 12% vs £31.8m in FY2024. Restated 2024 figure (IAS 16 policy change).

vs FY1 consensus of £36.4m: miss of £0.7m (−1.9%) — small miss, within rounding. On constant currency basis: also +12%.

"Group revenue for the year increased by 12% to £35.7m (2024: £31.8m). Revenue growth on a constant currency basis, using applicable exchanges rate at 31 December 2025, was also 12%."

2. EPS / Earnings — FY actual vs consensus

Diluted EPS: 13.17p, up 25% vs 10.51p in FY2024 (restated). Basic EPS: 13.18p, up 25% vs 10.58p in FY2024 (restated).

vs FY1 consensus of 11.6p: beat of +1.57p (+13.5%). Significant earnings beat.

EPS quality check: Effective tax rate 2025: 26.4%. Underlying effective tax rate (excluding prior year adjustments): 22.9%. Stated normalised rate context: 2024 restated rate was 20.7%; 2025 rate is 26.4%. Difference from 22.9% underlying: +3.5pp above normalised rate — just above the 3pp threshold. The higher 2025 rate reflects policy change impacts. Restated EPS at 22.9% effective rate: PBT £8.67m × (1 − 22.9%) = £6.69m profit. Shares 48.43m → restated EPS = ~13.82p. The headline 13.17p EPS is actually slightly conservative vs a normalised tax rate — no 🚨 required; if anything, EPS quality is clean/conservative.

3. ARR / Forward Indicator

ARR increased by £4.5m (+14%) to £37.0m — a record growth in this measure, 25% above FY2024 ARR growth of £3.6m. ARR exceeds annual revenue (£35.7m) — highly positive forward indicator.

"The Group's ARR increased by £4.5m (+14%) during the Period, representing an increase of 25% over the growth achieved in 2024 (£3.6m on constant currency)."

4. EBITDA / Profitability

EBITDA: £13.2m, up 23% (2024: £10.7m restated). EBITDA margin: 36.9% (2024: 33.6%). Adjusted EBIT: £8.8m, up 38%. Gross margin: 73.2% (2024: 71.6%).

"In 2025, under the revised accounting policy, EBITDA increased by 23% on a comparable basis to £13.2m (2024: £10.7m). Adjusted EBIT for the year increased by 38% to £8.8m (2024: £6.4m)."

5. Free Cash Flow / Balance Sheet

Free cash flow: £5.2m (2024: £2.6m), up 101%. Net cash: £5.6m (2024: £3.1m). Significant FCF improvement despite 4G France upgrade costs (~£1.0m), restructuring (~£0.4m) and pre-payment of £0.7m corporation tax. Clean balance sheet — no debt.

"Free cash flow (cash flow from operations after tax and investing activities), was £5.2m (2024: £2.6m), despite significant outflows in the year for the 4G upgrade programme in France (approximately £1.0m), restructuring costs in the first half (approx. £0.4m); and a pre-payment of £0.7m in corporation tax made in December."

6. Dividend

Total dividend: 10.0p (2024: 4.50p). Interim 2.5p paid September 2025. Final proposed: 7.5p (2024: 3.00p). Dividend yield ~4.4% on average price. Massive dividend increase signals confidence.

"This results in a total dividend of 10p per share for the financial year ended 31 December 2025, representing a yield of 3.6% based on the closing share price for 2025, or 4.4% based on the average share price for the year."

7. Accounting policy change (IAS 16)

FRC-prompted reclassification of tracking units as PPE (IAS 16) rather than contract cost assets (IFRS 15). Applied retrospectively. Prior year 2024 restated. Effect on P&L: modest (EPS +0.73p in 2024 post-restatement). The 2025 EPS of 13.17p is on the restated, cleaner accounting basis.

8. KPI highlights

New fleet subscriptions: +7% to 79,576. Subscription base: +11% to 333,922. NRR: 98.1% (2024: 95.7%). Italy ARR +43%, Spain +35% — continental acceleration.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

  • Guidance phrase: "The outlook for 2026 is very encouraging" — qualitative only. "Closing ARR was higher than Group revenue for the year, and this augurs well for the achievement of our financial goals for 2026." No numeric FY2026 guidance. One year forward. Confident qualitative language supported by record ARR growth.
  • No upgrade-triggering numeric language. But the combination of: (a) 13.5% EPS beat, (b) ARR > revenue (strong forward visibility), (c) record ARR growth, and (d) "very encouraging" outlook — this is upgrade-triggering in practice even if not numeric.

Classification: 🟢🟢 Upgrade-triggering — record ARR growth, 13.5% EPS beat, ARR exceeding revenue, and confident outlook. Provisional points: +13.

Divergence check: Current year beat (EPS +13.5%) + Constructive/positive outlook = aligned. No divergence.

The main watch point is FY26 execution: can the company sustain 12%+ revenue growth as the UK subscription base matures and Germany remains soft? 🏁 Strong upgrade cycle: clean 13.5% EPS beat, record ARR growth, FCF doubling, 122% dividend increase — brokers will raise materially across all metrics; valuation re-rating probable if execution sustains. VLX — Volex Group PLC

Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as pre-FY trading update accordingly. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

PHASE 0B — FX Revenue Check

Volex reports in USD. Revenue is global across 25 countries. The RNS does not include a Currency Movements section with explicit GBP breakdowns by currency. However, Volex reports in USD and has significant USD-denominated operations (North America, Asia manufacturing). The consensus revenue in the Sharescope data is in USD ($1,172.9m FY1). Revenue exposure: manufacturing primarily in Asia (RMB), selling globally (USD, EUR, GBP). Management typically guides on a USD basis. GBP-reporting is likely to introduce some FX noise but the core metric is USD operating profit margin.

From the RNS: "full year data centre revenues are now expected to be approximately double the $118 million achieved in the prior year" — USD revenue metric. No formal currency percentage breakdown vs prior average rate. However, given Volex's global footprint and USD reporting basis, and that consensus TP/EPS in Sharescope is in GBP pence (38.2p), there is a GBP/USD translation effect. No explicit Currency Movements table present. Given the complexity and no formal disclosure, cannot calculate a precise FX penalty. Phase 0B not triggered by the strict RNS disclosure requirement. No penalty applied. Note: GBP/USD translation will be a minor factor in broker modelling — not scored here.

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

  • Routing: pre-FY mode (latest qtrly report = Q2). Interpreting incoming RNS as pre-FY trading update (year ending 31 March 2026, so this is a trading update with ~1 month to go). Sharescope data reflects pre-RNS state.
  • FY1 consensus: EPS 38.2p · Revenue $1,172.9m (~£869m at 1.35 USD/GBP)
  • FY2 consensus: EPS 41.0p · Revenue $1,237.3m
  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS net change over full snapshot: 32.8p → 38.2p = +5.4p (+16.5%). Strong continuous upgrade cycle: 32.8p (May) → 35.1p (Jul, H1 results) → 37.3p (Nov–Dec) → 38.2p (Feb 2026). Revenue: $1,061m → $1,172.9m (+10.5%). 4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING (flat at 38.2p / $1,172.9m for 6 weeks pre-RNS). Direction: firmly positive year, multiple upgrade steps.
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 46.9% of FY = $549.9m · EPS 44.3% of FY = 16.9p
  • Prior-year H1 actuals (1y ago): Revenue $518.2m · EPS 15.1p
  • Implied H2 YoY (pre-FY mode): FY1 consensus $1,172.9m − H1 actual $583.9m = implied H2 $589.0m vs prior H2 $568.3m → +3.7% YoY. Implied H2 EPS: 38.2p − 19.6p = 18.6p vs prior H2 20.7p → −10.1% YoY — but this is now overtaken by the RNS upgrade.
  • FX: N/A — Phase 0B not triggered per disclosure criteria.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

RNS type: Pre-FY Trading Update (Year ending 31 March 2026, ~1 month to go)

1. Revenue — FY guidance vs consensus

FY2026 revenue: "at least $1,220 million" vs FY1 consensus $1,172.9m.

Beat vs consensus: $1,220m − $1,172.9m = +$47.1m (+4.0%) minimum. Upper bound not stated but range of analyst estimates was $1,149.3m–$1,192.2m — the "at least $1,220m" guide is above the entire analyst range.

"The Board now expects Group revenue for FY2026 to be at least $1,220 million."

2. Operating profit / margin

Underlying operating margin expected to be "slightly above the top end of the Group's 9–10% target range" — i.e. >10%. Prior consensus underlying operating profit: average $114.8m (range $111.5m–$117.0m). If revenue ≥$1,220m and margin >10%: implied operating profit ≥$122m vs consensus $114.8m = beat of +$7.2m (+6.3%) minimum.

"Underlying operating margins are expected to be slightly above the top end of the Group's 9-10% target range, reflecting both operating leverage from higher revenues and a continued focus on operational efficiency."

3. Data centre driver

Full-year data centre revenues expected to be approximately double $118m achieved in prior year = ~$236m in FY26. This is the primary driver of outperformance. Accelerated customer requirements fulfilled (near-term capacity needs), reflecting Volex's global scale advantage.

"Full year data centre revenues are now expected to be approximately double the $118 million achieved in the prior year."

4. Geopolitical/tariff caveat

Limited direct exposure to Middle East markets. Broader macroeconomic implications "difficult to predict." Board does not anticipate material near-term impact given diversified end markets. No quantification.

5. Capital markets event — 22 April 2026

New medium-term growth targets to be presented. AIM → Main Market listing being considered (FTSE250 eligibility anticipated). Largest shareholders being consulted.

"The Board believes that a move to the Main Market would facilitate access to deeper pools of capital and a broader range of investors, supporting increased liquidity in trading of the Group's shares."

6. FY27 caveat on data centre accelerated demand

Management explicitly flags that the accelerated customer demand dynamic "may not recur at the same level in FY2027" — important forward qualifier.

"The Board is encouraged by the strength of the Group's positioning in this market, although this particular dynamic may not recur at the same level in FY2027."

EPS quality check: No EPS disclosed in trading update. Operating profit metric is underlying (pre-amortisation, restructuring, SBC). No tax rate deviation check possible from this RNS alone. Note: Volex has a history of acquisition-related adjusting items; headline EPS will be adjusted figure.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

  • Guidance phrase: "full year results now expected to be significantly ahead of current market expectations" + revenue "at least $1,220 million" + margin "slightly above the top end of 9–10% target range." Covers current FY (FY26). Forward-looking FY27 caveat on data centre explicitly included.
  • Classification: 🟢🟢 Upgrade-triggering — explicit "significantly ahead" language, "at least" revenue figure above entire analyst range, new medium-term targets to follow. Provisional points: +14.
  • Divergence check: Current year beat + FY27 mild caution on data centre dynamic. This is a divergence: FY26 🟢🟢 vs FY27 mildly 🟡. Not a full reversal — FY27 caveat is about one specific dynamic (accelerated demand) not the underlying business. Flag: 🟡 Beat quality — FY27 data centre dynamic explicitly flagged as potentially non-recurring at same level. Carry as separate row in Phase 5.

PHASE 3 — HISTORICAL BENCHMARKING

Revenue trajectory (HoH YoY): +30.4%, +10.3%, +12.6%, +11.9%+ → 🟢 Steady — consistent double-digit growth.

EPS trajectory (HoH YoY): +6.3%, +10.1%, +29.8% (H1 FY27 surge) → 🟢 Accelerating on H1 basis.

2. Seasonal H1 % of FY Baseline, Tracking Deviation and Signal (pre-FY mode)

  • Revenue baseline: 46.9% × $1,172.9m = $549.9m
  • EPS baseline: 44.3% × 38.2p = 16.9p
  • Revenue tracking (pre-RNS): H1 actual $583.9m ÷ FY1 consensus $1,172.9m = 49.8% vs baseline 46.9% → deviation = 🟢 [+2.9pp] → 🟢 STRONG BUY
  • EPS tracking: H1 actual 19.6p ÷ FY1 consensus 38.2p = 51.3% vs baseline 44.3% → deviation = 🟢 [+7.0pp] → 🟢 STRONG BUY
  • H2 EPS burden: FY1 consensus 38.2p − H1 actual 19.6p = 18.6p required vs historical H2 avg 18.2p — burden essentially equal to consensus assumption. Post-RNS upgrade: burden increases to ~20.9p (≥40.5p FY − 19.6p H1), which is still achievable given the data centre strength.
  • Buy triggers: H1 Rev > [$549.9m × 1.015] = $558.1m → 🟢 ✓ ($583.9m > $558.1m) · H1 EPS > [16.9p × 1.015] = 17.2p → 🟢 ✓ (19.6p > 17.2p)
  • Historical hit rate: Both buy triggers fired. Revenue and EPS both in Strong Buy territory pre-results. RNS has confirmed and exceeded.

3. Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical

Pre-FY: compare implied H2 vs prior H2.

  • H2 Revenue: ≥$636.1m vs prior H2 $568.3m → ≥+11.9% YoY → 🟢 strong
  • H2 EPS: ~20.9p vs prior H2 20.7p → ~+1.0% YoY → 🟡 flat (driven by H1 capturing more EPS this cycle and data centre revenue H2-weighted)

4. Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

  • EPS trend: 32.8p → 38.2p, net +5.4p (+16.5%). Consistent upgrades throughout year with H1 results (Jul), Capital Markets update (Nov), and quarterly progress.
  • 4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING (flat 6 weeks before this RNS — pre-result consolidation)
  • Divergence: Price has run from 354p (May 2025) to 499p (peak Mar 2026) — +41% alongside +16.5% EPS upgrades. Pre-RNS price at 427.5p already pricing in a beat (price pulled back slightly from 499p peak — some caution). RNS now confirms and extends the upgrade.

5. Structural/One-Off Flags

[Data centre doubling — partly one-off accelerated demand]: Revenue doubling from $118m to ~$236m includes a component of "accelerated customer requirements" where Volex fulfilled near-term capacity needs other suppliers couldn't meet. This is explicitly flagged as potentially non-recurring at the same level in FY27. Structural growth in data centre is intact; the acceleration boost is a one-off component.

[AIM → Main Market migration]: Potential FTSE250 inclusion would significantly expand the institutional investor base. Capital Markets Event on 22 April will be a major catalyst — new medium-term targets expected.

"The Board believes that a move to the Main Market would facilitate access to deeper pools of capital and a broader range of investors."

PHASE 4 — BROKER-REACTION SIMULATION

#1 Driver — Revenue "at least $1,220m" + "significantly ahead" language — above entire analyst range: The dominant catalyst. With consensus range of $1,149–$1,192m, a floor of $1,220m is a 2–6% beat at the bottom and potentially 5–10%+ if the actual lands closer to $1,250–1,270m. Operating margin >10% adds further punch. This forces an immediate revenue and EPS upgrade cycle.

#2 Driver — Data centre revenues doubling (~$236m) — confirms structural positioning: Data centre was the growth thesis. A doubling in one year confirms Volex as a credible, scaled beneficiary of AI infrastructure capex. The FY27 caveat is important but does not undermine the structural case — it only flags that the accelerated-order dynamic (customer stockpiling/urgency) may moderate.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY1 (FY26) EPS: UP — from 38.2p to estimate 42–44p (+10–15%). Revenue: UP from $1,172.9m to $1,220m+ consensus floor; broker estimates likely $1,230–1,260m range.
  • FY2 (FY27) EPS: UP more cautiously — from 41.0p to 42–44p (+2–7%), reflecting new medium-term targets from Capital Markets Event (22 April) offset by data centre normalisation caveat.

Target price and recommendation: Consensus TP 496p likely revised upward to 540–600p range. At 427.5p, upside to revised TP: 26–40%. Brokers will reiterate/upgrade to Buy/Strong Buy. Potential for new initiations post-AIM migration.

Conservative guidance read-through: "At least $1,220m" is classic conservative floor language. "Significantly ahead" is strong. Taken together, actual result likely $1,230–1,260m. This increases upgrade cycle probability.

Key risk: The FY27 data centre caveat is real. If accelerated demand created channel inventory builds (customers stockpiling), FY27 data centre revenues could step back to $180–200m rather than sustaining $236m. This would cap the FY27 upgrade. Additionally, AIM → Main Market listing uncertainty and macro/tariff headwinds cited.

"The Board is encouraged by the strength of the Group's positioning in this market, although this particular dynamic may not recur at the same level in FY2027."

Consistency check: Net FY1 EPS revision direction: upgrade (+10–15%). Tone must be Constructive or Strongly positive. → 🟢🟢 Strongly positive / upgrade cycle starting.

Overall tone: 🟢🟢 Strongly positive / upgrade cycle starting

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

Para 1 — Headline numbers: The single definitive catalyst is the statement that "full year results are now expected to be significantly ahead of current market expectations" with revenue guided to "at least $1,220 million" — a floor that exceeds the entire analyst range of $1,149–1,192m. The #1 metric is data centre revenues, now expected to be approximately double the prior year's $118m (~$236m), driven by AI infrastructure demand and Volex's ability to fulfil accelerated customer capacity needs when competitors could not. Underlying operating margin is expected above the top of the 9–10% target range, implying underlying operating profit of ≥$122m vs consensus $114.8m (+6.3% at minimum).

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: Pre-RNS H1 tracking signalled strength: revenue +2.9pp above seasonal baseline (Strong Buy) and EPS +7.0pp above baseline (Strong Buy) — both buy triggers fired. The implied H2 revenue of ≥$636m is +12% vs prior H2 $568m, consistent with data centre-driven acceleration. The FY27 caveat — that accelerated demand "may not recur at the same level" — is the key constraint on the upgrade cycle. Brokers will need to assess how much of the $236m data centre revenue is structural vs pull-forward. The bear case for FY27 is a step-back to $180–200m in data centre rather than sustaining $236m; even in this scenario, Volex's other divisions (EV, Medical, Consumer, Industrial) are described as trading "broadly in line" with H1 — providing a resilient base.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: FY26 EPS upgrades from 38.2p to 42–44p (+10–15%) are highly probable. Revenue consensus will be revised to $1,230–1,260m. FY27 EPS upgrades are likely more modest (41p → 42–44p, +2–7%) pending new medium-term targets at the Capital Markets Event on 22 April 2026 — this event is the next major catalyst and may provide guidance that underpins a further upgrade cycle. TP from 496p to 540–600p range, implying 26–40% upside from 427.5p. AIM→Main Market migration is an additional non-earnings catalyst. 🏁 Strongly positive: revenue floor above entire analyst range, data centre doubling, margin above target — immediate upgrade cycle starting; FY27 normalisation caveat limits the second-year upgrade but the Capital Markets Event on 22 April is the next major catalyst. Score 87/100.

PHASE 0B — FX REVENUE CHECK

The RNS discloses constant-currency revenue of −30% vs reported −31%. The difference is 1pp, which is within the 0.5pp threshold... actually 1pp exceeds the 0.5pp constant-currency override threshold. Let me assess properly.

Constant currency revenue decline: −30% vs reported −31%. Difference = 1pp. This exceeds the 0.5pp override threshold, so the override does not fire.

Geographic revenue split: UK £88.4m (49.7%), North America £45.8m (25.8%), APAC £28.5m (16.0%), EMEA £15.0m (8.4%). North America USD/CAD exposure = ~25.8% of revenue. No single non-GBP currency exceeds 30%. Phase 0B: no penalty applies. Proceed to Phase 1.

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

  • Routing: pre-FY mode (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY results. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.
  • FY1 consensus: EPS 9.7p · Revenue £176.5m
  • FY2 consensus: EPS 9.2p · Revenue £162.6m
  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS net change over full snapshot period: 16.0p → 9.7p = −6.3p, −39.4%. Heavy downgrades concentrated in Jul–Aug 2025 (16.0p → 9.7p in one step). Last-4-week trend: 🔴 FALLING (price 289p → 273p; EPS flat at 9.7p but revenue oscillated 178→176.5m, slight downward drift). Revenue net change: £207.6m → £176.5m = −14.9%.
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 51.5% of FY = £90.9m · EPS 49.7% of FY = 4.8p
  • Prior-year H1 actuals: Revenue £140.2m · EPS 11.7p
  • Implied H2 YoY (pre-FY mode): FY actual £177.7m − H1 actual £97.3m = H2 £80.4m vs prior-year H2 £117.5m → Revenue H2 YoY: −31.6%. FY actual EPS 10.0p − H1 actual 6.3p = H2 4.7p (cross-check below in Phase 3) vs prior-year H2 11.3p → EPS H2 YoY: −58.4%. Note: FY1 consensus EPS was 9.7p; actual delivered 10.0p — RNS-derived figures used throughout.
  • FX: No single currency >30% exposure. Phase 0B not triggered. N/A.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

RNS type: FY Results (Preliminary Results for year ended 31 December 2025)

1. Revenue figures FY 2025 actual: £177.7m, down 31% YoY (2024: £257.7m). Constant currency basis: −30%. vs FY1 consensus £176.5m: beat of +£1.2m / +0.7% — effectively in line.

"Revenue decreased by 31% to £177.7 million (2024: £257.7 million) (30% lower on a constant-currency basis)."

2. EPS / earnings figures Adjusted basic EPS FY 2025: 10.0p (2024: 23.0p, −57%). vs FY1 consensus 9.7p: beat of +0.3p / +3.1%. Basic EPS: 5.2p (2024: 18.8p). Adjusted PBT: £13.7m (2024: £34.0m, −60%). Reported PBT: £7.6m.

EPS quality check: Effective tax rate 25.8% vs UK standard rate 25.0% — deviation of 0.8pp, well within the 3pp threshold. No tax distortion. Adjusted EPS excludes: share plan expense £0.2m, exceptional costs £2.6m, EMEA goodwill and asset impairment charge £3.3m. The impairment is non-recurring; the adjusted figure is the appropriate basis. No restatement required.

"Adjusted basic earnings per share was down 57%, to 10.0 pence (2024: 23.0 pence)."

3. Order book / forward work No order book or forward work coverage metric disclosed. Consultant headcount at year-end: 2,003 (2024: 2,578, −22%). Coaching completions: 828 (2024: 877). 45 new clients secured (2024: 52). North America: 218 consultants coached in H2 vs 114 in H1 — a notable inflection.

"An increase in client demand towards the end of the year was reflected in our coaching completions as we coached 218 Consultants in the second half of 2025 compared with 114 in the first half."

4. Margin, profitability, cost signals Adjusted operating margin: 7.6% (2024: 13.0%). Adjusted operating profit: £13.6m (2024: £33.4m, −59%). Exceptional costs reduced to £2.6m (2024: £4.9m, −47%). EMEA goodwill and asset impairment: £3.3m. Cash conversion: 292% (operating profit basis). No explicit forward margin guidance provided. Sales transformation programme launched — costs not quantified but described as ongoing investment.

"Adjusted Group operating margin decreased to 7.6% (2024: 13.0%)."

5. Capital returns and per-share items Total dividend 2025: 10.0p (2024: 22.5p, −56%). Final dividend recommended: 4.0p (subject to AGM approval 21 May 2026). Cash position: £35.3m (2024: £40.6m). No debt. Cash conversion 292% (adjusted: 200%). Distributable reserves: £23.3m.

"The Board recommends a final dividend of 4.0 pence per share, following an interim dividend of 6.0 pence per share, a total dividend for the year of 10.0 pence per share (2024: 22.5 pence per share)."

6. Qualitative tone — forward-looking statements Management flags: encouraging signs in some markets; geopolitical/Middle East uncertainty a risk; client appetite for AI-enabled skills increasing; sales transformation programme underway; Board "optimistic that areas of the Group less impacted will continue to experience the modest uptick in activity seen over recent months." No numeric FY2026 guidance provided.

"The Board remains focused on positioning FDM to return to sustainable growth across the Group as soon as market conditions permit, and we continue to align resources carefully by region, in line with current and anticipated demand, while applying rigorous cost management and taking a prudent approach to investment."

2B — Outlook & Guidance Classification

Forward-looking statements are entirely qualitative. No numeric guidance for FY2026. Language: "encouraging signs… in some markets", "modest uptick", "optimistic that areas of the Group less impacted will continue to experience" that uptick — explicitly carved out to regions away from Middle East disruption. "Return to sustainable growth as soon as market conditions permit" — conditional, not committed. "Prudent approach to investment."

This is qualitative-only guidance with no numeric uplift, following a year of severe earnings decline. The tone is cautious optimism at best, conditioned on macro recovery and explicitly hedged by geopolitical risk.

Classification: 🔴 Cautious — qualitative-only growth guidance with explicit macro caveats; no numeric commitment; conditional recovery language. Provisional points: −5 to −8.
